Being a Starweaver certainly has its advantages, but also plenty of rules. Once a deal is made, you must seal a covenant and follow the proper terms. For those used to traveling trade or running small stalls, such rules can feel a bit restrictive.
With EverSpring's name behind us, even the largest merchants treat us with respect — some even approach us first simply because we're Starweavers.
I used to be the same — traveling from place to place, doing small trades along the way. Saved up a little, then came here hoping to make something bigger of it.

options.content: How many Starweavers are there in Huaxu?

talks.content: It's a far cry from the days when I had to go door to door trying to gather stock.
How many? Hard to say. Plenty of shops register just to make their names sound more trustworthy. If I had to guess... perhaps six or seven out of ten.
In any case, it's common to meet Starweavers in all sorts of trades wherever you go.
Mr Cong, this year's building work at EverSpring has already gone well beyond the plan. It was meant to be a modest repair, and now there's even a tea room added.

Yes, I know — Li provided the silver for that. If his gift was accepted, why not mine? We Starweavers earn our living abroad and return home to honour EverSpring — it's been our custom for generations.

We truly cannot, sir. You know how people are — everyone wishes to contribute to EverSpring. The guild was never a grand one to begin with; it's grown brick by brick to what it is now. We can't continue like this forever.
If we keep building at this rate, EverSpring will wear itself thin — and we'll all end up rebuilding in the end.
I don't care. You've taken Li's silver, you'll take mine as well. If not, I'll come by in the dead of night and leave the money here myself.
Well... Mr Li has been waiting since the year before last for this year's building quota. He put in his request the moment it opened — there is, after all, an order of precedence.
Then use my silver to help the new Starweavers — just as the guild once lent its hand to me.
I'm not sure. But the Starweavers made this moon, piece by piece — there must be a way up!
And it's like a huge incense burner for our city! Someone's got to climb up and clean it once in a while.
Yes, but where's the way up? I can't see anything!
Shh, I'm thinking! I'll figure something out!

options.content: What are you two talking about?
Why do you want to climb it?

talks.content: Whoa! A foreigner!?
Someone said the very top's the highest place in Mistwharf! You can see the whole Mistwharf from up there. We just want to have a look!
See you, traveller! Come on, let's get back to figuring out how to climb it!
Do you like the big moon too?
Uh-huh! We want to count all the Chipgulls that fly over EverSpring in one day!

options.content: So it's not real? People built it?

talks.content: Silly Bunny! Everyone likes it! It's so big you can even see it from the sea!
What? Really? It's so bright and huge! How can you not like it? You must be fibbing!
You didn't know? Oh, right — you're not from here! The moon's actually a giant incense burner in Mistwharf. A really rich Starweaver paid to have it built!

options.content: Why did they make it look like a moon?

talks.content: Oh, I know this one! The Starweaver said people who sail away are like stars in the sky — they'll all come home one day! So home needs a bright moon to guide them back!
Aren't you a know-it-all! Then do you know what the Starweaver called it?
Erm... I forgot...
Ahem! Let me tell you then — it's called... Homeward Bright Moon!
That's such a long name! No wonder I forgot. "Big Moon" sounds much better!
Didn't expect to stumble upon something this old today. It seems barely stable enough to read the weather, let alone fortunes...
It must date back to my great-great-grandfather's time — or perhaps even earlier. Well, you get the idea. It's ancient.
Me? I happened upon this old Stellapass and thought I'd keep it as a curio. And you? Are you interested in relics as well?
Ah, a traveller with a taste for Huaxu craftsmanship. Then allow me to play the host — ask away, and I'll share what I know.
Ah... this Stellapass — now that's a piece of history!
There you are. You wished to learn about the Stellapass, did you not?
Reciting it by rote won't help. Use your head — you must understand it, or it will never stay with you.
Easy for you to say. I can hardly read, and that sheet's packed full of words. I can't make sense of them.
Packed? The Starweavers' maxims run to only seven lines. The Nine Chapters of Dafeng have nine!
Well, I've not memorised the Nine Chapters either...

options.content: What are you two talking about?

talks.content: Ah, you're a traveller, aren't you? Pardon the scene. My friend here's just joined the Starweavers — I'm teaching him our trade maxims.
Fulong, where do you think you're going? Back here! Keep reciting!
If they hadn't asked about them when we joined, I'd never have learnt a word. I trade fair and square — that should be proof enough, without all this fuss.
Nooooooo!!
Enough talk. Recite!

options.content: I'm curious about the maxims as well — what are they, exactly?

talks.content: You are? Very well then — one more listener won't hurt. You can both listen in.
There are seven in all. They go as follows:
Count not profit but righteousness as honour;
Count not splendour but virtue as nobility;
Count not cheapness but quality as value;
Count not cunning but honesty as skill;
Count not rarity but fitness as treasure;
Count not hoarding but kindness as wealth;
Count not rhetoric but truth as measure.
By Lord Argent — how did you remember every word? You've got second sight, seeing the text clear through the page?
Not everyone's as slow as you! Traveller, was there any line you didn't quite catch? I can explain it if you wish.
Good day. I'm the enquiries clerk for EverSpring. Should you have any questions about the guild or the Starweavers, please don't hesitate to ask.
Of course. What would you like to know? Is it about EverSpring and the Starweavers, the services we provide here, or something else?
Take care, and do visit again if you have further questions.
Long, it's been a while. Care to try the new Silver Needle? The fragrance is exquisite~
Still in the mood for tea, are you? Haven't you heard? A batch of Loong Qiqi incense has just appeared in Haojing — no one knows its source — and the price's shot through the roof!
It's always been expensive, yes, but this? Five, six times the usual rate! Someone's clearly manipulating the market, driving it up on purpose.
Easy there, Long — no need to blow your top. It's nothing worth losing sleep over.

Nothing, you say? Every shipment of rare incense in Haojing passes through me! My own batch of Loong Qiqi hasn't even arrived, and suddenly another turns up from nowhere — now my regular clients are demanding answers!
So you rushed all the way to EverSpring overnight? Come now, catch your breath — sit and have some tea first.
You sly old fox, Chawen — what are you plotting this time? Don't tell me you've a hand in that mysterious batch yourself!
Now, now — how could I be to blame? I'm merely saying that fretting won't help. Report it to EverSpring, and they'll handle the matter properly.
Explain everything to the higher-ups. Before long, Haojing will have more Loong Qiqi incense in supply, and the price will settle of its own accord, will it not?
You mean to say... EverSpring will intervene? And what would they gain from that?
Stability, of course. With prices like these, incense ceases to be used as incense — it becomes a game of hot potato. Keep this up and someone's bound to get burned.
So EverSpring will no doubt release another batch soon, just enough to cool the market down.
Hmph... I've never seen the like. They'd best act quickly.

Come now, Long, sit and rest a while. There's no cause for such agitation. I've been with EverSpring for decades — I've seen this sort of trick more times than I can count. Here, let me pour you some tea.
The Borealberry jam that came in yesterday — why is it still held up in inspection? I need my goods, and I need them now!
Please, Mr Smith, do calm yourself. I'll look into the matter straightaway.
Let me see... three shipments of Borealberry jam from Hyperborea — yes, they did arrive yesterday. But it appears there's been a small mix-up. We're still checking everything over.
My bakery goes through barrels of the stuff every single day! The order was late to begin with, and now I'm nearly out — by the time your inspection's finished, I'll have no customers left!
What's there to check, anyway? It's jam, not contraband! They didn't even bother inspecting it back in Hyperborea!
Please, Mr Smith — just to confirm. Of your three ships carrying Borealberry jam, were two fully loaded and one only half?
Certainly not! All three were full — I watched the dockhands load every barrel myself!
And that, I'm afraid, is where the problem lies. When the ships arrived, our tally clerk noted that one hull was riding noticeably higher than the others. That's far beyond normal wastage.
You mean to say... someone stole my jam en route?
We can't say for certain just yet. The Ministry of Fortune has already instructed all three captains to hand in their logbooks. We should have the truth by tomorrow.
All right then... could you take me down to the docks? Even seeing the barrels — from a distance, at least — would set my mind at ease.
Of course. Though the shipment has already been moved to EverSpring's warehouse. Come, I'll escort you there myself.
No matter how far I wander, I always end up here again. What is this place? Who... who am I?
A Wishen...? Yes... I remember now. Born for no reason... left to wander without purpose. But still, I long to go home... Can you tell me... where that is?
Lord Argent...? No... that's not me. Lord Argent watches over Huaxu. I'm only... a Wishen.
I don't know where your home is... but I don't think it's here.
Who are you...? Could you tell me... where my home might be?
Is that so... and yet... I always find myself back here... Home... where could it be...
Home... but where is it? And where am I...?
You've come back... breathe in... do you feel it? The air... there's a scent — faint, but unlike any other...
Strange... but it's there — like candles at home, once they've burnt away... A warmth that pricks faintly, yet feels gentle and comforting... almost intoxicating.

options.content: Maybe it's just the incense from those who come to pay their respects.
As far as I know, leaves don't turn into Wishen.

talks.content: Right? That scent — like candles at home, once they've burnt away... A warmth that pricks faintly, yet feels gentle and comforting... almost intoxicating.
You wouldn't understand... that feeling of finally going home...
No... not that. The incense of mourning carries sorrow and yearning, but never the scent of home. I've wandered so far, so many times... yet this fragrance always pulls me back.
Perhaps you're right... Then what am I... some soil... the air itself... a pebble by the path... Mmm... it feels so warm here... maybe I'll just stay...
That's why I always come back. No matter how far I go, I return. Tell me — could this be my home? Why else would I feel... so at peace...?

options.content: Any way you look at it, this place doesn't feel like a home.

talks.content: Tell me... could this be my home? When I was alive... did I live upon this tree? Could I have been... a leaf?
But I can feel it... I'm connected to everything here. We share one breath — breathe in... the warmth wrapping around us... pulling me back... Ah... I'm going home...
Maybe... maybe I really was a leaf once... yes... that's why it feels so familiar... This is it — this is my home. I'm a Wishen... born of a leaf!

O merciful light of Lord Argent, shine through the shadowed bourne; let lone souls and lingering shades not wander, nor remain forlorn. Let the woes of yore be laid aside; this day be ferried across, bathed in kindly light.
Greetings, traveller. A deliverance prayer — verses passed down through the Wuqiongzang Sect, to guide the Wishen here to peace.
By vow and decree we summon the lost: Cease your wandering; hasten unto the Realm of Bliss...
Ah, it's you. Would you lend your voice, and chant with me?

options.content: Could you recite the whole prayer?
What brings you to chant it?

talks.content: Of course. It would be better still if you joined me.
My father... he passed away last year. Now it's only my mother and me. Whenever I miss him, I come here to recite a prayer or two.
By vow and decree we summon the lost: Cease your wandering; hasten unto the Realm of Bliss...
O merciful light of Lord Argent, shine through the shadowed bourne; let lone souls and lingering shades not wander, nor remain forlorn.
Perhaps it does, perhaps not. For me, it's a small solace. When I was little, I always thought Father worked too hard. I used to tell myself — once I was grown, I'd let him live in ease and peace.
Have you heard the tale of Huaxu's Wishen? They are spirits bound by unfinished business, unable to move on. If Father still can't let us go... he might have become one too.
Let the woes of yore be laid aside; this day be ferried across, bathed in kindly light.
But before I could shoulder the family myself, he was already gone... So I come here and pray, hoping he's at peace, somewhere beyond my reach...
Perhaps... perhaps he'll come here too, one day...

options.content: What makes you think your father would come here?
If he could see you now, he'd rest easy.

talks.content: O spirits wronged and untimely dead, let every knot be loosed; all bonds and clinging longings — unbind, and fade with the light.

I cannot say... it's only a feeling. If he isn't here, then let this prayer be for the other Wishen still bound to this world. And if they cross paths on that unseen shore... please... tell my father of me.
Then... may this prayer reach the other Wishen still bound to this world. And if they cross paths on that unseen shore... please... tell my father of me.
The Bagua guideth the way; at the Gate of Water the path of blessing openeth. Pass onward to the gentle bourne — in quiet, safe and sound.
In lives to come, rise or fall as thy heart inclineth; sow thine own good fortune, and its fruit shall long endure.
By writ and vow we charge the dead: cast off the cloud of doubt; swift as the edict bids, depart to blissful fields.
Oh, Grandpa, you're being silly again! Not on the ground, not in the water — on my head! Hmm... if that's too hard, my shoulder's okay too!

options.content: Were you talking to a Wishen?

talks.content: Huh? Talking to myself? Maybe! But you spoke to me first — so now I'm talking to you!
Nope! Just me talking to me! But then you said something — so now I'm talking to you!
Then who were you really talking to?
You don't know where you are, do you, traveller from far away? It's scary here! Really scary! All the Loongcions and Earthborn who die in Huaxu — they all turn into Wishen and come here!
Well? Are you scared? If you are... you'd better run quick!
Grandpa! If you're really back, make a leaf fall on my head!
Hey! You really came back? Not even a little bit scared?

options.content: The Wishen won't hurt me. So why would I be afraid?
I hope you'll get to see your grandpa.

talks.content: Me too! But some travellers I met before — when they heard the dead turn into Wishen here, they just screamed and ran away!
I will! Grandpa's definitely coming back to stay with me.
They don't know the Wishen don't hurt anyone. They just stay here... really quiet...

options.content: So what are you doing here?

talks.content: Grandpa got really sick — he said it was something called "ageing". Then Lord Argent came and took him away. Before he went to sleep, he told me he once saw, at Twilight Ravine, people who died turning into Wishen.
He said maybe he'd turn into one too — then he could stay with me forever.
I waited and waited at home, but Grandpa never came back. Then Mum said the Wishen only live here... so I came to find him.

options.content: But it's so spooky here. Aren't you scared?

talks.content: Mum says we can't see the Wishen. So I told Grandpa — if he can hear me, drop a leaf on my head! But Grandpa's so silly... he still hasn't done it...
I was, at first. So I started talking to Grandpa. Then I thought... even if there are other Wishen here, they were people once too, right?

People who die still have family. And when there's family, someone's always missing them. Like me and Grandpa — even if he's gone, we still remember him. When I think about that... I'm not scared anymore.
Hmm... I wonder how long this tree has been standing here.
I asked Fang — he said it was already here when he got here. Jie said the same. But they've both been gone for ages now... So when did this tree start growing?
Hi there! Did you come to see the big tree too?
Heehee, I knew it! I told Fang and Jie people would be curious about it — but they just laughed! And look, someone really came!
Huh? You don't like trees? But this one's special! It's not like any of the others!
Bye-bye! Next time you come back, let's talk about the tree again!
Oh well... if you don't like it, that's fine. I'll just keep thinking about the tree. You can go talk to someone else!
I can hear it — the breath of all things: the whisper of leaves, the murmur beneath the soil, the drip of water. I can hear... everything.
Do you hear it? The tree — it keeps talking. None of them can hear... no one but me... only me.
Of course they do! You just don't listen — your ears are sealed shut! Be still. Feel it. Listen... there! It's speaking again — it's saying...
Hush... its voice... so faint... I can't quite catch it. Just a bit more time... just a little more...
This tree! It keeps talking!
I hear it! Louder than before! You — were you drawn here by the leaves as well? Tell me — did you hear it too!?

options.content: (...I'd better stay away from this lunatic.)

talks.content: No! Listen closely — beneath the rustle there's another sound, a whisper of its own. It's speaking again... calling to me!
I knew it — you're not like the others! What did it say? Tell me, quickly!
You'll come back... on the day the tree foretold.
Grow... yes. From a tiny seed to what it's become. Like you — walking from far away, each step taking root, a path growing a journey.

options.content: If you were alive, I'd tell you to see a doctor.

talks.content: Blossom... yes. A tree lives long, yet its flowering is brief — that's why every eye is drawn to it. People are the same: pulled by unseen seasons, and then — they bloom, sudden and bright. Even Lord Argent would pause to marvel.

options.content: If you were alive, I'd tell you to see a doctor.

talks.content: Decay... ha... Do trees mourn their own decay? When they fall, new life stirs beneath. Yet... that's my thought, not the tree's. To it, decay isn't sorrow at all...
The tree... it keeps repeating one line...
Hmph. You'll never understand — neither me, nor the tree. It doesn't matter. The tree has already told me... everything.
In the end, I've learnt this: everyone hears a different voice. The tree speaks what lies hidden in our hearts — and now it's calling my name...
It says... what has withered shall bloom again, what is lost shall return.
But beyond my name... I heard its own voice too. It's telling us...

options.content: If you were alive, I'd tell you to see a doctor.

talks.content: Do you know where we are? Every time my head clears, I end up back here. The clay idol on the offering table — its face all cracked, like the wall back home.
Home...? Can't call it to mind either. I only remember incense in the air — not this musty kind, but sweet, like sugar frosting. Did you have sweets where you're from?

I don't remember sweets, but we had a river — so wide you'd never see the far bank. In summer, people cast their nets, and the fish came up shining. One slap of its tail — and I'd be soaked all over. Ever seen fish that glow?
No... but I've seen a great wooden wheel, taller than this tree. When it turned, it hummed softly, lifting water up to the fields.
Once it jammed — lots of people gathered, knocking and tapping. I squeezed in for a look... and got a face full of mud. Heh... did you get mud on yours too?
How would a Wishen get mud on his face? Just the wind. Tell me — why are we here? I've walked off plenty of times, and always ended up back again.
Yesterday I walked east. Saw a field of wheat, all gold. I crouched to touch a handful — but the moment I reached out, I was back here again.
I want to go home... Tell me, where is our home, really?
Don't know... But wherever it is, it's surely not here.
Right... definitely not here.
Hey, you there! What are you gawping at? Yes, you. Don't look like you belong here... and sure as hell not one of the regulars. So, what brings you here, then?
Oho, got some bite, have you? This isn't a playground for brats like you. Only legends like me — hic! — the great Chizhatian — get to walk these streets, you hear?
Hey, I'm being nice here, you know! You don't even know the half of it — long ago, monsters called the Jiao haunted these parts. Man-eating beasts. Their favourite snack? Fresh-faced cubs like you!
You'd better start begging me to watch your back — hic! — or the Jiao will swallow you whole.
Heh, lucky you ran into me. Tell you what — buy me a fine pot of wine — hic! — and I'll make sure you get out of Haze Market in one piece. Deal?
You're drunk.
Me? Drunk? Nah — hic! — not me! Come here, I'll tell you all about the... hic!... the Jiao... hic!
Oi, kid — Haze Market isn't the sort of place you just stroll into for fun.
You again, eh? Hah... you don't often see the same bright-eyed youngster twice in this place. Back so soon? Not scared the Jiao will gobble you up?
(He seems a touch more sober this time...)

options.content: So what exactly are the Jiao, then...?

talks.content: Oh, curious now, are you? And here I was thinking Miss Zhiliu's honoured guest would've heard a few of Haze Market's tales already.
Oho, fiery little thing, aren't you? The last one who talked to me like that — hah, I threw him to the Jiao!
You knew who I was all along? Then why pick a fight with me on purpose last time?
But I know who you are — Mr Qiu's aide, Miss Zhiliu's honoured guest. So I'll be generous and let you walk away in one piece.

options.content: So what exactly are the Jiao, then...?

talks.content: Ha! That's the fun of it. Like I said — not many fresh faces like yours turn up round here. So — fancy hearing my tale of the Jiao? Buy me a pot of wine and I'll tell you.

options.content: Make it a good one, and I might.

talks.content: Heh-heh, knew you'd bite. In Huaxu's old lore, they say when the Loongscions fall under the Dark Loong's spell, they become dreadful creatures — the Jiao.
Tch... no fun at all, are you? I took you for a livelier sort than those coin-counting traders. Never mind — I'll just have to find some bargeman to fetch me a pot of wine instead.

The Jiao have no voices of their own, and they fear the light. They dwell in damp, shadowed caverns, feeding on the flesh of men. To draw their prey closer, they steal other voices — singing from deep within the dark.
Those who hear that hauntingly beautiful song draw closer, curious... and end up in the Jiao's belly. Now then — where do you think they gather most often?
Don't tell me... the cavern outside Haze Market?
Ha! Sharp little thing, aren't you! That's right — the Tidesong Cavern itself!
Are there still Jiao around these days?
No, not these days — no need for creatures like that anymore.
What's that supposed to mean?
It means what it means. Wouldn't be half as fun if I told you outright, eh? You're a sharp one — go on then, have a guess.
Why do you think no one's seen a real Jiao in years — only stories left behind? And why has the Tidesong Cavern fallen silent ever since Mr Qiu came?
Let's see... old cotton, bit of tung oil — pack it in tight. Two thin planks either side, nail 'em firm... aye, that'll hold her.
Kiddo, do me a favour — pass me the rivets from that tool kit of mine, will you? Look at these old nails — barely holding on. Leave 'em like this and she'll shake herself apart in no time.
(You follow his gesture, find the rivets, and hand them over.)
Cheers, kiddo. Right then... ha! Done!
Aye. Mr Qiu brought me in to patch this old tub up a bit. Man like him could build a few hundred new ones, yet he clings to this battered heap — funny thing, that.
Best step back, kiddo. I need to saw off this rotten bit — noisy work. Don't want you going half-deaf on my account.
Best patch that seam up soon... leave her soaking a few more months and the core'll rot clean through.
She's old, aye — but good timber lasts. Treat her right and she'll see out a few more decades yet.
Ah, you're back, kiddo. Got questions in that head of yours, or just here to shoot the breeze with an old carpenter?
Quite a few new faces in Haze Market of late — far too chatty when they trade. No class whatsoever.
Tell me about it. Saw this fine little trinket at a stall the other day — thought I'd buy it for the missus. So I asked the price, and guess what he said?
Let me guess — "family heirloom," "dug up from a tomb," one of those tales best left untold.
Worse — breaks the Market's rules! Everyone knows the golden line here: talk price, not provenance. Trade the goods, never the tale behind them.
Ha! That reminds me — a few greenhorns at my stall the other day, calling out prices in the open. Not a whisper of code between them. No respect for the rules at all!
Next time I meet Mr Qiu, it'll have to be somewhere respectable — a proper teahouse, not... whatever this place is.

Having to come down to Haze Market every now and then... dreadful for one's reputation! If anyone were to see me here, I'd never live it down — they'd say I was rubbing shoulders with crooks and swindlers!
You've got quite the opinion of Haze Market.

And who might you be? You don't look like one of the locals... Wait, are you from Mr Qiu's Archaeological Society? No, no, that can't be it — those students never carry anything half as dangerous-looking as that sword of yours.

So what exactly are you after, then? I'll have you know I'm one of Mr Qiu's honoured guests — here to discuss business! No need to go flashing that sword about. And just so you're aware — I'm carrying a Lunarose sachet!

options.content: If you despise Haze Market so much, why do business with Mr Qiu?

talks.content: Jumpy? Nonsense! I simply know better than to trust the sort that lurk around these streets. If you're not one of them, take my advice — keep your wits about you, or they'll have you fleeced before you know it.
Mr Qiu... he's different.
Off already? But you never told me what brings you here!
But if you are one of them... well — forget I said anything!

options.content: So you really despise the people of Haze Market?

talks.content: He's a man of real talent — everyone in business, every collector worth his salt, knows his name. More than that, he's a pleasure to deal with — it's like he sees straight through you.
Hmph! That lot — lawless ruffians, the sort who treat lives like weeds. The dregs of Huaxu — rot that's poisoned its very morals!
There's a saying — when you work with clever folk, you never need to finish your words. They'll catch your meaning and see it done before you even ask.
"Haze Market," they call it — nothing but a den of thieves and thugs! There's no honour among them — they'll chase any coin, however dirty. Pfah! As if any of them still knew what a conscience was!
Oh, plenty! Mr Qiu's generous to a fault — every batch of aged tangerine peel he buys off me is over a hundred years old! Not many in Huaxu can afford such treasures, I can tell you that.
Best keep your distance. Don't be taken in by their polite faces and fine clothes — every one of them's got blood on his hands.

options.content: But isn't Mr Qiu one of them too?
You really think Mr Qiu's clean?

talks.content: He even funds archaeology out of his own pocket! Without his support, half of Huaxu's glorious past would still be buried underground, never seeing daylight.
No, no — Mr Qiu's the exception! He's only here to keep that rabble in line, to stop them doing all those wicked, heartless things. He's the only decent soul in this pit.

Mr Qiu's like a lotus rising from the muck — pure and untouched by the filth around him! To stay that clean in a place like this, and still make a name for himself... remarkable, truly remarkable. You're too young to understand.
And besides that... let me think...

options.content: All right, all right — I get it, you're a hardcore fan of his.

talks.content: Generous, that's what he is! Those of us who deal with him often — every festival, every holiday — Mr Qiu never forgets us. One time it's fine pastries, another time rare curios... he's thoughtful like that, always is.

A what now? "Hardcore"? You young folk and your bizarre jargon — half the time I've no idea what you're on about! Just like my eight-year-old, always tossing around some new term... what was it she said the other day—?
If he weren't so good to us, do you think I'd drag myself all the way down to this wretched place just to wait on him?
Speaking of my little girl — she's quite taken with Mr Qiu herself! Whenever he visits, he brings her sweets, fine pastries... she's forever asking when he'll come again.
(Its form flickers between shadow and pale light, as though it's fighting itself.)
Huff...
Rraugh!
(It raises its head, bloodshot eyes meeting yours — whether from pain or the effort of holding itself together, you cannot tell.)
(As your blade flashes, the Bi'an snaps — its body swallowed by darkness as it lunges at you.)
...Groan... grhh... rrhh...
Awoo... whuh... rrhh...
(Before your eyes, the Bi'an takes its own life.)
(The creature collapses at your feet, its final breath fading into silence.)
(You lay the fallen beast to rest, as gently as you can.)
(From dust it rose — and to dust it fades...)
Brr... freezing again. Rotten weather. Everything's frosted up — gears stiff, sensors half-asleep. Oh dear. Mr Qiu'll have to foot the repairs again.
Hmm? Who are you? What are you doing out here? Off you pop, now. This isn't a place ordinary folk are meant to wander!

options.content: You looked as if you needed a hand, so I thought I'd check in.

talks.content: He did? That can't be right. He said the Gritblight Expanse was my brief alone. Before I left he even said— what was it — "no old records, nothing worth digging into," or something along those lines.

Oh, thank you, kind soul! I've been out here so long — camping in the wind and sleeping under the stars — that I'd almost forgotten normal life being existed... apart from those Sable Bi'an prowling around.
Still, you'd best go home and grab a thicker coat. With the swings here you'll be frozen stiff in no time.
Whew. I'd better throw on a couple more layers myself.
Hot one minute, freezing the next... My grandmother always said it used to be spring all round.
Ah—! It's scorching again! Heat makes me tetchy. Ugh, this wretched coat — off you come!
Hey! Who are y— oh, right, I remember you. Back again, are you? Brought a coat this time?

options.content: I don't mind the cold or the heat.

talks.content: Good. You've no idea how absurd this weather gets — teeth chattering one minute, sweating buckets the next. It's crazy.
What? Then you've not seen it at its worst. Give it an hour — teeth chattering one minute, sweating buckets the next. It's crazy.
Aw, don't go! Took me ages to find someone to chat with. If I don't talk to a normal human soon, my tongue'll go rusty.
Ha! You've come to the right person. I've been out here so long I've nearly pieced the whole story together — this place and that blasted Blightening.
What— no place to set the incense? Good job I brought a burner! After risking my neck to get here, it'd be a bit rich to leave empty-handed!

options.content: What are you doing out here? It's dangerous.
Linger any longer and a Sable Bi'an will be along to make a meal of you.

talks.content: I know! Thanks for the warning. That's exactly why I'm here. I'll light a stick of Lunarose for Lord Argent where only the brave venture, and beg Them to purge the Scourge of Zhuyin once and for all!

No need to fret. I know it's dangerous — that's the point. I'm lighting a stick of Lunarose for Lord Argent right here, where only the brave venture, and begging Him to purge the Scourge of Zhuyin for good.

Don't worry about me. I've no weapon, true, but I've got quick legs and a quicker head! It isn't my first time out here. You watch yourself — if a Sable Bi'an shows up, I'll be off like a shot and won't have time to haul you along.
Go on then — don't trouble over me!
Here we are! Once I light the incense, Lord Argent will surely descend and wipe that wicked beast out for good — just like in the old tales!
Huh? You again. You've got nerve, coming back to a place like this.

options.content: I could say the same about you...
I've got other things to do. I should get going.

talks.content: Ha! Fair point. Like I said, I'm quick on my feet. If trouble turns up, I'll be gone before it catches me. You should head out, though — safer that way.

options.content: I don't need to run. I can drive the Sable Bi'an off myself.

talks.content: All right, then. Until fate brings us together again!
Really? Didn't take you for the tough sort. You're not from Huaxu, are you? Your clothes don't look Huaxu, either.
Will you join me in offering incense, then? Two voices together — surely Lord Argent will hear us better.

options.content: Doesn't it feel a bit odd to offer incense out in the middle of nowhere?

talks.content: You don't know the half of it. You know why the skies twist and churn here, don't you? It's because of the Scourge of Zhuyin a hundred years ago. But do you know why that foul beast brought such ruin on Huaxu?
(You take a stick of incense and join him in the offering.)

options.content: So you mean to call Lord Argent the way people did in the old tales?

talks.content: All right, I won't keep you guessing. Long ago in Huaxu, there lived a wicked creature called Zhuyin.

That's right. These days everyone's burning incense everywhere — Lord Argent must catch it from all sides and hardly know who needs It most! So I figured if I burn mine here, where no one ever comes, It'll take notice.
It sowed unrest in people's hearts and drove them to harm one another. The land fell into misery and people knew no peace, so they lit incense — one after another — and prayed for Lord Argent's help.
Take notice of what, exactly?
On high, Lord Argent caught the scent of the incense, learned of Zhuyin's crime, and grew wrathful. It called on Its divine might and banished the beast beyond Huaxu's shores.
That there's incense burning in the middle of nowhere, of course! They'll see how sincere my heart is!
Then the immortals of the Xuanheng Sect combined their strength, bound Zhuyin with the Loong Seal, and sealed it upon the sacred mountain. Only then did Huaxu know peace again.

options.content: So you mean to call Lord Argent the way people did in the old tales?

talks.content: Right, enough chatter. Will you light another stick with me?
Great! Incense side by side today — fast friends tomorrow!
Fair enough — outsiders don't always get our ways.
Where's my purse!? I had it a second ago...
I only stopped for a moment to watch that vendor making sugar figures... then I reached into my pocket to buy one, and my purse was gone.
Was it stolen? Or did I drop it somewhere?

options.content: I can’t imagine pickpockets in Huaxu.

talks.content: Thank you... My purse's gone, and I can't even remember where I last had it. Maybe... maybe someone lifted it...
Y—You may be right... If someone really had stolen it, surely Bi'an would have intervened...
I'll have another look around. Thank you all the same.
Where's my purse!? I had it a second ago...
I've looked everywhere and still can't find it... What am I supposed to do now? I haven't even bought my boat ticket home yet...
Oh, it's you again. Did you find my purse? Or...
Ah... then I suppose that's that... It wasn't much, but it was everything I brought for this trip.
No. I'm from Mistwharf. It took me ages to get here by boat. I'd heard Haojing was a grand city, and it really is. Just look at those buildings. And the streets are so much busier than back home.
Since I can't find it, I'll have to ask the Ministry of Fortune for help. Maybe they can find me somewhere to stay for a while, until my family can send me some money.
There was so much to see — I got carried away... and before I knew it, my purse was gone!
That surprised me too at first. It's one of the Three Ministries, after all, and yet it still deals with small troubles ordinary people run into.
Quite a few people have offered to help me look for it... Haojing really does have a lot of kind people.
I actually just asked a local about it. He said Bi'an only deals with crimes and serious offences. There are plenty of things they either don't have time for or can't get involved in.

And if the Magistrates of Yingtian had to deal with every little matter, that would be overkill. So the Ministry of Fortune handles these day-to-day troubles instead, and they have people assigned to cases like this.
I'll wager it was that fast-talking hawker.

If you ask me, that lady can stop looking. I've had my eye on him from the moment he stepped onto this street. And out of everyone she crossed paths with, the dodgiest by far was that sugar-figure seller.

options.content: And what makes you say that?
Why were you watching her so closely in the first place?

talks.content: She passed plenty of people, but he only stopped at that sugar-figure stall. Rule out everyone else, and who does that leave? Her.

options.content: Couldn't she have just stopped to watch him making sugar figures?
You've got nothing to back that up.

talks.content: I wasn't watching her! I was watching that dodgy sugar-figure seller! Ever since he set up his stall next to mine, he's been luring all my customers away with that gaudy little act of his!

Exactly! That's the whole trick. Put on a flashy little show to draw people in... then while everyone's watching, his hands are so quick no one notices a thing, and your purse is gone before you know it!
Hmph! You just don't know him. Those flashy little performances are exactly how he lures people in. One day I'll catch him in the act, and then you'll see I was right.

options.content: If he truly stole it, why hasn't Bi'an come to arrest him?

talks.content: So I keep an eye on him day and night. One of these days I'll catch him in the act, and then I'll report him!

options.content: If he truly stole it, why hasn't Bi'an come to arrest him?

talks.content: That's exactly the trick that sugar-figure seller is pulling!

options.content: If he truly stole it, why hasn't Bi'an come to arrest him?

talks.content: Well... they're on their way! They'll be here sooner or later! Hmph, you don't know what you're talking about. I've no time to argue with you!
Don't fret, friend! Back home they call me the Master of Lost-and-Found. My wife misplaces earrings and other jewellery all the time, and I find every last one of them!
I've got a simple way of finding lost things, taught to me by a master from the Wuqiongzang Sect. Works like a charm, I tell you!

options.content: I'm curious. Care to explain it?

talks.content: Now that's what I like to hear! But first things first — let's help this poor traveller find her purse. Once I've found it, I'll tell you all about it.
Hmm... where could it be?
It works perfectly at home! Why won't it work out here in the street? Maybe I didn't learn it properly... that must be why it's failed me!
Oh, it's you. I still haven't found that traveller's purse... though she seems to have given up on it by now. She even asked me just now where to go for help if it really is gone.
Still... I can't work out why my method's failed me.

options.content: What exactly is this method of yours?

talks.content: Ah, it's one of those things — simple enough in practice, but a bit of a headache to explain. Still, if you really want to hear it, I'll do my best.
Ha! Knew you were the curious type. Very well. First, you need to figure out when it was lost — the month, the day, even the hour if you can. The more exact, the better.
A 31-day month counts as a Great Month. A 30-day one is a Small Month. And February... that's a Neutral Month.

For a Great Month, the order goes: Heaven, Earth, Spring, Star, Man, Time, Wind, Fortune, Clarity — then back round again. For a Small or Neutral Month, it changes: Heaven, Clarity, Fortune, Wind, Time, Man, Star, Spring, Earth.

options.content: Wait, wait... you've completely lost me. What do those words even mean?

talks.content: Heaven, Spring, Star, and Man — those tell you which way to look: west, south-west, north, and south. Earth means it'll turn up on its own in a couple of days.

If it's Time, that means it's been stolen — good luck getting that back! Wind means simple carelessness, or that they just haven't looked properly. Fortune means someone they know took it. And Clarity... for my missus it's almost always Clarity, because the thing's still at home somewhere.

options.content: And what did you get for her?

talks.content: To be honest, if it had been Time, I'd have given up. But it was Spring... so I turned everything upside down to the south-west of where she lost it, and found nothing!
Could it be... that she lost it long ago and only just realised? Ah... nothing I can do then!

options.content: That's far too complicated for me. I'm off.

talks.content: It was definitely the Spring sign... so why didn't it work?
Told you — there are pickpockets about on this street. Someone saw a little girl earlier — face all smeared with grime.
Pickpockets? In Huaxu? Don't be absurd. The Nine Chapters of Dafeng aren't just for show. If anyone tried it, wouldn't Bi'an be on them in an instant?

We're only talking it over — no need to act as though I'm wrong already. I'm telling you, I saw her. A little thief, plain as day. And I think she's not stealing things the usual way... There could be other tricks to it.
Tch... What "other tricks"? What, make the poor fellow's pouch sprout wings and fly off on its own?

I saw it with my own eyes... That little thief used some strange kind of magic. In a flash — whoosh! — a wriggling tentacle shot out, snatched something from a man's bag, then dropped it on the ground...
That's ridiculous. You expect me to believe that?
Mm-hm. The world's a big place. Stranger things have happened.
Boshan Incense House anniversary offer!
Boshan Incense House anniversary offer! Buy ten, get five free!
Boshan Incense House — a long-established shop with craftsmanship you can trust. Fine quality, fair prices, and service to match!
You've been standing here for a while now — are you interested in our incense? Please, do come in. Our attendants can help you choose the right incense and sachets.
We're a long-established shop, run directly by the Starweavers themselves. Our name speaks for itself, and so does our quality.

options.content: I've no real use for incense. And I already have a sachet.
Do you sell anything besides incense?

talks.content: Oh? Then you must not be from Huaxu. For people born here, incense is part of everyday life.
Of course. Aside from incense, we also carry our special Shujin sachets, and the accessories are sold separately as well. If you're looking for something decorative, we also have Ivorywood carvings.
That's all right. We also sell sachet pendants, carved scented-wood ornaments, and our most popular item — the Boshan censer.
But our most popular item remains the Boshan censer.
You might consider taking one back as a souvenir for a friend — a small keepsake from your travels.
Why not have a look? We've got our anniversary sale on today.
Boshan Incense House anniversary offer! Buy ten, get five free!
Out for another stroll through the market? Have you been in Huaxu long? Have you tried any of the local tea, or taken in the sights?
What brings you to Boshan Incense House today?
You're interested in our history? Well, you may know of the Starweavers — the merchant guild here in Huaxu. Boshan Incense House is one of the shops they run directly.

We have branches not only in Haojing, but throughout Huaxu. Incense is our main trade, though we carry other goods as well. People come to us for our good name — and because our incense speaks for itself.

options.content: I came from Mistwharf. Why don't you have a branch there?
What exactly is a Boshan censer?

talks.content: You've travelled a fair bit within Huaxu, I see. Yes, though we're run by the Starweavers, we don't have a branch in Mistwharf.

It's simply a vessel for burning incense. The first was forged on Mount Boshan, and the name has endured. It's small and exquisitely made — practical, and pleasing to the eye as well. It's one of our most popular items.
It's not for lack of trying. We opened one once. But the locals were long accustomed to buying their incense from EverSpring. We drew customers at first, but in time, business dwindled.
Have you ever been to Mount Boshan? It's a lovely place — beautiful scenery, and Huaxu's best-known source of incense.

options.content: I haven't, but perhaps one day.

talks.content: And so our Mistwharf branch closed its doors.

I hope you get the chance to see more of Huaxu while you're here. It's not like the lands beyond, where Filthoids are a constant threat. Here, under Lord Argent's protection, we've known peace for centuries.
Safe travels. Do come again.
Just so we're clear: I'm very particular about incense. If it's too dry, I won't take it. And if the scent fades too fast, I'm not interested either.
Of course. We'll do everything we can to meet your requirements. Some blends may be out of stock at the moment, but I can check when the next shipment is due.
Go on, then. But let me be clear — I want it delivered as soon as possible. I can wait, but not for long.
Certainly — we won't keep you waiting. I'll check with our other branches first. If they have what you need, we'll have it sent over straight away.
Very well. I must say... Boshan does know how to look after its customers. Just don't forget—
Of course — we'll make sure the quality is exactly as you require.
The incense you sent last time was excellent. I'll have more of the same — delivered to my house again.
I've compared quite a few incense houses, and in the end Boshan has been the most dependable. I've bought well over a thousand catties here over the years, and the quality has always been steady.

options.content: Why do you buy so much incense?

talks.content: Me? I'm an incense blender. Naturally I buy in bulk and develop new blends at home.
Years ago, I used to place orders with smaller, local incense shops. The prices were lower, yes, but the quality varied wildly.
Later, friends kept telling me not to fuss over saving a bit of money. For independent blenders like us, consistency in raw materials matters far more than saving a little on the cost.
If you develop a blend with one batch of raw materials, then make it again with another and the finished scent turns out completely different, that does your reputation no favours.

options.content: True enough. If I were the customer, I wouldn't be pleased either.

talks.content: Still... even though Boshan's quality is dependable, they don't always carry the rarer materials, or ones from very specific places of origin. For those, we still have to source from independent suppliers.

Well, the name says most of it, doesn't it? I develop and blend incense independently. Huaxu has always taken incense seriously. If everyone relied only on the formulas handed down by the Hall of Incense, things would grow stale soon enough.
Take Loong Qiqi, for example. It's a rare material, hard to come by. If you want the real top-grade stuff, you have to go to the coastal region it comes from and seek it out yourself.
So in private, we like to experiment with ingredients and come up with blends of our own, for customers who want something a little different.
Well... it all comes down to how seriously people in Huaxu take incense. That's why we spend our days racking our brains over every little step.

Developing new blends consumes a great deal of raw material. Growing those materials myself would be far too difficult. Oh, some people do manage it. But for someone like me, it makes far more sense to buy from a reputable incense house.
Alright, take care. I'll see you around.
And that's why I stick with Boshan Incense House. Reliable as ever.
Who makes candied fruit like this...? If someone with bad teeth ate it, they'd be at Zesheng Pharmacy before nightfall with toothache.
Serves me right for being greedy. I've been sampling things all the way down the street. Never thought I'd run into anything this vicious. I'm done. Never again!
Candied fruit... Want to try some? No idea what they've coated it with, but it's way sourer than any of the others. Look at this slogan — "Huaxu's Sourest." Honestly, who would buy that...?
(You take a piece from her and cautiously bite into it...)
Probably for the best... Better stay away from anything that vicious.
Why aren't you saying anything? Are you alright? Hey... hey!
(With a single bite, the sourness hits so hard your insides twist into knots, your whole face puckers up, and your mind goes utterly blank.)
Why won't anyone try my pastries...? Is it the way they look? But they smell amazing...
W—Would you like to try one? Free samples, of course... And if you like it, maybe take some home for your family...
(You glance at the boxes of sweets laid out before her. One of them catches your eye.)
Y—You like this one? It's my special Fish-Scale Cake. I slice fresh local fish from Haojing, marinate it in vinegar, then layer it over a lotus-flavoured sponge. But... no one will even try it.

options.content: I'm not surprised no one wants to try it...

talks.content: W—What? I spent ages perfecting it... I even gave it a name. Lotus Vinegar Fish.
How could that be? I worked on this new treat for so long. If you don't like it... then... then try this one!
Do you want to try some? It really is delicious. I added lots of vinegar... and the fish is lovely and fresh too.
A fried dough stick soaked in stinky tofu brine, then coated in flour and fried all over again. The process is terribly complicated. One batch takes ages. I call it... Stinky Delight.
Something came up at home. I have to go!
Why won't anyone try my pastries...? Is it the way they look? But they smell amazing...

Hm? Oh, it's you again! You actually came back. You did like the pastries I made, didn't you? Do you want Lotus Vinegar Fish or Stinky Delight? Um... actually, maybe not Stinky Delight. It hasn't sold in ages, so I took it off the menu.

options.content: Maybe... just maybe... that you're not good at cooking?
Have you come up with anything new?

talks.content: How could that be? I've always been good at cooking. When I was little, I used to make my father treats of my own invention. I once made...
I've never stopped chasing my culinary dreams!
Caterpillar Lettuce Rolls! Fresh caterpillars from the garden, heads removed, wrapped in lettuce leaves and grilled over the fire. When you bite in, it goes crunch!
Ta-da~ A brilliant new treat, made with one of Huaxu's signature incense materials. The texture's special too. Want to try it?

options.content: Tell me what it's made of first...

talks.content: Oh, right, I still make Caterpillar Lettuce Rolls. Want to try some?

options.content: Ah... I really should be going. Good luck with the new recipe!

talks.content: I chop Ivorywood into cubes and mix it with tofu. When you eat it, you get the firmness of Ivorywood and the softness of tofu. They balance each other perfectly!
Huh? Why are you running again!? Is my food really that awful...?
Wait... Ivorywood might not be edible. Or is it? Anyway, the texture is... very good! Do you want to try it?

options.content: Ah... I really should be going. Good luck with the new recipe!

talks.content: Huaxu special snacks! One bite and you'll be back for more!
Just look at that glossy chilli oil. One bite, and it'll warm you right up in winter or perk you up in summer. Properly invigorating, this is!
And it's got a story behind it. Ever been to Cloudweave Valley? Years ago, I was there on business and ended up staying for a while. This was what the locals treated me to.

The first time I tried it, I was gasping for breath. The moment it hit my tongue, the heat struck first — so fierce it felt like it went straight through me. Then the saltiness came through, clean and sharp. Only after that did the flavours of the ingredients begin to open up.
In Cloudweave Valley, these are a local favourite — hotpot skewers. Care for a taste?
Of course it is! If it weren't, why would I have stayed in Cloudweave Valley for so long just to learn how to make it?
There you go! Don't be shy — have a couple more!
So then, fancy a taste? Free samples!
(Hot, hot, hot, hot, hot! This is way too much for someone who's never tasted anything this intense...)
Why's your face gone red? Are you alright? Want some water?
Water... I need water...
That used to be a little cloth-shoe shop. Now look at it — a woodcarver's stall... East Market's changed so much.
Haven't walked through here in ages. These old bones don't care much for traipsing all over the city anymore.
Don't think I've seen you before, child. You're not from Haojing, are you? Here to pick up a souvenir, perhaps?
Ah, yes... visitors to Haojing always end up wandering through East Market. But for us locals, there's nothing much here that feels new anymore.
Hmm... truth be told, not really. East Market's changed beyond recognition these past few years. The old shops we knew have either shut down or moved elsewhere.
If you've the time, you'd do better to see more of Huaxu. There's far more worth seeing beyond the city.
So I won't recommend anything at all. Rather than buying souvenirs here, you'd be better off leaving the city and taking in the scenery.
That used to be a little cloth-shoe shop. Now look at it — a woodcarver's stall... East Market's changed so much.
Back again, child? What a coincidence. These legs of mine aren't what they used to be, so I don't come this far very often... and yet here we are, running into each other again.
Ah... takes me back. When my husband was courting me, he used to find excuses to run into me everywhere... and in the end, he won me over. But... ah...

options.content: I... I wasn't trying to bump into you like that...

talks.content: What are you on about, child? I don't come here much these days. It was my old man who was always here — he loved the bustle. Whenever he went out to buy meat and veg, he'd make a detour and come here instead of going to West Market.

options.content: So he doesn't come here anymore?

talks.content: He passed on last year... so I won't be walking this way with him again.
Haha! You're an amusing one, child. I didn't mean anything by it. Seeing you just reminded me of my late husband... Ah, best not dwell on that.
East Market's been turned into a tourist strip these days. Most of the old shops where we used to buy the usual things have shut down.
Until next time, child. And remember to haggle a bit when you buy something. Don't just hand over your coins straight away.
Look around — where d'you see anyone selling fruit and veg now? It's only the young ones who come for the buzz.
Maybe it's just as well... He's gone now. If he could stroll through here again, he'd be disappointed, I reckon.
(His eyes are sharp and unreadable. He watches the passing crowd in silence. When you stop in front of him, his gaze fixes on you at once.)
What is it?

options.content: Shouldn't you be the one telling me that?
You're the owner, you tell me.

talks.content: Mm... I run this place. I sell timber. Are you buying?
Mm... yeah. Just opened up. I sell timber. Are you buying?
Alright...
You... again.
Last time... you said you weren't buying. So why are you back today?
Just passing by. Thought I'd see how business was treating you.
They told me to open a shop in Haojing. Said people here liked woodwork.
But nobody comes in. Business isn't good.

options.content: Why do you talk like that?
What do people buy timber for?

talks.content: I'm... not good with words.
Lots of things. Folding screens. Tables. Stools...
If I take it slow, I can get it right.

options.content: What do people buy timber for?

talks.content: Most of it has to be carved. I can do that. I just need time.
So, furniture?
Mm... sort of. But nobody's buying. People don't want it. I rented this place for half a year. When the lease is up... I'll leave.
People say you look a bit intimidating, so they're afraid to come in. Maybe you should smile more?
Intimidating? Smile...?
(He hesitates, as though trying to work out which muscles to move. After a long, awkward moment, he forces his face into something meant to be a smile. It looks strange.)
Like this...?

options.content: (Pat him on the shoulder.) Let's not force it... your usual face is fine.
(Give him a smile.) There you go. Something like that next time.

talks.content: Mm... right. Maybe I'll carve a smiling face into the wood instead. That's easier.
Thanks... I'll try. With everyone.
Good day! You'd look lovely in our designs. Fancy trying something on at Qianxiu Pavilion?

Care to have a look? Qianxiu Pavilion is one of Haojing's best-known ready-to-wear shops, and every piece is hand-stitched by our own seamstresses. If anything catches your eye, I can bring it over for you to try on.

options.content: It's too much hassle trying things on.
What's wrong with what I'm wearing?

talks.content: You're a visitor, aren't you? We have a saying here in Huaxu: "Fine feathers make fine birds."
You already carry yourself beautifully. The right outfit would only bring that out even more.
Why not step inside and have a look?
Of course. Take care, then. If you ever feel like stopping by, you're always welcome.
New dishes at Tongfu Eatery! Incense in the cooking — an aroma you've never tasted before! A secret technique taught by a master chef from distant lands!
Good day! Here for a quick bite or a proper meal? We've just added a few new dishes to the menu, and they've all been going down very well. Care to try one?
Certainly! We've got three to recommend today — one sweet, one savoury, and one sour. What are you in the mood for?
The chef at Tongfu Eatery's lost his mind! He's actually chopped up Auntie Wan herb and mixed it into the meatballs!
You've no idea — I've always hated the smell of Auntie Wan. One whiff of that stuff and it feels like my nostrils are under attack!

And get this — he's even given it some fancy name: "Emerald Meatballs". I went over thinking it had to be something special. Turns out it's just minced meat mixed with Auntie Wan, wrapped in sticky rice dough.
You can't smell it when they bring it out, but by the time you taste it, it's already too late! What about those of us who can't stand Auntie Wan?
What!? You actually like Auntie Wan!? No, no — I can't even talk to you right now. Anyone who likes that stuff must have something wrong with their nose.
Exactly! If they're going to use something with a smell that strong, they should put it clearly on the menu. Tell people before they order, so they can decide for themselves!
Tongfu Eatery owes me for this! I went out to treat myself to a nice meal, and all I got out of it was a foul mood!
And now look at me — I went out to treat myself to a nice meal, and all I got out of it was a foul mood!
Hey, take it easy. Just skip the place next time.
You're right! I'm never going back. From now on I'm eating at Bazhen Pavilion just down the street!
You didn't go rushing over to Tongfu Eatery? Hmph. I knew it. Customers aren't all fools. The ones flocking over there wouldn't know good food if it hit them in the face.
Just look at Tongfu Eatery — nothing but gimmicks. Throwing pungent herbs into dishes and calling it innovation? It's an insult to Huaxu cooking. Utter rubbish!

options.content: Come on. Is it really that bad?

talks.content: You tell me! In Huaxu, we do things properly. A good dish gets its fragrance from proper ingredients, proper seasoning, and proper heat!
See? You know I'm right. And our regulars at Bazhen Pavilion? Every last one of them knows their food.
Not from cheap tricks like that... Anyone who really knows food would laugh at the lot of them.
When they taste a dish, they care about what it's supposed to taste like — how the seasoning and ingredients come together. Not this flashy nonsense. Hmph.
All sparkle, no substance. Have they forgotten what Huaxu cooking's really about!?
All sparkle, no substance. Have they forgotten what Huaxu cooking's really about!?
Oh, brilliant. They've lured the customers right over. As if it's anything more than a passing novelty. People will get bored soon enough. Do they seriously think that rubbish is good?
I don't buy it... no way it's that good. You — yeah, you! Come here a moment!
Yes, yes — you. Come here. I need a favour.
Fine — don't help, then! No need to pull that face. Who needs you anyway?
Have you tried Tongfu Eatery's new dishes?
Here's what we'll do. I'll give you some money. Go in like a regular customer, order a few of their new dishes, and bring them back here. What d'you say?
That's more like it. Here — this is for you.
All sparkle, no substance. Have they forgotten what Huaxu cooking's really about!?
Well? Did you bring it back?
Here you go.
(He snatches open the container, bends down to sniff it carefully, then somehow produces a pair of chopsticks and pops a bite into his mouth.)

That's... really good! They haven't smothered the dish in it — the original flavour's still there. The herb just lifts it, gives it a bit more bite. Hits the mouth and the nose at the same time... ah. Now that is exquisite.
You don't taste something like this every day. Brilliant... Absolutely brilliant!
(He doesn't answer. He's already lost in the food, oblivious to everything else.)
Xiufang... don't leave me... Xiufang...
(The man reeks of booze. You hesitate, wondering whether to slip past him — then he grabs your arm.)
Xiufang! You came... you finally came! Don't... don't marry him, alright? Don't leave me... please... I'm the only one who's ever loved you with all my heart...

options.content: Hey. Look at me. I'm not Xiufang.
(Say nothing and let him mistake you for his ex-wife.)

talks.content: You're not...? I... I... *sobbing* She really isn't coming... she really isn't...
Xiufang... you've no idea how much I've missed you... Why — why won't you see me?
Waiter! Three more jugs! Tonight I'm drinking till I drop!
Is he really that good? Good enough for you to spend your life with him? Or... were all those promises you made me just lies?
Xiufang... I swear — I'll stop drinking. I will. We can... we can start over...
(A sob catches in his throat. He sways, then crumples to the ground and passes out.)
They brought Emeraldfinches to Haojing!? That's unbelievable!
You've got to hand it to the East Market merchants — they'll make a gimmick out of anything.
What are they trying to sell anyway? They're not plucking the birds' feathers to make ornaments, are they?
Oh, don't be so grim. They're for admiring, of course. Sipping tea while watching the birds does make for a rather refined little pleasure, doesn't it?
Charming, perhaps, but how do they make sure the Emeraldfinches actually fan their tails for the customers to see?
Ah, that's the clever part. They've hired the finest painter in all of Huaxu to cover folding screens with lifelike female Emeraldfinches.

They put one in every private tea room, then let the males loose. The poor things don't know where to look, dazzled by all those painted females on the folding screens, so they start fanning their tails like mad, afraid they'll miss their chance to impress them.
Trailing Glory Teahouse... is it round here somewhere?
The flyer said East Market, but I've already checked several streets and still can't find the place.
Oh, excuse me! Have you seen a teahouse called Trailing Glory? I heard they have several beautiful Emeraldfinches there. I've adored birds ever since I was little.
The moment I heard Haojing had a place like that, I was so thrilled I rushed straight over... but I can't seem to find the place anywhere.

options.content: I've no idea where it is.

talks.content: Oh... that's a shame.
Trailing Glory Teahouse... is it round here somewhere?
I finally get a chance to see Emeraldfinches up close, and yet the place is never open when I go!
Oh! It's you. Are you looking for Trailing Glory too?
What? No, no, I did find it in the end. But when I went in, the place was completely empty. The owner said they'd lost all the birds at Port of Parting Stars...
Isn't that absurd? How do you lose a whole flock? What am I meant to do now?

options.content: Don't worry. I'm sure they'll be found.

talks.content: I suppose you're right, but... Ah well, there's no point fretting over it. Thanks. I do feel a bit better now.
It's a shame... ah well! I'll give it a little time, then come back later and see whether they've found them.
(sobbing) No... Lord Argent, it's not fair... My teahouse hasn't even opened yet, and the finches we ordered have vanished without a trace... What am I supposed to do...?
I picked out all that tea, and it's still sitting at home untouched. The bird feed's still sitting there in the teahouse going to waste. At this rate, I won't even be able to pay the hands I took on!
Why does this sort of thing always happen to me...?
It's my own fault. I should have just stuck to painting. What possessed me to open a teahouse in East Market?

I let that embroidery seller put ideas in my head. I was drawing embroidery patterns for him as usual that day — just a few apricot blossoms, and that should have been the end of it. But then he asked me to paint an Emeraldfinch.
To paint it properly, I had to go out and watch them for myself, studying how they moved until I finally got it just as I wanted.
As soon as I finished, a wild male Emeraldfinch came over, stared at the painting for a moment... and fanned its tail. I could hardly believe it!
I thought, well, I'd never seen anything like it. So I told the merchant about it the next day, and he said the painting was so finely done that the bird had mistaken it for the real thing.

Then he said my work ought to be seen by more people. Why not paint a whole set of lifelike female Emeraldfinches, put them all together, lure in the males, have them fan their tails, and charge people to come and admire the spectacle? We'd make a fortune, he said.
And that's how Trailing Glory Teahouse came about. But... who could have known it would end up like this...?
Now I've nowhere else to turn. All I can do is pray the men sent to fetch the birds will bring back as many as they can. Even a few would help...
Boat rides! Ten coins a trip! Tickets here — line up! Once the boat's full, we're off!
Good morning! Heading to the West Market by boat?

options.content: I can get there on foot.

talks.content: You'll need to queue at the back for a ticket first. Everyone else is waiting their turn. You look like a sensible sort — you wouldn't jump the queue, would you?
You jest, {性别:sir|miss}. You must not mind a long walk. It's nearly an hour on foot from the East Market to the West Market.
(You queue up, buy a ticket, and board the boat.)
That's why we run these boats across the lake, so people can get where they're going a bit faster.
(The ferry carries you across to the West Market.)

Locals use them to get across the city quickly, especially when they're in a hurry. As for visitors — well, they come for the experience too. With scenery like this, a boat ride on the lake is a pleasure in itself.
Wouldn't you agree?
Boat rides! Ten coins a trip! Tickets here — line up! Once the boat's full, we're off!
Good morning! Heading to the West Market by boat?
Not many people about today, so no need to keep you waiting. We'll set off at once!
Very well. Come and find me if you'd like a boat ride!
(The ferry carries you across to the West Market.)
Something's off about Haojing's layout... the more I look, the stranger it feels.

The East Market lies to the right, yet turns in towards the left; the West Market lies to the left, yet turns in towards the right. The two face one another with a stretch of ground between them. The city was clearly planned to suit the terrain — good for trade, and convenient for the people.

But that lake in the middle of the city stands several feet above both markets, and the whole face of the rise is so smooth and level it looks as though someone had sliced it away with a blade. It does not look like a natural formation at all.
Tell me, how do you suppose such a rise came to be?

options.content: It's only a bit higher up. What's so strange about that?
Must be Lord Argent's divine power at work!

talks.content: No, no, that is not the point. The West Market is where people live, and the East Market is the city's commercial heart, yet both lie very low. If the lake ever rose in flood season, would it not pour straight into both markets?

Just so. Do you know what I was thinking, staring at that lake just now? It is almost as if, when the city was built, some monstrous thing rose up from underground... only to be struck flat in a single blow.
No, no, that will not do. When we come upon something we cannot make sense of, we ought to look into it and learn the truth. Only... this one truly is difficult.
Still... Haojing is under Lord Argent's protection. If there truly were such a danger here— ah, listen to me, talking nonsense and tempting fate. No. Impossible.
What kind of power would that require? Surely no one in all the world but Lord Argent could accomplish such a thing.
I have stood here for weeks and still cannot make sense of it. Perhaps the day I finally do will be the day I move on.
Remember when it used to be quiet round here? Drop a line and you'd pull up a couple of big ones in under half an hour.
But look at it now. Pleasure boats running back and forth all day, oars splashing, waves slapping, Loongscions and Earthborns laughing and shouting from one end of the boat to the other.
And the fish? Long gone — driven right down to the depths. I've been sat here for half the day now and haven't had so much as a nibble. Whole trip's been for nothing.

options.content: You could always fish somewhere else.
Maybe it's just you. I could catch fish here easily enough.

talks.content: I've been fishing this stretch for over thirty years... I know exactly where the big ones gather, which bank the current runs steadiest along. You get attached to a place like that. Hard to just up and go somewhere else.
Ha! Barely out of nappies and already talking big, are you?
Still, you're right. Haojing's changed — busier now, more crowded. Everything changes. Why should us old codgers be the only ones stubborn enough to keep clinging to the same old patch?

Back in the day, I could land seven or eight big fish in a single morning. The restaurant owner used to wait for my catch before he even fired up the stove. And you've got the nerve to say it's down to my skill?
Ah well... I'll go and have a look at the ponds outside the city tomorrow. My legs aren't what they used to be, but I ought to learn to move on, oughtn't I?
If you're that full of yourself, then here's what we'll do. We come back at dawn, before the boats start running, fish this very spot, and see who catches more. What do you say?
If you really commit to practising the Five-Animal Frolics, all those little aches and everyday niggles will ease on their own.
If you really commit to practising the Five-Animal Frolics, all those little aches and everyday niggles will ease on their own.
The body stays sound when everything inside is flowing as it should. Once that flow is blocked, problems start creeping in one after another.
That's why you have to keep moving. Once the body loosens up, all that stiffness inside starts to ease, and you feel better all over. Am I right?
You there, young friend — I've seen you about before. Are you interested in the Five-Animal Frolics as well?
Really? It's rare to see someone your age take an interest in this sort of thing. My own son? Tell him to turn in early and rise with the sun, and he'll argue with me half the night.
So then, would you like to practise with us? Or is there something you want to ask?
There are five forms in all, each based on an animal native to Huaxu.

The Skink, the Rainseer Frog, the Angler Heron, the Petit Boar and the Red Fox. Each form trains a different part of the body. The Skink form, for instance, focuses on the hands — grip, control and dexterity.
The Rainseer Frog form works the legs. Have you seen how they leap? We may be old, but we still need to get about now and then, even if we're no longer as spry as the youngsters.
The Angler Heron form helps loosen the neck and shoulders. Years of bending over books or work take their toll. By the time you get to our age, you're stiff from morning to night.
The Petit Boar form builds strength through the whole body. You put some force into it, like a Petit Boar in a temper. It's excellent for loosening the muscles and joints.
As for the Red Fox form, it sharpens speed and reflexes. Red Foxes are nimble, quick-witted creatures — darting and springing about the fields so lightly that no one can ever catch them.

options.content: Those don't sound like the sort of animals you could really imitate.

talks.content: Ah, you're looking at it too narrowly. The Five-Animal Frolics aren't about copying an animal's movements exactly. They're about borrowing what each creature does best and turning it into movements that suit the human body.
When I first learnt the set, I'll be honest — some of the movements didn't feel quite right. So I had my son help me adjust a few things. The version we've got now fits us old folk like a glove.

Go through a full set and you'll work up a light sweat, but feel comfortable all over. It won't wear you out, but it won't feel like a waste of time either. If you ask me, you youngsters ought to give it a try.
If you ever feel like joining us, come here at dawn. We practise here every morning.
That can't be right... I only knocked that Five-Animal Frolics picture book together on a whim. It can't really be doing them any good, can it? Or are they just muddling through it on their own?

options.content: Hey, what are you sneaking about here for?

talks.content: Ah—! I don't know anything! I'm just an illustrator! I didn't do anything! All right, fine, yes, I drew the Five-Animal Frolics — but I never thought anyone would actually take it seriously!
I hadn't even said anything, and you'd already told me everything.
I—I... whew. I thought it was the children of those old folk coming after me. So you're just some traveller passing through... You nearly scared me half to death!
Listen, please don't tell anyone I had anything to do with the Five-Animal Frolics. Just pretend you never saw me, all right?
They don't seriously believe in that Five-Animal Frolics stuff, do they?
I've been hanging about here for days now, keeping an eye on them, and from the look of it, they're not even following my drawings properly.
Then again, in the Frog form I drew, you're supposed to leap three feet into the air. No way those old folk could manage that... which is probably just as well...
Ah! You again! The one who knows I drew the Five-Animal Frolics! Why are you back? I didn't do anything, I swear! I'm only watching to make sure they don't hurt themselves!
(He's giving himself away again...)

options.content: Why do you think they might hurt themselves?
Why did they think your picture book could help with their health?

talks.content: What else? I draw picture books. Most of my work's about cultivation, immortality, all that mystical stuff. As for the Five-Animal Frolics, I only knocked it together on a whim.
Ah... that's a long story. Most of my picture books are about cultivation, immortality, all that mystical stuff. And, well... to help them sell, I'd sometimes dress the part.
Some of the movements are completely ridiculous. Unless you're someone like a Magistrate of Yingtian, there's no way an ordinary person could pull them off.

You know — the whole enlightened-master act. Flowing robes, solemn face, the lot. If people asked, I'd tell them it all came from my own cultivation experience. Of course, nobody really believed me. They just took it as sales patter.
And they're all old folk. If they insist on copying my drawings and end up pulling something or taking a tumble, who do you think they'll come after? Me, obviously!
But somehow, once the story got around, it started to take on a life of its own. Before I knew it, people were saying I was some enlightened master, or even one of those immortals...
Still, after watching them these past few days, I've realised it's not as bad as I thought. They're sharper than I gave them credit for — they've toned down all the more over-the-top bits I drew.

And after that, people kept coming to ask how I trained, how I sought immortality. So I thought... well, if they were halfway to believing it already, I might as well lean into it and knock together some "cultivation method" to sell them.
Hah! Now that I look at it, it's actually rather convincing. It almost looks like a genuine cultivation method.
You know the rest. Most people didn't buy it, but for some reason that old fellow who came asking for the Five-Animal Frolics believed every last word.
If he wants to get up early and practise, fine... but why does he have to drag me out of bed as well... yaaawn...

He found some dodgy little booklet from who knows where, and now I'm the one getting hauled out of bed every morning because of it. None of the other old folk make their children come along, so why am I the only one stuck here?
If we weren't out here in the street, I'd just lie down and go straight back to sleep. Ah... I miss my warm blanket... my nice soft bed...
You... haven't got anything to do, have you? Good. Come stand in front of me and block out the light. I'm going to shut my eyes for a bit.

options.content: Why don't I pull the sun out of the sky for you while I'm at it?

talks.content: That's a splendid idea! Go on, do it now!
Ah! Brilliant! Why didn't I think of that? One leaf to shade the eyes... though a bit of the light still gets through. Never mind. I'll make do and try to sleep anyway.
If he wants to get up early and practise, fine... but why does he have to drag me out of bed as well... yaaawn...
Brilliant... bril... br—snrrk—!
(The drowsy man lets out a loud snort and jolts awake.)
Mm... snrk... When did I fall asleep? What time is it now? Is the old man still doing his Five-Animal Frolics?
Oh... this late already? Mum should be bringing food over before long. Hm? You look a bit familiar. Have we met somewhere before?
Ah, that's right — you're... um... ah, never mind. I know I've seen you before.
Me? I'm waiting for my father to finish his Five-Animal Frolics. No, that's not right. It's not that I want to wait for him. He made me stay here!
