My old man got hold of some picture book from who knows where and started treating it like some kind of sacred health guide. Then he dragged half the neighbours into getting up early every day to practise. Look — see that group of old-timers over there? That's them.

options.content: What does that booklet have to do with you?

talks.content: Nothing at first... ah, well, I suppose it's my own fault. After he brought it home, I had a quick look through it and found some of the movements downright absurd.
My mum? Hah! She's not in the same boat as me. If I say I'm not coming, the old man'll come at me with a broom. If my mum says she's not coming, he won't dare make a peep.
If someone without years of physical training tried copying them, they'd definitely end up injuring themselves.
That's what you call... what's the phrase again? Ah, right — the pecking order at home. And me? I'm right at the bottom.

So I found a bit of time to rework some of the movements, make them a bit more manageable. And somehow that turned into, "Well, since you revised the booklet, you're coming along and helping us train." Now I'm hauled out here every morning!
See you around! Next time, could you bring me a pillow?
You have no idea how early they start. I never get enough sleep. I'm dying here...
Us Haojing lot — apparently all we do is eat and drink. That's our life~

That's what that fellow said to me last time. Well? Sounded like him, didn't I? Truth be told, he wasn't entirely wrong. What is there in life besides eating and drinking? It was the tone of it that rubbed me the wrong way.
Hmph... the more I think about it, the more it winds me up! Forget it. Even if he asked me over for a game, I wouldn't go. Hm? And who might you be?
A traveller, eh? Well then, let me have a word with you.
Now then, Zhang, that's enough of that. Don't go scaring kids off like that other bloke did.
I'm only joking! First time in Haojing, is it? If there's anything you don't know, just ask us old-timers. You'll usually find us here in the West Market anyway.
That's right. We've lived here our whole lives. If you're looking for a proper meal or a nice drink, we can point you in the right direction.

options.content: Anything fun to do in Haojing?

talks.content: Plenty! If you want a proper meal, just head over to the East Market, pick any restaurant you fancy, and order whatever they're known for. You won't be disappointed.

There's always something going on around the square in front of the hall — temple fairs and the like. Come festival time it gets so crowded you can hardly move. Not for us, though. We like a bit of peace and quiet.
Specialities? None worth mentioning! I'll be straight with you. All that so-called "local produce" in the East Market is there to fleece visitors like you.
Ah well. New faces come through this city every day, but the old familiar ones get fewer and fewer.
Anything bad would've gone out of business years ago. The places still standing are the ones Haojing folk keep coming back to.

Yeah. That's why we live on the west side. This is the old quarter. Much quieter than the East Market. See these houses? They've all been patched up over the years. They didn't use to look half this fresh.
Now, now. If you really want something to take back for family and friends, my wife makes pastries at home. If you don't mind something plain, I could bring you some.
We're getting older, while the city grows newer by the day. Sometimes I think... we've hardly seen any of the world ourselves. Before we're laid in the ground, perhaps we ought to travel a little.
You? Travel? Out of all of us, you're the one who can't bear to leave Haojing.

When you've lived somewhere all your life, you grow attached. How could you not? Still, off you go, kid. No sense wasting your day on two old relics like us. You'd do better to spend it seeing more of Haojing.
Look at you, in such a hurry. Careful now — don't go tripping on the stones.
Always rushing about, just like my own boy. He hasn't been home for quite some time now, and not a word from him either.
Oh? What made you stop? Where were you hurrying off to?

options.content: I just came over for a chat.

talks.content: I should think so. You young people have spring in your step. At your age, you hardly feel tired at all.

Oh, that's kind of you, dear. That's how it is when you get old. Your children go off and live their own lives, and sometimes you only see them once in a great while. They've barely sat down before they're off again.
Just the other day I saw a tall lad jump up, spin in mid-air, and then spring off as if it were nothing. It was like something straight out of the old Huaxu tales. Quite a sight, that was.
When they're away, the days drag on and on. But the moment they come home, time flies, and before you know it, they're leaving again.
Ah, listen to me, going on like this. Thank you for keeping an old woman company for a while.
Look at you, in such a hurry. Careful now — don't go tripping on the stones.

You do look awfully familiar. Weren't you the one who went flying past my roof the other day? Honestly, you kids these days — the roads in Haojing are perfectly good, and still you have to go flying about.

options.content: It wasn't me. You've got the wrong person.

talks.content: Wasn't it? Let me get a proper look at you... Oh, perhaps you're right. That one was dressed all in black, and you're in white from head to toe — even your hair. Must be my old eyes playing tricks on me.
Don't mind an old woman's fussing, dear. It's dangerous to go flying about over the rooftops like that. Think of your parents — if anything happened to you, they'd worry themselves sick.
What!? It's gone up that much!? You can't be serious.
When I was little, my mum would give me three coppers every morning. I'd spend two on a plate of pan-fried dumplings, and after school I'd still have one left for a tanghulu skewer.
And now, the moment you buy anything to eat, you're thirty coppers down. That dumpling stall down the lane shut down ages ago, and the stuff in the East Market is dear enough to make your eyes water.

options.content: Sounds like prices in Haojing have gone up quite a bit.

talks.content: Tell me about it. I've lived here all my life. No one feels it more than I do. These days, where in this city can you still get dumplings for two coppers?
And I heard there's a new bakery in the East Market selling those desserts that are all the rage in Hyperborea. Prices are through the roof, and people still queue up for them all day long.

options.content: Maybe they pay people to stand in line.
Maybe it really is that good.

talks.content: That actually makes a lot of sense. You're young, but you know a thing or two about these sales gimmicks. I wasn't interested in the place at all at first, but when you see that many people queuing, you do start to wonder.
Who knows? There's no shortage of good food in this world. I'm not about to pay a fortune just to try it. Though... I suppose trying it once for the novelty wouldn't hurt.

I really miss that clay-pot noodle stall outside the school. The moment it opened each day, the smell would drift in through the windows and set my mouth watering through the whole lesson. Haven't the faintest where it's gone now.
Hm... now that I think about it, maybe I should go and see what all the fuss is about.
I'll need to put this place down for repairs as soon as possible. If one of the main support posts rots through, the whole thing could come down and hurt someone passing by.

No. Quite a few of these old houses on the west side of the city were left behind when their original residents moved away. Once a place stands empty, it falls under the Ministry of Fortune. We come by from time to time to deal with any problems that turn up.

Leaking roofs, damp walls, loose tiles — problems like that all need seeing to. These houses have stood here for generations. In a way, they're antiques — just not the kind you can simply move and put away.

options.content: What about the people who used to live here?

talks.content: Quite a few of them have been fixed up by the craftsmen at the Hall of Craft, so they look sound enough from the outside. But the structure's still old, and sooner or later problems will start to show.

options.content: What about the people who used to live here?

talks.content: Moved away, I'd imagine. By now it must have been several generations. The ones still living round here are mostly old folk who can't bear to leave the old place behind. The young tend to move elsewhere.
Oh, all sorts of places. Most move to other cities. There are plenty of well-known ones in Huaxu. Others go to the newer districts on the outskirts of Haojing.
But wherever they go, so long as they remain within Huaxu, they are still under the protection of the Nine Chapters of Dafeng.
Ma... Pa loved you so much. Wherever he is, he wouldn't want to see you in tears.
Ma, please talk to me... You've been crying this whole time. It hurts to see you like this...
Your pa's gone... he's gone...
Ma, didn't you always tell me that when people die, they turn into stars in the sky? Maybe Pa's one of them now... watching over you.
Don't cry... Ma. If your eyes get all puffy, you won't look like yourself anymore.
He's gone... how could he just leave me behind...
Ma... Pa loved you so much. Wherever he is, he wouldn't want to see you in tears.
Ma, please eat something... Look at you, you've got so thin...
Have you come to pay your respects? If you've brought an offering, you can leave it in the wooden box outside. My mother's not really up to talking right now.
Oh... you're wearing white, so I thought you were here for the funeral. Sorry about that.

options.content: You don't seem all that sad.

talks.content: It's only because I can't fall apart right now. You saw my mother... ever since Pa died, she won't listen to anyone.
If I don't hold this family together now, no one will.

options.content: You're far too mature for someone your age.

talks.content: Is that... a compliment? When Pa was ill, he told me that once he was gone, I'd have to take care of the family.
No one knew Ma better than he did. And now... it's all turned out just like he said it would.
So I can't cry right now. I have to stay strong... for her.

options.content: You're doing well. You're a brave kid.

talks.content: Thank you.
(As you turn away, you think you catch a glimmer in the corner of her eye.)
What were you thinking? Who books a band for a funeral these days?

What are you talking about? Having suona at a funeral is tradition. Your great-uncle worked himself to the bone all his life — can't we at least send him off properly? Make sure it's not all cold and quiet?
That's ancient history. Nobody in Haojing does that any more. The minute that suona starts up, it'll wake the whole neighbourhood. Then someone will go and complain to the Hall of Founts.
I booked them ages ago. Paid a deposit and everything. The neighbours all know. I don't believe people have turned their backs on tradition to the point they'd complain about a funeral!
This isn't about what other people think. Those are the rules in Haojing. Fireworks are banned in the city during the Grand Incense Rite too, aren't they?
The artificers at the Hall of Craft said that once this smoke purifier's ready, we'll be able to set off fireworks again.
So that means they haven't finished it yet, right?
Don't talk nonsense. It'll be finished this year. Then we'll have fireworks in Haojing again, just you wait!
Lin... from the moment we met at that poetry gathering, it felt like we'd known each other for years. You don't come by friends like that often. Here's to you, brother.

Last year, I wrote to invite you back to my hometown. I promised I'd knock walnuts down from the trees for you myself. But you wrote back saying you were unwell. Then other things got in the way... and before I knew it, it slipped my mind.
Where's that sound coming from...? It sounds so familiar...
That's wedding music... Is there a wedding nearby?

Ha... Lin, do you hear it? Remember when we were travelling together? You snapped off a willow branch, tapped it against the water to keep time, and sang... it was this very tune. "To the Groom." You said that when I turned fifty, we'd sit down together and have a drink.
I've brought this cup for you. You always used to say one drink was enough for you — never any more than that. But today...
Ha ha! Go on — drink! Drink your fill today! Joy, sorrow... pour it all into this cup. Even if death has come between us, we're still raising it together.
Overgrown Hutong... should be this way...? Or...
If I don't find the place soon, the food'll be cold by the time it gets there. I've already had three complaints this month. One more and I'm in for it.
Though... come to think of it, none of this is really my fault. If anyone's to blame, it's...

Oh, lots of people! First off, the cook started messing about as soon as he got to the stove, going on about how the "breath of the wok" wasn't right today. He had to make two practice dishes before he even started on the customer's order.
Then, just as I'd packed the food up and was about to head off, the boss's little girl latched onto me and refused to let go till I'd told her a story.

And on top of that, the customer's address was no help at all. All they gave me was the name Overgrown Hutong, but nothing about where to find it — whether it's near the Port of Parting Stars or closer to the Hall of Founts.

options.content: Why is the boss's daughter at the restaurant?
What's this "breath of the wok" supposed to mean?
If delivering food is your job, shouldn't you know your way around?

talks.content: Ha! It's a long story. Back then, it was just the boss cooking at home. He was such a good cook that word spread all around the West Market, and before long people were turning up at his door hoping for a bite.
I don't really know either. I can barely tell soy sauce from vinegar, so you're asking the wrong person.
I'm not a local! You can't expect me to know every street in the city.
Eventually they started feeling bad about freeloading all the time, so they talked him into opening a private kitchen. That way they could eat his cooking fair and square.
But I'll tell you this: if the boss were cooking it himself, he'd never fuss about the "breath of the wok" like that. He's been away lately and left the whole place to his apprentice.
Besides, I only got to Haojing about three months ago. Up till a month ago, I could barely understand the local dialect, and I'm still learning.
So really, the restaurant is just his home. Having children around at home is perfectly normal, isn't it?

options.content: You'd better hurry and deliver the food.

talks.content: That guy's a real pain. He keeps saying he can't let his master lose face, so he practises the dish several times before he even starts on the real order — and I'm the one who ends up late with the delivery...

options.content: You'd better hurry and deliver the food.

talks.content: Maybe cut an outsider a bit of slack, yeah?

options.content: You'd better hurry and deliver the food.

talks.content: Oh no! And now this is your fault as well! If you hadn't kept me talking, I'd have delivered it ages ago!
That little tucked-away place? Yeah, I've heard of it. It's tiny — hard to get a table. If we go now, we'll probably be out of luck.
Every place I suggest, you shoot down. What exactly do you want from me? Fine — don't bother treating them at all, then.
Now, now, my friend — no need to lose your temper. It's no good for your health. We've guests coming from far away, and I only want to host them properly. That's why I'm trying to choose carefully.
Save it. I'm done. Go ask someone else. Ah, what about that one over there in white?
(Both turn towards you.)
Friend, might you help us settle this? I take it you heard what we were talking about just now?

options.content: I didn't catch much of it.

talks.content: No matter, I'll explain. I have an honoured guest arriving soon, and I'm trying to choose a suitable restaurant to host them. I can't quite make up my mind, so I was hoping for a second opinion.
Excellent. That saves me having to explain it all again. We've narrowed it down to three places. Let me run them by you.
"Second opinion," my foot. He's just been driving me up the wall.
First, Tongfu Eatery. It's in the East Market and only just opened. They specialise in fusion cuisine, and the dishes are quite inventive. The only thing is...
Tongfu Eatery's dishes are inventive. Your guest may well enjoy trying something new.
Bazhen Pavilion does classic Haojing fare. Just avoid the dishes outsiders might find harder to appreciate.
How do you know you can't get a table if you haven't even tried asking?
The only thing is that you think fusion food loses the real character of Haojing cuisine.
There, you see? That's exactly what I've been saying all along. Just stop overthinking it and listen.
Not entirely... In any case, the second is Bazhen Pavilion. It's been around for years. It used to be in the West Market before it expanded and moved to the East Market.
You may have a point. Perhaps I'll go with...
If you ask me, that's the obvious choice. Proper old Haojing fare, and the place is respectable enough. More than suitable for an important guest.
What is it now? At this rate, every restaurant in the city will be shut before you finally make up your mind.
And yet they haven't introduced a new dish in years. They're still coasting on past glory.
Fine. Then the third — the private kitchen in the West Market. People queue for ages just to get a table. And somehow that still doesn't satisfy you.
You said yourself — I might have to queue for ages. My guest will be here in just a few days. What if we can't get a table before then?
You see? This is exactly how he drives me mad. I'm done. You sort him out.
Must be a miracle I found this place. Who knew there'd be food this good hidden down a little alley like this?

Of everything I tried, the Jade Velvet Slices stood out the most. They were so delicate they nearly melted in the mouth. Made with tender winter melon and simmered in a bamboo shoot broth, the dish had a depth of flavour I never would have expected — richer even than braised pork trotter.

And the dessert... the osmanthus and condensed milk worked beautifully together. Once it came out of the steamer, they set a preserved plum on top and pressed it in ever so lightly, just enough to draw out a touch of tart juice without disturbing the cake's texture.

Those flavours... they were exquisite. Truly exquisite. I've spent years travelling across Huaxu in search of fine cooking, and I thought I'd tried everything worth trying — yet this little kitchen has completely won me over.
Haojing really is full of hidden masters...
Zhang, your mynah was rattling off a few lines of poetry today. Been listening to your grandson practising at home, has it?
Rubbish! Why can't it just be that the bird's clever? Heard it once and picked it right up, just like my grandson. That boy learns fast.
Honestly, Zhang... your grandson... where do I even begin? How can you say that with a straight face?
I've lived my whole life straight and honest. Never once have I told a lie!
All right, all right. You two are at it again. Come on, let's talk about something else. My Chirrup Warblers moved this morning — they've built a nest in the old locust tree by the gate.
No wonder you didn't bring them out for a stroll today. So they've moved to a new spot.
Though... do either of you know what's got into Li today? He's gone and caught himself an...
An Angler Heron, I heard. That codger gets stranger by the day! Our grandsons are in the same class, so I tried talking to him about how the boys were getting on, and he just snubbed me!
I got so worked up we had a proper row, and now he's at it again today, making a spectacle of himself.
Ha! And you think your temper's any better?
What's that supposed to mean?
Come on now, that's enough, you two...
Common folk, showing off their plain little birds, as if any of them could hold a candle to mine.
Come on, Nitwit, give them a proper squawk. Let them hear what the grandest bird in all Haojing sounds like.
Go on! Squawk! What's wrong with you?

options.content: Have you tried giving it something to eat?

talks.content: I fed it a whole bucket of fish this morning. Its belly was bulging by the time it was done. Don't tell me it's hungry again already.

What's that supposed to mean? Don't tell me... this bird understands what I'm saying? Well, I'm not bullying it. I just want one good squawk out of it, so those old fools over there can see whose bird's the best!
Though looking at it now, its belly doesn't seem that big... What is this thing, some bottomless pit?
Common folk, showing off their plain little birds, as if any of them could hold a candle to mine.
I've fed you and given you water, so come on, make some noise! Let them hear you!
Come on! Goo-goo! Gah-gah! Goo-gah! Goo-goo-gah-gah!

options.content: Why do you care so much about making it call?

talks.content: Oh, it's you. That trick you told me to try didn't work. This Angler Heron still won't make a sound. I've fed it, tried coaxing it, done everything I can, and still it won't call.

options.content: You got a grudge against them or something?

talks.content: So those idiots can hear it, obviously! The louder the better. If it could deafen the lot of them, even better!

options.content: You got a grudge against them or something?

talks.content: A grudge? Hah! As if I've nothing better to do than hold grudges!
It's just that the way they carry on gets right under my skin. I got so sick of the lot of them that I went out and bought this Angler Heron just to get back at them properly!
See that one there, the one with the full head of grey hair? His wretched grandson's spoiled rotten at home and thick as a brick at school.
That boy's not half the student my precious grandson is, and yet that old fool goes round bragging about how bright and clever he is. Absolute nonsense!
Then there's that other one, the gap-toothed codger. Heaven knows what goes on in his head. He keeps birds here in Haojing of all places, and not just one — a whole lot of them!

Those Chirrup Warblers have no manners at all. They're always flitting about and fouling wherever they please. The other day I was lying in the courtyard enjoying the evening air, and one of the blasted things flew straight over my head and took a—!
(The old man's voice cuts off at once. When you look at him again, his face is red, and the words seem to stick in his throat.)
Pah! Forget it. Just thinking about it pisses me off. They're all a pack of idiots! This time, I'm going to make them pay for it properly!
Come on! Nitwit, squawk!
(You recognise the board as a Huaxu pastime. You once read about it at EverSpring, though you never really understood the rules.)
Interested in Xiangqi too, are you?

options.content: I know a little. Not much.
I don't understand it at all.

talks.content: Take a look at the board. Black's up a pawn but down an elephant. Red's two chariots are working well together, but they still haven't managed to break through Black's cannons. What do you reckon — who's got the better game from here?

Perhaps. If Black moves the horse from four to six, then brings the cannon from eight to six, both of Red's chariots come under threat. If Red moves a chariot, the horse falls; saves the horse, Red loses the initiative.
Red could play chariot four to six. If Black captures, then chariot eight to six follows at once. If Black sidesteps instead, he loses the cannon and gives up the initiative.
A sensible answer. The board looks settled at first glance, but both sides still have room to turn it around. Hard to call it either way.

options.content: If you can see all that, why not tell them?

talks.content: My young friend, Huaxu has an old saying: when watching a game, a true gentleman keeps his counsel. That's why I keep quiet.
Shall we invite Mrs Chen round? Have a little get-together at ours — play a bit of dominoes.

I haven't really had the time lately. My son and his wife have been arguing day in, day out. I turn in as soon as it gets dark, only to be woken in the middle of the night by them quarrelling. Still, it's between the young ones. It's not really our place to interfere.
So all I can do is lie there and listen to them go at it till first light. Ah... I'm getting too old for all this. One late night and I'm aching all over the next day.
You can't just let them go on like that. You've got to look after yourself. If it comes to it, have them stay somewhere else for a few days. They can come back once they've sorted things out.
When I get the chance, I'll have a word with them. If they do move out, you must all come over and play dominoes with me.
The other day I even picked up a set of dominoes made from mutton-fat jade. They're smooth and warm in the hand. When they move out, you'll have to stay and play with me for days on end.
Weren't you just saying you can't manage a late night anymore? Funny how you perk up at the mention of dominoes.
They're not the same thing. Well then, are we playing or not? Mrs Chen still owes me a hairpin from the last game. Heaven knows what she'll end up handing over this time.
Alright then! I'll go get her right now!
You're really asking for it! I turn my back for five minutes and look at you! Home. Now. And do your homework!
I'm not going home! I want to stay out and play with Tangdou! I don't want to study! I don't want to practise writing! No!
Tangdou's in the top three every time. And you? Bottom of the class, every single time. The teacher keeps calling me in, saying I let you run wild at home and never discipline you properly.
Honestly—! I ought to give you a good—

options.content: Ooh, someone's getting a good hiding!

talks.content: (Her hand flies up in anger, then hangs there in mid-air. After a long moment's hesitation, she slowly lowers it.)
You wretched little brat! Ugh...!
Mum...
Fine, go on then. Go play with that bunch of little troublemakers. Just make sure you're home early.
Thanks, Mum! You're the best mum in the whole world!
(He darts off and vanishes in an instant.)
All he wants to do all day is run about outside. His homework is nothing but scribble. You could stare at it all afternoon and still not make out a single character.

And what's this supposed to be? After "I wandered lonely as a cloud...", he writes, "...then tripped and shouted right out loud." What sort of nonsense is that? That boy really does need a proper talking-to!
Why are you looking at me like that? You think I'm going to hit him? The Nine Chapters of Dafeng don't let people beating their children whenever they please.

options.content: And if the Nine Chapters didn't exist... would you?

talks.content: Just try sitting down with him over his homework once, and you'll be grinding your teeth too.

The maths teacher gave them a problem the other day. He sat there counting on his fingers for ages and still couldn't work it out. It went like this: six Loongscions go to the market. Each buys eight fish. How many fish do they bring back altogether?
Exactly! If only my boy were half as sharp as you.
Are you joking, or is your arithmetic just as hopeless as my son's?
That boy stared at the page for half an hour. I kept pressing him for an answer before he finally looked up at me.
I asked him if he knew the answer. He just blurted out "18." I told him that was wrong. After another long pause, he came up with "28".
I didn't know whether to laugh or cry. I said, "Why don't you just start at zero and guess every number one by one?" And he nodded and said, "Mum, you're right."

I was fit to burst... but what else could I do? In the end, I had to teach him a daft little trick. I said, "If you can't work it out, draw it. Draw six Loongscions, each with eight fish. Then count them properly."
And do you think that helped? Ha! I'm getting angry all over again just thinking about it. He drew one Loongscion with two fish in his hands, two on his shoulders, and two under his feet.
Exactly! I asked him the same thing. Do you know what he said? He scratched his head for ages, then said, "Mum... he's got nowhere left to carry the fish."

options.content: Your son... might actually be a genius.

talks.content: It's not funny one bit! Just thinking about it sets me off all over again. Honestly, the Nine Chapters of Dafeng ought to give us parents some sort of exemption.
So that before I lose my mind altogether, I can at least take off my shoe and give him a couple of good smacks on the backside!
Sorry I'm late... I tried to sneak out, but Mum caught me...
You didn't get in trouble, did you? If she was going to tell you off anyway, you might as well have stayed at home.
How could I? We said we'd look after the kitten every day, didn't we? I brought her some ham. I stole it from the meat Mum had hanging up in the yard.
Hey! That's for the festival! If your mum finds out, she'll definitely tell you off again!

She tells me off no matter what I do. One more thing won't make a difference. The other day I was doing a maths problem. She said if I couldn't work it out, I should draw it. So I did... and then she told me off for that too.
Why would she tell you off for drawing it?

You tell me! It's not my fault, it's the question. It says one Loongscion goes to the market and buys eight fish to take home. Who does that? Who buys eight fish at once? You can't even carry that many!
Haha... it's just an example the teacher made up. It's only a maths problem, silly.
Whatever... it still doesn't make sense. Of course I couldn't work it out. But...
But what?
Do you think the kitten could eat eight fish? Should we bring her eight fish?
We're still balancing this year's tax ledgers, and next year's audit's already looming... I'm run off my feet.
And that's not even the worst of it. The most urgent thing right now is— ah! The port fire safety inspection! I nearly forgot!

options.content: What's a port fire safety inspection?

talks.content: Huh...? What else would it be? Fire safety at the port. Same as anywhere else — something catches fire, you put it out.
You don't seem the type to ask something that basic... Oh! I get it. You mean, it's right by the water, so why would it even need fire prevention? Right?

options.content: I mean the actual duties. What does the job involve, day to day?
What I mean is, why are they only starting to do this now?

talks.content: Ha! Knew it. Well... part of it's just down to history. The Port of Parting Stars was built a long time ago, and back then they didn't exactly plan for this sort of thing.
Oh, right. Hang on, that's oddly specific. Why are you asking in such detail? Don't tell me you're here to inspect my work...? No, you don't look like an inspector.
Er... well... Haojing's an ancient city. When the Port of Parting Stars was first built, people just didn't think about things like that.

The warehouses along the shoreline are packed close together. Once a fire takes hold, it spreads fast and is hard to contain. Even a full team of Loongscions would struggle to bring it under control quickly.
Ah, never mind. You're not catching a genius like me off guard that easily.

Not that there was nothing in place. It's just that a lot of the old fire points had fallen into disuse, broken down, been abandoned, or else had too little water pressure. People treated fires as rare accidents, not something worth preparing for properly.
And Huaxu folk can't live without incense. The port warehouses are full of it, along with silk, timber, oil-paper... all the sort of things that go up from a single spark.

Fire safety work is fairly straightforward. You prevent fires where you can, deal with them when they happen, and clean up afterwards. The real trouble at the Port of Parting Stars was that, for a long time, no one took prevention seriously.
Then a few years ago, there was a major blaze. Some foreign merchant ships were here for the Grand Incense Rite, loaded with incense, and somehow a fire broke out.
If some idiot forgets to snuff out their incense... honestly, it doesn't bear thinking about.
The new man in charge does, though. There was that major fire a few years back... Since then, we've had night wardens patrolling the port district every evening, keeping an eye out for fire hazards.
In any case, ever since then, whenever the Grand Incense Rite approaches, we go over all the port's firefighting equipment from top to bottom to make sure nothing like that happens again.

We've also rebuilt several warehouses, torn down a lot of old shacks, and moved the lamp oil into separate storage with proper firebreak walls. More recently, we've had the artificers from the Hall of Craft dig ponds and wells and improve the fire pump carts.
That's the general idea. We're still fine-tuning things, of course. If you have any suggestions, feel free to drop a note in the Hall of Founts' suggestion box — someone really does read them.
I was up all night poring over the old texts. My eyes are shot... at this rate, I'll be at the Spring of Yu before long.
When I first joined the Hall of Founts, I used to see Li brewing herbal tonics every day and think he was old before his time... Looking back, he was the sensible one after all.
Seems I ought to find time to visit Zesheng Pharmacy myself and get something to keep me going. I'd quite like to keep this old body going a few more years yet.

options.content: Is the work at the Hall of Founts really that tiring?
Isn't Zesheng Pharmacy for treating illnesses?

talks.content: Well... that's not an easy question to answer. Of course it's tiring, but not in the same way as manual labour. It's not the sort of work that leaves you sore and bruised and sprained every other day.

Oh, come now. If you're run down, that's illness enough. Being worked half to death counts too. The apothecaries at Zesheng know their trade. They put together different herbal formulas for different ages and conditions, which makes things a good deal easier.
You might want to get something from Zesheng Pharmacy yourself. You do look a bit pale. Maybe it's just your clothes washing you out, but either way, a tonic wouldn't hurt.
Most of the time, it's dealing with all sorts of people, then spending the whole day checking endless piles of figures. And if you make even the slightest mistake in the sums...

For students who spend all day bent over their books, they've got little herbal pills to soothe tired eyes and clear the head. For those of us worn out by work, they even make restorative herbal blends in little sachets, so you only need to brew one up each day.
Ugh... no. I'd rather not think about it.

And of course, older people often like to buy stronger tonics. But those aren't much good taken on their own, so Zesheng Pharmacy will even prepare them for you, turning things like donkey-hide gelatin into cakes and sweets.
My wife's bought them a few times. I tried some myself, and they were actually rather good. If she hadn't stopped me, I'd have eaten the lot like snacks.
You know what the Grand Incense Rite means? Time off! I've always wanted to go to Hyperborea and see the snow...
Whoa, whoa, hold it. Before you start planning your perfect holiday, how about we deal with all the work for the Grand Incense Rite first?
Too late... my mind's already out of the Hall of Founts. My soul's halfway to Lord Argent on the back of a Chirrup Warbler.
Right. When you get there, do ask whether Lord Argent is pleased with this year's festival supplies. And while you're at it, see if they'd like to finish the work you've been dodging.
Oh, listen to you, asking Lord Argent to do our work for us!
You've got it backwards. I'm not asking anyone to do your work. I'm saying you've still got a pile of it waiting, and here you are daydreaming.
Tch. You're young, and already acting like an old stick-in-the-mud. Can't even take a joke. What's wrong with daydreaming about something nice while we're out here getting some fresh air?
These numbers shouldn't be in this column... did I put that in wrong?
That can't be. Ever since the new measure came into force, there shouldn't really be anyone left unregistered now, whether they're residents or merchants.

options.content: Why wouldn't they register before the new measure?

talks.content: Mostly because it's a hassle. Some only come to Haojing for short-term jobs. Unless they're planning to settle here, they usually don't bother registering with the Hall of Founts.

Mm... it's actually quite simple. We spoke with the incense wardens at the Hall of Incense. Any registered resident receives an extra stick of incense for free each day when they go there to make an offering.
Even when we go door to door, some people are away for work or travelling, so the figures can end up a little off.
It's not especially precious incense, of course, but people tend to think — if it's free, why not? ...Ah, probably shouldn't have said that... I didn't say anything! You didn't hear a word!

options.content: How do you tell who's registered and who isn't?

talks.content: As for merchants, that's even easier to understand. Anyone doing business in Haojing is supposed to pay the market licence fee on time. If they don't register, that's one payment they can dodge.

Ah... that's thanks to a rather amazing art called Incense Discernment. We asked the Xuanheng Sect's incense wardens who master it to mark registered residents with a distinctive scent, different from the usual incense.

If you're planning to stay in Haojing for the long term, do come to the Hall of Founts and sort out your census registration first. We're even giving away a special Lord Argent plush doll at the moment. Well? Want one? Just go get it sorted now!

Ordinary people wouldn't be able to tell the difference, but anyone trained in the art of Incense Discernment can spot it straight away. After all, the very first thing you learn is how to recognise scents.

The effect doesn't last forever — it usually fades after two or three months. Luckily, Haojing folk take their daily offerings seriously, so they just go back to the Hall of Incense and have it renewed before it wears off.
Next time, come straight to Hall of Founts. Putting it off only makes matters worse.
I know you've got important business to attend to. I thought I'd just sort out these minor trifles myself... didn't want to be a nuisance...
That would be fine, if you were actually capable of sorting it out. But you aren't.

Take this well. If you'd reported it dry, we'd have fixed it ages ago. But no, you insisted on digging it yourself. And the result? You've undermined your neighbour's wall, caused a collapse, and injured someone!
It... it was an honest mistake, truly... I never realised my sense of direction was quite this rubbish. I could have sworn I was digging downwards...
Whatever the excuse, in future, come to us the moment trouble strikes. We'll sort it out straight away — just stop meddling with things you don't understand!
Why has the Hall of Incense put in for a budget top up this year? What exactly is it for?
You haven't heard? Ah, right, you were on leave when they came to file the request.
They say that with the Scourge of Zhuyin still looming, the Grand Incense Rite has to be more lavish than ever to calm people's nerves.
For instance... take the Lunarose for Haojing. Usually, we just buy standard Skylily from local farmers. But this year? They're insisting on premium stock, straight from specialist plantations.
Plantation-grown Skylily is top-tier stuff. That's going to cost us a fortune.
Precisely why the original budget fell short. Fortunately, the annual revenue has been rather healthy this year.

Overseas trade is booming, driving up tax revenue and bringing in tourists. But naturally, more visitors mean we have to splash out on the Rite to ensure it leaves a lasting impression. It's a cycle, really.
Right, right, you're making my head spin. Since the Hall of Incense is pulling out all the stops, we at the Hall of Founts can't be seen falling behind.
So — let's seize the opportunity and draft a proper plan for the Rite, shall we?
No sooner had we finished the proposal to optimise the Rite's procedures than he went and fell ill...
Now the whole affair has landed squarely in my lap. Ahh... what a spot of bother.

options.content: That's a bit dodgy, isn't it!
You look like you're in a bit of a bind.

talks.content: Well... I wouldn't go that far. His constitution has always been poor. Come to think of it, his last leave was due to a flare-up of an old ailment.
You know of the Grand Incense Rite, surely? It's the most significant event in the Huaxu calendar — it only comes around once every four years.
Now I think on it, I really ought to buy some tonic and pay him a visit soon...
The Hall of Incense proposed making this year's Rite grander than ever. The higher-ups signed off on the concept, naturally, but when it comes to the actual execution...
Since it wasn't my idea to begin with, I must admit I'm at a complete loss. I say, you're a foreign traveller, aren't you? From your perspective, what makes a festival truly engaging?
Yeah — out west, near the outskirts. Just hanging around, acting shifty. Doesn't look like a decent sort.
Did you challenge them, then? Ask what they were doing with all that gear?
If I'd done that, I wouldn't be standing here nattering to you, would I? I was up the mountain for mushrooms, head down in the dirt, when I spotted 'em lugging this massive crate into the woods.
Got me thinking, though — why drag all that kit up a mountain? Unless they're building a hideout or something?
It's odd, I'll give you that. Might just be preparations for the Grand Incense Rite, though. You never know. Best leave it to the officials. Let them sort it out.
The western outskirts again? Why is it always the western outskirts with these complaints?
I know we've got projects running out there — we even notified the locals — but the complaints just keep rolling in...
Look at this. Claims there's a racket in the middle of the night. Sounded like metal grinding on metal. But when the forest patrol went to investigate? Silence. Not a sausage.
And this one's from a restaurant runner. Reckons someone's playing a prank — ordered dozens of meals to be dumped at the western outskirts' entrance. Feeding the ghosts, I suppose?
It's all piling up, isn't it? Every incident points that way. You don't suppose there's actually something wrong out there?

options.content: Sounds like a Wishen is acting up.

talks.content: A Wishen...? Please, we deal in facts here, not fairy tales. I can't file a report based on superstition.

options.content: Why don't you go see for yourself?

talks.content: You're probably overthinking it. Then again... once you rule out the sensible options, sometimes the mad answer is the only one left.
With the Grand Incense Rite coming up? I'm swamped. If I had the time, I'd have gone days ago. I'll have to find someone else to make the trek.
If you want my opinion? It's likely just some bored merchant building an illegal villa in the hills to show off.

options.content: Why don't you go see for yourself?

talks.content: Quick — get me some tea! I've just come back from the western outskirts. I'm dying of thirst!
Here, calm down. What's brought this on? What possessed you to go tramping all the way out there?
Give me a second... Hah! I'm a wreck now. It's those endless complaints about sneaky people in the woods. The higher-ups sent me to poke around.
Ah, rings a bell. You don't think it's... the Drifters, do you?
Rubbish! Absolute tosh. If the Drifters wanted to cause trouble, they'd hit Haojing directly, wouldn't they? Burn it all down like they did last time.
Fair point. But who else in Huaxu causes trouble if not them...? So, what did you find?
The grand truth is... sweet nothing! I dragged myself up and down that mountain and saw nothing. I was convinced I'd find an illegal building site at the very least.
But no! Not even a loose roof tile! Look at me — I left looking respectable, and now I'm a sweaty, dusty wreck!
You've done your bit. Rest up. I'll pop over to the office and file the report for you.
Right, I need to massage my legs. Oof... they've gone completely dead. You'd better carry me over there first!
Right. So the shipment you were carrying went missing at the docks. Not cargo? Then what was it — Emeraldfinches!?
Aye. Hauled 'em all the way from Mistwharf. Some painter here in Haojing commissioned the lot.
No... hold on... let me process this. First of all, are you even permitted to trade Emeraldfinches? Does the Ministry of Fortune list them as a sanctioned commodity?
Oi, don't look at me. I'm just the boatman. If you officials don't know the rules, how am I supposed to?
This is... complicated. If it were simple theft, the Nine Chapters of Dafeng would have already flagged it and sent a Bi'an to investigate.
Yet the port is calm. There's been no alarm. Which implies only one thing — those birds decided to leg it themselves!
Well, what do we do? Those birds are worth a fortune! We can't just let them flutter about Haojing causing a muck, can we?
Calm down, let me think... Right! I'll alert the clerks to keep their eyes peeled. You need to help, too — grab whatever feed you used during the trip and use it as bait.
Right! Consider it done!
How on earth did the bloody things get out?
No one on board would have turned them loose. There's no profit in it — you'd gain sod all except a headache.
But to say they escaped on their own? That’s rubbish. They’re just birds. Magic or not, I doubt they suddenly grew thumbs and learnt to pick locks overnight.

Hasn't the whole of Port of Parting Stars been gossiping about this? How are you out of the loop? We shipped in from Mistwharf. A few days back, the skipper took a job hauling a flock of Emeraldfinches to Haojing.
The pay was massive. The very next day, the whole crew went out to catch the blighters. Took ages to round up the quota, shove them on board, and rattle all the way to Haojing.

Then yesterday, we finally dock, the skipper goes to register the cargo... and the Ministry of Shipping acts like we've brought in aliens. Said they'd never heard of anyone shipping Emeraldfinches and flat-out refused us entry.
So we were stuck on the boat overnight. And come morning, the cages are wide open and every last finch has done a runner!

options.content: Why on earth would anyone order Emeraldfinches?
How did they manage to escape?

talks.content: Plenty of reasons. Any one of them is enough to get us hauled before the Ministry of Fortune for a grilling. First off, Emeraldfinches aren't exactly on the approved trade list. Then again, no one's ever been daft enough to try selling them before.
It takes all sorts in Huaxu, doesn't it? We've hauled plenty of odd cargo before. You know Petit Boars?
Hah! That's exactly what I want to know! Look at the cages — vertical iron bars. There is a door, yes, but it's secured with a proper heavy latch.
Second, birds have straight guts. What goes in comes straight out. If they entered the city on full bellies, they'd be... well, plastering the streets. You can't exactly house-train them, can you?
Fatty little things, but the city nobles go mad for the meat. Emeraldfinches, though... I'll admit, this is the first time we've ever taken a contract for them.
To open it, you have to twist the bolt almost a full turn anti-clockwise, then shove the door outwards. It's not something you do by accident.
And third... neither us nor the buyer realised just how massive Haojing actually is. Not one of us had a plan for how to move the flock across the city once we got here. Absolute shambles.
There used to be a trade in their tail feathers, but that was always done out in the wilds. Nobody raises them inside city.
Do you really reckon a bird with a brain the size of a pea could figure that out? Not a chance!
And if they bought 'em for the pot... well, I've heard the meat is sour and tough as old boots. If they were any good to eat, Mistwharf wouldn't be absolutely crawling with wild ones, would it?

I can't for the life of me work out how they did it. I've heard there are folks in Khemet who can talk to beasts. If we catch the birds, maybe we should hire one to interrogate the little blighters...
They're gone... I'm done. All that work, down the drain...
Is there anything more soul-destroying than slogging away at a job you know is doomed from the start?

options.content: What's got you in such a state?

talks.content: I'm not "in a state." I'm just painfully aware of how pointless this is. Shouldn't we be putting our precious time to proper use?
Instead, we're wandering about this massive city on a wild goose chase for six missing Emeraldfinches. It's utterly farcical!

options.content: What would you consider a "proper use of time"?
But if you don't find them, you can't really report back, can you?
Well, good luck with the search!

talks.content: We've finally made it to Haojing! We ought to be strolling through the East Market, sampling the local delicacies, offering incense at the Hall of Incense, or paying respects to Lord Argent at the Hall of Adjudication!
Fair point... but this method is dreadfully inefficient. Thousands of years of Huaxu wisdom, and the best plan we can muster is "walk around and look"?

Right... thanks for the pep talk. I'll just summon a burst of enthusiasm, go gallivanting madly about the city, and return triumphantly with six birds in my arms... It'll be quite the spectacle. Don't miss it.
I rather imagined the incense wardens would use Incense Discernment to just lure the birds back effortlessly — commanding them exactly like they do the Bi'an in battle!
They've already found one? On someone's roof? How on earth did it get up there!?
What's the plan, then? That Emeraldfinch is strutting about like he owns the manor, causing a right scene...
Spare me the commentary! I can picture the disaster quite clearly. Just get the wretched thing down, will you?
I'd love to do that! But how? The moment we climb up, it squawks and legs it. We daren't get too close, or it'll vanish for good.
Don't be dense! Use bait! Chuck some fruit and veg on the ground, step back, and wait for it to come down. Simple.
We tried that trick ages ago! It comes down right enough, but the second we lunge, whoosh — straight back up it goes!
With a neck like a twig and a body that fat... it defies the laws of physics!

options.content: (You recall your past encounters with Emeraldfinches.)
(You ponder effective ways to catch birds.)

talks.content: I spent time in Mistwharf, where wild Emeraldfinches are everywhere. They never seemed frightened of me.
Back home, villagers would spread grain out to dry during harvest, and birds were always trying to nick it.
...Not frightened? You mean they don't scarper or screech when you approach?
We'd rig up a basket trap propped open with a twig. You leave a gap for the bird and put some bait underneath.
Er... fanning their tails doesn't count as being scared, does it?
Then you wait. When the bird hops under, it knocks the twig, and the basket drops right on top of it.
What's this? I've heard Loongscions have odd talents, but are you some born bird-whisperer?
Brilliant! Now you mention it, I used to do that as a lad in my village, just for a bit of sport...
No, wait! If they fan their tails for this one, maybe {性别:he|she} is actually... a peahen spirit in disguise!
I grew up in Haojing; I've never heard of such nonsense. Still, give {性别:his|her} method a go. But for a bird that fat... we're going to need a massive basket.
Rubbish! Under the Lord Argent's rule, animals are forbidden from becoming spirits!
I've got a rice hamper at home. I'll fetch it!
My point is, you're too tense. If you just act casual and walk over like I did, you might not spook them.
There's logic in that... You there! Yes, you! Chop chop! Do exactly as {性别:he|she} says!
Qianxiu Pavilion's orders are up again this year... Our embroidery's doing really well in Haojing.
But sadly, I've actually come to turn the business down. Just as we were poised to make a name for Cloudweave Valley across all of Huaxu, everything went pear-shaped.
What happened in Cloudweave Valley?

To be honest, the weather back home has been bizarre. Usually, it's lush ground, perfect for silkworms, but this year? Unrelenting heat, streams running dry, and acres of mulberry trees simply withering away.
Naturally, silk production has plummeted. Many farmers had no choice but to pack it in and find other work just to put food on the table.
With no raw silk, the seamstresses can't supply the outside world. So here I am, cap in hand, trying to negotiate my way out of contracts with the city's tailors.
Qianxiu Pavilion's orders are up again this year... Our embroidery's doing really well in Haojing.
Even if they offered a king's ransom, we simply don't have the materials. My hands are tied... Still, it's a long trek from the Valley, so I might as well stay and haggle for a couple more days.
Oh, it's you again. We've had a chinwag before, haven't we? I was going to ask if you knew any decent lodgings, but looking at you, I reckon you're not local either. Never mind.
I'm not from here, but I know the East Market is always chock-a-block with trade. You might have some luck poking around there.
Is that so? Cheers, I'll send my assistant to have a look. Truth be told, I suffer terribly from seasickness. I loathe the boat, but it's the quickest route from the Cloudweave Valley to Haojing.
Still, credit where it's due to the Hall of Craft for cutting that canal. Without it, we'd be trudging over those wretched mountain paths for a fortnight just to get out of the Valley.

options.content: Why is silkworm farming so important to the Cloudweave Valley?

talks.content: Hmm... cracking question, that. Where to start? It's chalk and cheese compared to Haojing, I tell you.
Well... I could just fob you off by saying the climate is perfect for it. But if you want the real answer, I'll have to give you a bit of a history lesson.
The canal... well, it's a canal! Sorry, stating the obvious there. Haha! But I assume you're asking about its history, not what a canal actually does?

While Haojing sits on flat plains, the Cloudweave Valley is tucked deep in the mountains. Ages ago, our ancestors fled there to escape the Filthoids. Slowly but surely, they built a proper life amongst the peaks.
Way back when — maybe a thousand years ago? Before Huaxu was united, a powerful Loongscion clan lived in our parts. Their leader was called Sang.

Because of our peculiar geography and weather, the Cloudweave Valley was prone to unpredictable floods and droughts. Even when Sang was alive, she tried everything but couldn't completely fix the flooding.
It's lovely back there, mild all year round, plenty of rain. None of these wild temperature swings you get here. I visited Haojing once in winter, and the wind cut across my face like a bloody knife.

Sang possessed magic that resonated with nature itself. After she awakened, she led her people to wipe out the Filthoids plaguing the area. Then, she used her gifts to teach the common folk how to raise silkworms.
But later, the clever folk from the Jishu Sect gave us a tip. They suggested digging a canal to divert floodwaters and irrigate the fields. So, they drew up the plans.

Even the grub's different. We like strong, bold flavours in the Cloudweave Valley. The stuff here tastes bland as water by comparison. I can stomach it for a meal or two, but after that? I'm pining for home cooking.
The silk from Sang's tribe was top-notch, famous far and wide. It wasn't long before Starweavers travelled thousands of miles to buy it, bringing news of the Nine Chapters of Dafeng with them.
You know the rest. It cost a fortune, but with those massive Mechapuppets from the Jishu Sect, we overcame every hurdle. It was quite the legendary feat back in the day.
I could rabbit on all day, but you really need to see it for yourself. If you get the chance, travel around Huaxu a bit more.
Later, Sang became one of the first Loongscions to enter the Nine Chapters. With help from the Hall of Craft, we dug the canal, linking us closer to Haojing.

Even though the Jishu Sect isn't what it used to be, they're still deeply respected in the Cloudweave Valley. Coming to Haojing this time, I actually thought to myself that the capital looks a bit backward compared to home!
Naturally, the silk trade stuck. Other places in Huaxu produce silk nowadays, of course, but since we had a head start, our weavers are still the best in the business.
Only three per cent loss on this fruit shipment? Good. Very good.

We simply must secure that Loongscion with the freezing magic, whatever her price. Ah, but she isn't a local, is she? I suppose I'll need to sort out a residency permit before I can make her a proper offer.
Hmm... You've been eyeing me for a fair while, haven't you? What's your business? I'm a trader from Southpeak, not a local of Haojing, so I'm afraid I'll be useless if you're after directions.
Southpeak... ah, that's a world away. It's an island south of Huaxu, named for the colossal mountain that dominates the landscape.

It belongs to Huaxu, technically, but we're so remote we barely see the mainlanders. It's too sweltering there to grow incense, so to maintain the Nine Chapters of Dafeng, we're forced to import our stock from Haojing.
In exchange, we ship Southpeak specialties up to Haojing. The logistics are a nightmare, mind you. We usually need the Loongscions and their magic just to keep the goods intact.
Mostly provisions — food, drink — and some local handicrafts. Nothing extravagant, really. Just enough to offset our travel costs, with any luck.
The most precious cargo... that would be the Honeyfruits we've hauled in. The spoilage rate is dreadful, I'm afraid, which forces us to charge a premium.

options.content: Then how do you transport it?

talks.content: It's Southpeak's claim to fame. Back home, they grow wild across the hills. They're incredibly juicy and sweet. Quite the crowd-pleaser, actually.
The masters at the Hall of Craft designed us a special double-layered jar made of "ice porcelain". We pop the fruit in the inner chamber the moment it's picked, then pack the outer shell with ice.

But they're fiddly things. From ripening to falling takes a mere ten days. And once picked? It's a headache — they lose their flavour within twenty-four hours. That's why you rarely see them this far north.

options.content: Why not just grow the trees in Haojing?
What does the Hall of Craft have to do with it?
Why keep shipping it if the losses are so high?

talks.content: We load them onto the fastest Starweaver ships and race here. Even at top speed, we lose half the shipment before reaching Haojing, so we always have to pack double.

options.content: Why not just grow the trees in Haojing?
What does the Hall of Craft have to do with it?
Why keep shipping it if the losses are so high?

talks.content: We tried that, actually. The odd thing is, Honeyfruit is stubborn. It demands Southpeak soil. Even if you match the climate perfectly elsewhere, it simply refuses to fruit.
Decades ago, we had no way to ship it. The whole idea actually came from a Hall of Craft master who was helping build infrastructure on Southpeak.
Simple supply and demand. Besides, it'd be a shame to keep such a treat stuck on Southpeak. We want folks across Huaxu to enjoy it too.
He developed quite a taste for the fruit during his stay. He couldn't stop thinking about it even back in Haojing, so he returned to Southpeak just to solve the shipping problem.
Plus, we're up to our necks in the stuff back home. We're all sick of eating it! Swapping it for spices here in Haojing suits us perfectly.
This run was different, mind you. A Loongscion from the Republic of Luca joined our caravan. She's got a knack for ice magic, and thanks to her, we saved nearly the whole batch!
Pity she's only passing through. I'd love to keep her on the books permanently. Do you reckon she'd stay if I offered a heftier wage?
Everyone's had a gutful of Lord Taihao's patterns by now. Absolutely sod all creativity left in them.
Year in, year out, it's the same old tat — flowers, birds, bugs. No taste whatsoever. Dreadfully dull, you know?

options.content: Hello, I’m curious about what you were saying, you know?

talks.content: What do you think? The vase designs, you know? Hang on... are you copying how I talk??

options.content: I wouldn't dream of it, you know?

talks.content: You definitely are! Every time I visit Haojing, I bump into the most tiresome people. Either those dim-witted Wardens at the Hall of Incense, or some daft person in white mocking how I speak, you know?

options.content: Do you have a grievance with the Hall of Incense?

talks.content: That's better. I'm not actually cross, mind you. You're a sight better than those thick-headed incense wardens, you know?

options.content: Do you have a grievance with the Hall of Incense?

talks.content: Heavens no! I'm just lamenting how tragically dense they are every single year, you know?
I'm a porcelain merchant from Lotus Wharf. The Hall of Incense commissions a batch of jars annually for their incense. Usually, clients pick their own designs, you see?
Regulars usually like a bit of flair, something fresh. But the Hall? Same patterns, every time. Lord Taihao or the usual garden variety rubbish. It's a utter bore!
That's why I say they're a bit slow. I know the rule is "take the money and don't ask questions," but... you know, churning out the exact same thing? It's soul-destroying work.

options.content: Perhaps the patterns hold specific meanings.

talks.content: If the jars are for incense, maybe the patterns correspond to different varieties?
Why not try something fresh? How about painting a Lunarian on the jars?
Eh? You might actually have a point there... Is that why they haven't changed the designs in over a decade?
Oh? Brilliant idea! Lunarians are tiny and precious. They'd look absolutely lovely on a vase, you know?
Changing them constantly would confuse new recruits. Consistency probably makes inventory management much easier.
But I reckon I'll have to try that on my own time... You know, the Hall will just ask for the same old tat anyway.
Alright, point taken! I suppose I can accept that logic. I'll stop calling them sticks-in-the-mud from now on.
And here we are — Haojing at last! This is the busiest, most vibrant part of Huaxu!
Keep your valuables close, folks. Too heavy to lug around? Just pop your bags at the drop-off point and our porters will whisk them straight to your inns.
You are currently standing in the beating heart of the city: Port of Parting Stars. Hundreds of ships dock here daily, many sailing all the way from Cloudweave Valley, just like us.
Right, stick together! We're marching straight to the western market for a spot of lunch. It's been a long trek, and even if you aren't peckish, my stomach is growling something fierce!
This way, everyone! Keep your eyes on my red flag so nobody goes wandering off!
Eh? Which group are you with? You don't look like one of mine. Best scurry back to your own squad before your guide has a panic attack looking for you.
399!? Three days and two nights in Haojing, full board, plus return boat fare — the whole package for 399!?
Shush! Keep it down! You know the guide said not to discuss fees. I didn't buy it either at first, but that young lass swore down she wasn't having us on.
And I thought, surely she wouldn't dare lie after that? The Nine Chapters of Dafeng aren't just for show. Any funny business in Huaxu, and you've got Bi'an to answer to.
I suppose you're right. This is Haojing. Even crooks wouldn't be bold enough to pull a stunt right under Agent Loong's nose.
Exactly, so I signed up. It's not exactly a fortune, is it? Besides, the guide's been lovely. When folks got seasick, she was rushing about with tea and water — worked herself to the bone.
Sometimes I think... a young thing working that hard for peanuts? Even if she drags us to a souvenir shop, I wouldn't mind buying a trinket just to help her out.
Don't be a soft touch! Next thing you know, you've spent your pension on some dodgy tonic that makes you ill. It's not worth the risk.
Alright, alright, I'm old, not daft. I know you're only looking out for me. Don't worry, I'll keep my wits about me.
Cor, Haojing's huge! Makes my place back home look tiny.

Was worth sitting on that boat for donkeys' years, I suppose. What was that fancy saying the teacher taught me? Aye... "A journey well rewarded!" Och, remembering all those books is a right pain in the backside!
What are you gawping at? Never seen a hero from Cloudweave Valley before? I ken what it is — you're stunned by my massive charisma, eh? Just admit it!
(This lad's attitude feels oddly familiar... though you've never heard an accent quite like this before.)
Cat got your tongue? Are you mute or something? Oh ho! Oh ho! Not a peep out of you. Are you deaf, maybe?

options.content: You just remind me of a friend of mine.
I just think your accent is unique.

talks.content: Oho! So you can talk! I look like your pal, do I? What sort of pal is that then? Mind you, I'm a proper handsome devil, so your friend probably can't hold a candle to me!
Unique? Well, next to those posh Haojing folk, I reckon I do sound a bit different, don't I? But I'm from Cloudweave Valley, y'know. That's just how we talk back home.
You don't look like a local yourself, though! Which little nook or cranny did you crawl out from?

options.content: I'm from Purgatorio Island, a small island in the south.
I'm just a hero passing through.

talks.content: Purgatorio Island? Never heard of it! Doesn't sound like a proper Huaxu city at all. You must be a foreigner! Turns out we're in the same boat then, both just here for a lark in Haojing!
Oho! Listen to you, talking big! Well, going by your getup, you're definitely not from round here.
I was going to ask you where the good scran and fun spots are, but there's no point asking you now! I'll rest my legs a wee bit, then head into town for a wander. If fate allows, catch you later!
See you around.
I'll take the fire pump cart with me for now. Some bloody idiot thought it was a wooden barrel and poured sesame oil into it. Now the rats have got into it, and it's a right mess.
Understood, Master. But... when might we expect it back? I'm worried that...
Won't be long. I'll forge you an iron one this time — solid as a rock. It'll last you donkey's years without a hitch.

options.content: What's this pump cart you're talking about?

talks.content: You mean the fire pump cart? It's just the machine we wheel out to douse the flames when a house catches alight.
Never heard of it? There's a nursery rhyme we have in Huaxu: A barrel wide and deep, with handles curved and steep. Three lads to heave and run, extinguishing fires one by one.
That's describing our fire pump cart, plain and simple.

options.content: That... didn't really clear things up.
How does it actually work, then?

talks.content: Oh, it's dead simple. Fill the barrel with water, then two blokes grab the crossbeam and pump it up and down, like pounding rice cakes. That drives the copper pistons inside.
Then someone else grabs the hose, points it at the blaze, and whoosh! Water sprays out like a dragon's breath, and out goes the fire.
Sounds a bit fiddly just explaining it without the kit here. Tell you what — if you're keen, pop by the Hall of Craft sometime and I'll give you a proper demonstration!

options.content: Has Huaxu always used these things?
Couldn't you just use... magic or something?

talks.content: Not always. If it's a small fire, a bucket of water each does the trick. But for proper blazes where the smoke's choking you, we used to fill bladders with water and fire them out of cannons.

Hark at you, talking like a privileged Loongscion with your head in the clouds. Where are we supposed to find a powerful Loongscion just hanging about whenever a spark flies? Fires claim lives in an instant, mate.
Powerful stuff, mind you, but blasting water bags everywhere was a bit wasteful. That's why we came up with the fire pump cart. Works a treat, that does.
Better we rely on elbow grease and teamwork. Why bother with magic when good honest mechanics can solve the problem?
You sound just like those incense wardens at the Hall of Incense. Next, you'll be suggesting we set up an altar and pray for Argent Loong to send rain every time someone burns their toast.

options.content: You seem to have a bone to pick with the Hall of Incense.

talks.content: Oi! You trying to stir the pot? I've got no problem with them. It's just that some of them have heads made of solid teak — couldn't think outside the box to save their lives.
I don't like stiff-necked people, doesn't mean I hate 'em. Don't you go snitching to the incense wardens now! And you, the quiet one over there, keep your mouth shut too!
Er... haha... I didn't hear a thing, honest!
Have the lads from the Hall of Craft been round to collect the fire pump carts? I do hate putting them to so much trouble.
They have. Shall I release the standard maintenance budget, same as usual?
Not quite. We've had a bit of a... situation. An oil merchant arrived with split barrels, you see, and we had to loan him a pump as an emergency container.
The trouble is, nobody kept an eye on things. It completely slipped our minds... and as for the pump...
Ah... say no more. The warehouse rats can be absolute terrors...
Quite right. Anyway, when you're back at the Ministry of Fortune, put in for extra funding. Tell the Hall of Craft to forge us a custom batch in iron or copper this time.
Why do the Hall of Craft lot keep going back and forth to the Port of Parting Stars? Don't they ever get tired of it?
Don't say that! If they didn't service the equipment and a fire actually broke out, it'd be a disaster. Lives are at stake!
You always say that, but nothing ever actually happens, does it?
That's how it always goes. Everyone thinks they're safe right until the moment they aren't. One slip-up is all it takes. Have you forgotten what happened years ago...?

options.content: What are you two talking about?

talks.content: You little rascal. Were you earwigging on us?

options.content: Just thought I'd join the chat.

talks.content: Hahaha! You're a funny one. Alright then, Dong, spill the beans. I don't know the full story myself, just scraps of gossip over tea.
It's no secret, though I can't promise my version is gospel. You know how stories grow legs as they travel — a molehill becomes a mountain soon enough!
Stop waffling and get on with it!
It was years back... maybe four or five? On a pitch-black, windy night... a watchman walked the silent, empty streets of Port of Parting Stars, clutching a lone oil lamp.
He was shouting the warning — Dry air, be careful with fire! — weaving through the alleys like a wandering spirit in the gloom.

options.content: Since when do wandering spirits shout warnings?

talks.content: Oh, they do. Some Wishen just wail endlessly: I died so horribly... oh, the misery...
Hey! Port of Parting Stars only has a few warehouses. What's all this about "alleys"?
No, wait, you've made me lose my thread! Do you want to hear the rest of it or not?
Tsk... that was the old days. Back then, the port was so packed with warehouses you could barely breathe.
Just get on with it! We won't interrupt again, alright?
Ahem. So, the watchman was walking through these pitch-black lanes. Just as he thought the coast was clear and turned to head back... suddenly!
Something splashed onto his ankle. He yelped. It was scalding hot! He lowered his lamp to the ground and saw a nasty burn on his skin, but not a clue what caused it.
Seeing the mark made the pain kick in properly. He dropped to the floor, clutching his foot and howling.
Just then, a laugh echoed from nowhere. He followed the sound and looked up. There, on a roof bathed in moonlight, sat a pale child in crimson robes, hair in a topknot, giggling down at him.
Terrified, he stammered: Little one, why aren't you home in bed? Why sit on the roof? Why do you laugh so?
The child didn't answer, just kept laughing. The sound grew more chilling in the empty night, and the watchman wanted nothing more than to leg it. Finally, the child spoke:
The watchman is not a man, but a lamp. The arsonist is not the lamp, but the oil.
With that, the child stood up, dusted off his bottom, and jumped straight off the roof! In the blink of an eye, the child'd vanished into thin air.
That's when the watchman realised. The moonlight was bright enough to cast sharp shadows for everything in sight, but...
But what?! Stop pausing for effect, you're doing my head in!
The child cast no shadow!
Waaah!!!
Heheh, scared you, didn't I? Mind you, that's just a rumour I heard. All I know is that a massive fire broke out a few days later. And the rest... well, you know the history.
Load of old cobblers. Sounds to me like the watchman fell asleep on the job and made up a ghost story to cover his own backside!

Just take it as a bit of fun, don't get your knickers in a twist. Anyway, no one died, but we lost a fortune in cargo. That's why the Ministry of Fortune set up the Ministry of Shipping to strictly manage fire safety here.
So stop whinging about the masters from the Hall of Craft. If they don't mind coming here every day to keep us safe, you shouldn't be complaining either.
Alright, alright! I was just having a moan. You think I don't know what's good for us?
Hmph. As long as you know. Right, that's enough chatting. A quick breather, then it's back to work.
Ripple-Step! Watch me soar! I'll ride the clouds! Swift as a goose flying south, light as a dragonfly skimming the pond! Whoosh! Hah!
(The boy faces the water, winding up his arms like a windmill. He looks ready to take a flying leap...)
Don't jump! You'll hurt yourself!
(You wait for a good while. Despite all the shouting and dramatic posing, his feet remain firmly planted on the ground.)
Eh? What? You talking to me?
Are you actually going to jump?
I don't see anyone else around...
I wasn't planning on jumping in.
Then why are you... flailing about like that?
I'm practising the Ripple-Step! That chant I was doing? A master from the Magistrates of Yingtian taught me. Said if I memorise the words and train hard enough, I'll be running on water in no time!

options.content: What did this "master from the Magistrate of Yingtian" look like?
I haven't got time for this.

talks.content: It's a secret art to make you weightless! You can sprint hundreds of metres across the surface without sinking. Won't even get your boots wet. Brilliant, innit?

options.content: Why do you want to learn it?
I actually know a similar trick.

talks.content: Let's see... tall bloke, with a white patch in his hair. Oh! And a star-shaped scar right under his eye. He looked proper brilliant!
You've put me right off my stride! I bet my skills have gone rusty just talking to you!

Because it's wicked! If I learn the Ripple-Step, I won't need a boat to get to the East Market. That miserable old ticket seller won't let me on anyway — my mum told him she'd give him an earful if he sold me a ticket!
I have a unique travel technique. If I fire a gun while gliding, the recoil slows my descent, letting me fly much further.
(Why does that description sound so familiar...?)

options.content: What exactly did he tell you?

talks.content: Once I've mastered it, I won't need his rubbish ferry. I'll just dash straight across the waves! Just wait 'til Mian and Da Li see my heroic form. They'll be swooning all over the place!
What?! You can really do that? Wait, that's no good. Guns are strictly banned in Huaxu!
I told him that miserable old sod at the port wouldn't sell me a ticket to the East Market, so I couldn't go play with my mates.
Only dangerous criminals carry guns and knives around here. You... you aren't one of those scary types, are you?
Then he told me about this secret art for flying right over the water! I begged him to teach me, so he gave me a special chant and told me to practise here every single day.
Nah, you don't look the sort. Proper villains wouldn't waste time chatting with a kid like me. They'd all be Drifters, off plotting something nasty!

options.content: Drifters aren't all bad, you know.

talks.content: He said eventually, I'd feel a rush of power surge from my guts right up to my throat. Once I feel that, I just have to jump, and I'll master it!
Stop fibbing! My mum says Drifters are wicked monsters. She reckons if I don't behave, she'll whistle for one to come and bag me!
Only... nothing's happened yet. Blimey, maybe Mum's right. Do you reckon I can't do it because I haven't read enough books?

options.content: I think that "Magistrate of Yingtian" was having you on.
Your mum is right. Go home and study.

talks.content: No way! I saw it with my own eyes! He was amazing! He stepped on his left foot with his right and jumped again in mid-air! He even spun around whilst he was up there!

options.content: I haven't got time for this.

talks.content: Ugh! I only started learning the Ripple-Step to get out of studying! How've I ended up back where I started?

options.content: I haven't got time for this.

talks.content: Soon as it gets hot and the tide comes in, the parts sitting in the water get coated in algae. Then it's a struggle just to get the thing turning.
Same every year. They send us down to scrape it off, and my poor old back pays the price... No rest for the wicked, eh?
De-mossing the big lug. You can't see from up there, but under the axle, the green stuff's worked its way right into the cracks. Water alone won't shift that muck.
This old thing? No fancy name for it. It just powers the bone grinders over at the Hall of Incense. Most of us just call it the Big Waterwheel.
Needs a proper seeing to with a wire brush, followed by a lye wash. Otherwise, the blooming stuff just grows straight back.

options.content: Is it safe to leave it in the water all year?

talks.content: When it's running, grinding spices takes half the effort. Saves a massive amount of legwork, it does.
It's old pine, tough as boots. The only danger is if the moss wraps round and traps the damp. That's when the rot sets in.
The Hall of Craft built it here to catch the strong current. But lately — bad water, maybe — the moss has been growing wild. Slows down the incense belts something fierce.
So clearing the moss doesn't just keep it spinning; it lets the wood breathe so we can squeeze a few more years out of it!
So here we are, giving the old thing a scrub-down to get the green off its back!

options.content: Is it safe to leave it in the water all year?

talks.content: I'll just finish this section, then I'm off to the Ministry of Shipping to beg for a bowl of herbal tea. I'm absolutely knackered!
If they hadn't stopped the waterwheel, we wouldn't be dealing with this mess.
Don't be daft. You surely don't think the moss only grows because the wheel stops turning?
It's common sense! If it keeps spinning, the water smacks against the blades and washes the slime right off before it can stick.
There's no need to shut it down every five minutes just so some poor sod can spend half the day scrubbing away at it.
Fair point, perhaps. But what about the underwater supports? How does the current clean the moss off those?
