Well... if the wheel turns... that means the water is moving! And everyone knows moving water... err...
Oh, give over. Port of Parting Stars's water comes from Jiaolan Village, full of algae. Once that muck latches onto the wood, moss is inevitable.
Keeping it spinning might slow the rot a bit, but it won't stop it for good.
Tsk... Alright, give it a rest! Ever since you spent five minutes at the Hall of Craft, you think you can lecture the rest of us!
Hey... I was only trying to explain the facts, not lecture you... Oi! Don't cover your ears! Are you even listening? Hello?
Remember these three virtues: respect the law, uphold fairness, and practise diligence.
You don't possess the look of a Huaxu local, my young friend. A traveller from distant shores, perhaps?

options.content: Do you work here at the port?

talks.content: Indeed. I've served the Ministry of Shipping for three years now. My days are spent tallying the vessels entering Port of Parting Stars, monitoring their cargo, and calculating the tax revenues.
Naturally, I couldn't manage such a feat alone. It takes thousands of us working in concert to keep this port running like clockwork. Quite the operation, wouldn't you say?

options.content: How many ships pass through Port of Parting Stars in a year?

talks.content: Ah, well... precise figures are likely locked away in the Ministry of Fortune archives. But, reckoning by my three years on the dock, I'd wager...
In a full year? Over three hundred, certainly. Most ships docking in Haojing are domestic traders. The foreign merchant vessels tend to berth over at Mistwharf.
Leaving us so soon?
Every night, well past midnight, the ships come in. Dockhands shouting, chains clanking, crates scraping along... It's so loud I can't get a wink of sleep!
I'm a light sleeper as it is! When I lived in Mistwharf, my neighbour merely coming home late was enough to ruin my night, leaving me a groggy wreck the next day.
I thought moving to Haojing, thinking a proper, sprawling city would grant me some peace. But what happens? The roar of those massive ships barges straight into my bedchamber!
I was lying in bed, and I swear on my life, the sheer vibration nearly launched me into the ceiling!
Er... please, sir, calm yourself. Night ships must catch the tide; the tide waits for no man, hence the late arrivals. We never meant to disturb you. How long does this din usually last?
Two hours at best, four or five at worst! It's infernal!
This is a grave oversight on our part. We prioritised trade efficiency and completely neglected the peace of our residents.
Rest assured, I shall summon the relevant parties today. We will present a sensible solution within the week.
No, wait! We shall issue an order immediately. All ships docking at night are strictly forbidden from shouting. We'll refine the regulations further after consultation. How does that sound?

Good! Splendid! That's Haojing administration for you — far more sensible than those backwater officials. I'm a playwright, you know. I shall immortalise your efficiency in my next script. You'll be famous across the seas!
Boat rides! Ten coins a trip! Tickets here — line up! Once the boat's full, we're off!
Morning! Fancy a trip over to the East Market, do you?
(The ferry carries you across to the East Market.)
Sharp eyes on you! Just come from the East Market, have you? That'd be my older brother, Liu Fu, selling tickets on that side. Met him already?
I see... let me guess, is there a third brother named...
Spot on! Our brother Liu Shou is the very boatman punting the raft for you today!
Fu, Lu, and Shou... symbols of Fortune, Prosperity, and Longevity. Hah...
Boat rides! Ten coins a trip! Tickets here — line up! Once the boat's full, we're off!
Morning! Fancy a trip over to the East Market, do you?
Ah, a regular! No waiting about for you then. Hop on, we're off! Do say hello to my brother when you arrive!
See you around, then!
(The ferry carries you across to the East Market.)
J—Just a moment... let me check this guide to Huaxu greetings I just bought.
Ahem. Greetings, my... fiend. I am a bumble stranger, newly diseased upon this soil. Being a stranger to this... sewer, might I inquire as to the location of the bog... ah, no, the Chamber of Rain?

options.content: What on earth are you saying?

talks.content: You don't understand? What sort of rubbish lexicon is this... it swore this was the King's Language of Huaxu!

Did I mispronounce it? Hold on, let me turn the page... Right then. Greetings, my... liver-long companion? I am a scrot... no, sojourner... in Huaxu, unfamiliar with the terrain. Pray tell, where lies the Chamber of Rain?

options.content: You're asking for the loo, aren't you?

talks.content: "Could you" corresponds to... "Art thou", and "normally" is... eh? Wait. You aren't a local? You actually understand me?
Yes! Exactly! The loo! Hello? Wait... so you do understand me? You aren't a local?
Do I look like a local to you?
Oh, thank heavens! Finally, someone who speaks my language! I hired a translator, you see, but he claimed to have a "tummy ache," told me to wait, and promptly scarpered.
It's been half an hour and not a peep. I didn't dare wander off alone, but I can't just stand here like a lemon forever!
I thought about hunting him down myself. But since I haven't the foggiest how locals speak, I bought this... look!
(The yellowed title page reads in neat script: The Grand Compendium of Huaxu Salutations.)
A paperboy near the square. Said he'd give me a "foreigner's discount." Only fifty copper!
Claimed that with this book, any chap clueless about the language could pass for a scholar! Just a simple matter of cross-referencing, he said.

options.content: The other problem is, you weren't even reading it right.

talks.content: Outdated? You mean people in Huaxu don't speak like this anymore?
Not reading it right? What do you mean? Was my intonation off?
That looks like a guide to Ancient Huaxu dialect. People speak much more casually now. If you just chat to a few locals, you'll hear the difference.
I'm no expert, but you said "liver-long companion" when it should be "lifelong," and "newly diseased" instead of "descended."
I shall! You enjoy yourself too, assuming you're here for leisure like myself...
Ah! Is that so? Oh dear, I've made a right mess of it... So, I didn't actually need a translator? Everyone speaks quite normally?
More or less... yes.
Thank you kindly, {性别:sir|madam}. When I return home, I must tell the family about Huaxu. Safe, beautiful, and accommodating.
According to my little book here, it was... "A trip not in vain!" Did I get that one right?
Evenin', Auntie. Had something nice for dinner? Just out for a wander to work off the dinner?
My girl's back, so her dad insisted on trying his hand in the kitchen. Absolute disaster, it was — inedible. I had to whip up a whole new spread just so we didn't starve.
Oh! Mai's back, is she? How come she isn't keeping you company, then?
Her cousin's dragged her off somewhere to run riot. Those two were thick as thieves growing up, and having not seen each other for years... well, they're over the moon.
I have to say, Auntie, you've got a heart of stone sending such a young lass abroad. All on her own out there... I'd be worried sick she wasn't eating properly or wrapping up warm.
It was her idea. Said she simply had to go to the Republic of Luca to study drama — better atmosphere, or some such... She's a grown woman now. We could afford it, so we let her get on with it.
Ooh... studying out there must cost a pretty penny, eh? Sets you back a fair bit each year, I imagine?
Mai's got her head screwed on. Top marks, so the college waived her fees. She earns a bit on the side, too. Besides, the old man and I don't spend much, so we manage alright.

Good for you. The kids are all grown up and scattered to the winds now. My own is due back in a couple of days for the Grand Incense Rite... Shall we book a table at the Bazhen Pavilion for a proper catch-up?
Sounds lovely!
One, two, three... Where's Tiezhu? Why isn't he here? Did you see him on the way?
(Sniffs loudly) N-no... haven't seen hide nor hair of him since I left the house.
Snotty, I told you ages ago! You've got to physically drag Tiezhu out, or he'll never budge from his room!
Scamp, you... easy for you to say! Look at the size of him, then look at me... (Sniffs) You try dragging him!
Alright, pack it in, you two. We can still play with four, can't we? It's hardly the end of the world.
No! We agreed on five, so five it shall be! Attention! Commander Snotty!
Sir! (Sniffs)
Double time back home and commandeer a long, thin bamboo pole!
What do we need that for?
Lieutenant Scamp!
Sir!
Head to the East Market. Requisition a flower cart from Scent of Spring! Bring it here!
General, you aren't thinking of...
Of course! Lady Jade, stand down. We'll rendezvous here, march on Tiezhu's house, poke his window open, and let the sun roast his lazy backside!

"Where incense hangs on the air, Lord Argent descends; on the eve of the Rite, the forecourt is awash with light." In honour of the Rite, we present a special event: the Lantern Riddle Fair. Do come and enjoy it.
You've the look of a traveller about you, not a local. Visiting Haojing, are we? Fancy a crack at our Lantern Riddle Fair while you're here?
Truth be told, it's much like any other riddle fair. But with the Grand Incense Rite upon us, the city is absolutely heaving with returning wanderers and guests.
But of course. We've prepared a few trinkets. Nothing too lavish, mind you, but a sincere token of our thanks all the same.
Rest easy, we thought of that. The riddles aren't overly obscure; anyone with a passing knowledge of Huaxu culture should manage just fine.

options.content: That's all I needed to know.

talks.content: We've set up festivities in the West Market and the square by the Hall of Adjudication to mark the occasion. The riddles are just one way for us all to share in the joy. Lovely, isn't it?
Then I wish you a grand old time at the fair!
I... I have no words. The sheer magnificence of it all moves me to tears.
Have you come to pay respects to Lord Argent as well? Just look at this vast square, the Hall of Adjudication piercing the clouds... It is all so sublime, so monumental. It is just like...
I have journeyed across miles of mountains and rivers just to stand here in Haojing, hoping for a single glimpse of Lord Taihao. How can I possibly describe the feeling burning in my chest?
The Hall of Adjudication means everything to me! I spent a full year working and studying, scrimping and saving every coin just to afford the journey.
And today, right here, my dream has finally come true! Look at this splendid square, this wide, open road... surely it is a sign that my future is just as bright?

options.content: Why does the Hall mean so much to you?

talks.content: I was raised on stories of the Hall of Adjudication. My granny always told me that if I studied diligently, the Loong Lord would welcome me here one day.
To become a High Chancellor of Loongyuan, the best of the best, envied by all of Huaxu... to serve the realm and its people!
But I was young and foolish. I didn't understand why she pushed me; I only cared about playing. She always said she wanted to see me make something of myself, but she...
She never got the chance. She passed away when I was ten.
Since then, I swore an oath. Even if I never become High Chancellor, I had to come and see the Hall of Adjudication. I had to tell my gran in the spirit world that I'm sorry for letting her down.

options.content: You're a devoted grandson. Don't be so hard on yourself.
She didn't need you to be famous. She just wanted you to be happy.

talks.content: Thank you, but it is a bit late for that now. Still, at least making it here fulfils one of my oldest wishes.
Deep down, I know that. I am simply angry at myself for not giving her a better life while she was still here to enjoy it.
Even now, I had to save for ages just to visit. It is not as if I can actually afford to settle in Haojing.
What d'you mean I can't go in? I'll buy a ticket! No? So how do I get in, then? I want to see Lord Argent.
Sorry. The Hall of Adjudication is strictly no entry for the general public.
You've got it backwards. I'm not "general public." I'm a citizen of Huaxu, living under their protection! That makes me one of the family, doesn't it?
Look, mate, I'm really sorry... but I cannot let you through.
I came all the way to Haojing just to see Lord Argent. Let me have a quick look, go on. I promise I'll keep my hands to myself.
It's just not possible... Sigh, what am I supposed to do? He won't budge...
We appreciate your devotion to Argent Loong, but the Hall of Adjudication has rules. Only cases of the utmost gravity are heard within these walls.
Besides, the Loong Lord is burdened with endless duties. Even if you forced your way in, you'd be unlikely to find them.
If you truly possess talent, why not stand for High Chancellor of Loongyuan? You'd be invited inside to sit the exam, and could see the Lord properly then.
If I had that sort of talent, I wouldn't be wasting my breath here, would I? I just want a look! I've lugged this camera all the way from Hyperborea. One photo, and I'm off!
You see? There's no reasoning with him...
Sigh... We get a few of these fanatics every year...
Look! If your heart is truly devout, you need only gaze up at the Hall of Adjudication to see Lord Argent soaring through the clouds.
Mum, my eyes are stinging from staring so hard... why haven't I seen the Loong Lord yet?
When your devotion is pure enough, the Loong Lord will emerge.
Hmm... Excuse me! You there, can you see Lord Argent up there?
Wow! Really? Please, you have to tell me what Lord Argent looks like!
Is it because you aren't devout enough either?
Think of a long, winding body covered in scales, with two great horns on its head. Quite similar to the Loongscions, actually.
Lord Argent looks just like us — two eyes, a nose — but with sharp dragon horns crowning his head.
I'm not from Huaxu, so it's only natural that I lack the devotion.
Hmm... so he's exactly like the paintings? Mum, I told you the artists must have seen the Lord! They must have painted him from life!
Wow! So he really is different from the pictures! But how does he fly, then? Does he step on a cloud? Or does he just go whoosh — and vanish into the sky?
Oh, I see! Well, welcome to Huaxu all the same!
She's just a child with a wild imagination. Please, pay her no mind.
Thank you.
Not at all.
You gently pat her on the head.
Right then, let's head to the East Market. Mum will buy you some tanghulu skewers.
Morning paper! Morning paper! Fresh off the press! Haojing exclusives — spicy stuff, and all true!
Fancy a read? Fresh off the Hall of Craft's finest presses. Crisp text, sharp pictures, and stories polished by our cleverest scholars. Guaranteed to entertain!

options.content: What's in the morning paper today?
Aren't you a bit young to be working?

talks.content: Me? I'm a newsboy, obviously! From Lord Argent’s decrees to the neighbours' squabbles, there ain't a thing us paper lads don't know!
You're putting me in a spot! I know you're itching to hear the gossip, but I've got a living to earn. If I spill the beans for free, who's going to buy my papers?
It ain't really work, I'm just helping my dad. He's inside running the press. He promised if I shift ten copies, I get a stick of tanghulu skewer!
But here's the rub: all the juicy gossip we dig up is hidden inside these pages. So if you're curious...
Tell you what... I'll give you the headlines. Just a teaser, yeah?
Look, see this token? I've sold six already. Plus, I managed to flog a dusty old Grand Compendium of Huaxu Salutations to some clueless tourist! That counts as three papers!
(Buy a copy of the morning paper?)

Let's have a look... Today's big scoop... Blimey! "East Market: Floodwater Half-Drowns a Lord Argent Statue!" Then there's "Sixty-Two-Year-Old Widow Gives Birth" and "West Market Oddity: A Dog That Hunts Rats!"
Heh heh, so how about it? Want to contribute to my tanghulu skewer fund?
(Obtain a newspaper.)
All that talk for nothing! Ah well, never mind!
Right you are! Here's today's edition, hot off the press!
At first glance, these characters look a lot like the ones back home in Hyperborea. So why can't I make head nor tail of it once they're put together?
Excuse me, {性别:sir|madam}. I hope I'm not intruding, but could you spare a moment to help a traveller out?
You see, I'm a merchant from the Hyperborean Empire. My business in Haojing is concluded, but with my ship delayed, I've got a few days to kill in the city.
A paperboy flogged this journal to me, claiming it lists the town's finest attractions. Trouble is, I've been staring at it for an age and can't make sense of a single Huaxu character.
Another subject of the Empire! All glory to our Emperor! Though I must admit, your attire threw me... I took it for some niche local fashion.
Well, if you're one of us, I doubt you'll have much luck with this script either. Ah, never mind. I'll just have a wander and see where I end up.

options.content: Let me have a look, though I can't promise anything.

talks.content: (You take the paper from his hands and study it closely.)
(It's a wall of text with absolutely no illustrations. The dense, cramped characters are completely baffling!)
(My only option is to...)

options.content: I'm afraid I can't read it either.

talks.content: Oh dear... well, that puts us in the same boat. No matter, I suppose I'll just have a wander on my own.
It says here the West Market is hosting a temple fair. Apparently, the food stalls are excellent.
And over in the East Market, the shops are running promotions to celebrate the Grand Incense Rite.
There's a lantern riddle game in the central square, too. But the main event is definitely the Grand Incense Rite. It's the most famous spectacle in Huaxu. You simply mustn't miss it!
Oh! Does it really say all that? Thank you! I shall head over immediately and see what all the fuss is about!
Don't mention it!
Hear me out. When you go somewhere, the food and sights come second. It's the atmosphere that matters. You've got to get a feel for the place. Right?
We're just a bunch of old fogeys who can't sit still. Spent our youth rushing about, so now we volunteer here outside the Hall of Adjudication, teaching you youngsters a bit of Huaxu history.
It don't cost a coin, mind! Put your wallet away. We aren't flogging anything; we were just gathering dust at home and needed a spot of sun.
Oh, thank heavens! Oho! Another curious soul asking about Haojing history. Luo, you're up! Get over here!
That's Qian's specialist subject! Oi, Qian! Get yourself over here, we've got a live one asking about culture!
You're wondering what we're doing? Oh, we're just a few old souls with time on our hands, happy to answer any questions passers-by might have.
Right then, the tale of Haojing. You've asked the right man! Thousands of years back, there wasn't a "Haojing" to speak of — just a tiny settlement led by our ancestor, Yang.
Alright, keep your hair on. I'm coming! Well hello, love. You've certainly come to the right person for that.
We kept hearing visitors moaning, "Oh, Haojing's nothing special," or "It's dull as dishwater, just like everywhere else."
Back then, Huaxu was plagued Filthoids, folks were scattered to the winds, and everyone was scrambling for scraps. There wasn't a moment's peace.
Now, I'm not one for fancy definitions, but my girl — she's studying abroad, you know — she reckons "culture" is just the bits that make us special. The things you won't find anywhere else.
Well, that got our backs up, I can tell you! How can they judge the place without properly looking around? Haojing isn't a playground. It's the greatest living history book in all of Huaxu!
Thankfully, our great ancestor Yang awakened his art — Incense Discernment! Once mastered, he could hold back the Filthoids in these parts. But alas, one man's strength is but a drop in the ocean.
So, I've had a think and narrowed it down to three things that make Haojing properly unique. Pin back your ears and listen!

So, I gathered a few like-minded old mates, and we come down to the Hall of Adjudication every day to share what we know — free of charge! After all, you can't visit Haojing without seeing the Hall of Adjudication, can you?
So, the Nine Chapters of Dafeng were established to spread the art far and wide! And right here, where the foundation was laid beneath the Hall of Adjudication, the city of Haojing was born!

First off, look up. That's the Hall of Adjudication, where Lord Argent resides. Sitting high above the peaks with Lord Argent circling overhead — you won't find a sight like that anywhere else in the world.
But... it's not working quite as we'd hoped. While I'm nattering away to you, I'm missing all those other folk over there. We reckon we need a fresh approach.
At first, Haojing was half the size it is now. But as the Xuanheng Sect grew, folks flocked to our gates. The Loongscions studied Incense Discernment, whilst the Earthborns cultivated the spices.
Second is how we live. You might have noticed on your way in: here, a "family" isn't just mum, dad, and the kids. We have the whole clan all under one big roof.
What if we staged a show right here? Imagine it: suona horns blaring, drums banging — clang! boom! crash! — who could possibly ignore a racket like that?

That's how Jiaolan Village came to be. Even today, it's the prime spot for growing. The folks there have been planting and offering incense for generations. They probably know more about it than us city folk!
It's about sticking together. Rubbing shoulders day in, day out. If anyone's in a spot of bother, the whole lot pitches in. You don't see that sort of closeness much elsewhere.
Glad you think so! You've got more sense than my own son. He thinks I'm making a spectacle of myself, always trying to drag me back home to save face!

You sound just like my son! He insists a performance would be a "public nuisance." Nuisance to whom? Is anyone sleeping in the middle of this square? Do you think we're going to wake Lord Argent in the sky?
The Nine Chapters of Dafeng brought peace to Huaxu, and with peace came people. To this day, Haojing has seen two massive expansions and numerous repairs.

As for the third... well, I'm in two minds. I thought about mentioning incense, but Huaxu is full of the stuff, isn't it? Nothing special there. I considered trade, but Mistwharf probably has us beat on that front.

Haojing is getting on in years, just like us. Lots of youngsters have moved on, but this old city has witnessed a thousand years of peace. It's the premier city of Huaxu, and don't let anyone tell you otherwise!

The way I see it, Haojing's strength is that it's a bit of a melting pot. You can find food and fun from every corner of Huaxu right here. This city holds onto people's hearts. When our children leave, they always want to bring the best of the outside world back home.
Blimey, Luo, that was well put. Did you rewrite your script or something?
So you patch all those little bits together, and that's what makes Haojing truly one of a kind.
Oh, you flatter me! My wife and I rehearsed it at home a fair few times, actually.
Well said! If you ask me, you're a shoo-in for Haojing's Tour Guide of the Year!
Oh, Han! You flatter me, I've still got plenty to learn!
Even if you mean well, it's a bit much to be hawking that right outside the offices...
I don't know where he dug up that rubbish about Haojing being "boring". Everyone knows word on the street deals in extremes — it's either the greatest place on the land or an absolute dump.
But the old folks don't get how the discourse works. They just felt their hometown was being slandered, so they cooked up this whole scheme.
Honestly, there are some things you just shouldn't tell the elderly.

What else? A few tourists ran around like headless chickens, then complained the city was dull and told everyone to "give it a wide berth". My old man heard that and didn't sleep a wink for three days.
Next thing I know, he's roped in a gang of pensioners to set up this "encyclopaedia lecture" right here, grabbing passersby for a stern talking-to.
Did you meet them too? Or just passing through? Take my advice: if you value ten minutes of your life, steer clear of them. Walk the long way round.

options.content: You think what they're doing is pointless?
So you don't support promoting Haojing's culture?

talks.content: I wouldn't go that far... but you can see it's a bit intrusive, can't you? Especially doing it right in front of the Hall of Adjudication — the most solemn place in the city!
Don't put words in my mouth. I support promoting our culture, just not like this!
If they've got time to kill, why not go do Huaxu calisthenics with the old blokes in the West District? Pestering tourists here... it's just a public nuisance.

options.content: So you want to persuade them to go home?

talks.content: The trouble is, you can't change people's minds about whether Haojing is "fun" with just a bit of crude propaganda.
Fat chance of that! They think they've made great progress and want to double down. Now they're plotting to stage a full-blown opera right outside the Hall, drums and gongs blazing.
Everyone comes for different reasons. Some come for ancient ruins, see the shiny renovated streets, and say: "Ugh, it's all fake antiques. Boring! One star!"
Just wait a couple of days. There'll be new complaints: "Why are there a bunch of noisy old fogies outside the Hall of Adjudication? Disrespectful to the Loong Lord. One star!"

options.content: You make a very good point.
They might not be entirely wrong, though.

talks.content: Others come for the Loong Lord. They go to the Hall of Adjudication, don't see him, and say: "What a waste of time, I didn't see the loong at all. One star!"
Right? Glad you agree. I just hope he wakes up to reality soon. We should just go home and live our lives. What outsiders think of Haojing is their business.
Oh, sure. In a sense, they might help some punters understand the city a bit better. But ask yourself: do those tourists actually care?
Haojing was never meant to please everyone. Truth be told, no place can. People decide how they feel on their own. Nothing anyone else says will change that.

options.content: So you want to persuade them to go home?

talks.content: What does it matter if they like it or not? We're the ones living here day in, day out. We know what the city is really like. And who doesn't love their own hometown?
They're here for a month at most. Even if they listen to thousands of years of history, it mostly goes in one ear and out the other. They won't truly feel it.
Anyway, I'm going to fight the old man on this. He claims his opera won't be a nuisance? Fine. I'm going to sleep right here just to prove he's disturbing me.
If a place doesn't give them what they want, they'll have a whinge about it. Even Lord Argent couldn't stop them. People have mouths, and they'll say whatever they please.
Let's see who cracks first...
My wife was just walking down the street, minding her own business. Then this bloke comes barreling along, not looking where he's going, and rams his cart straight into her.
I was looking! I shouted at her to move from miles away, but she just ignored me! With a load that heavy, I couldn't exactly stop dead on a sixpence, could I?
She's getting on in years! Of course her hearing isn't what it used to be. You could have asked someone near her to help. Excuses won't fix this now!
It all happened too fast for that! I shouted myself hoarse trying to warn her. If she still didn't hear me, you can't pin the crash on me!
Save your breath! I'm done arguing with you. Let's get the mediator involved. They'll see we get some justice!
Gentlemen, please, settle down. First things first: how is your wife doing? Has she received any medical attention?
Taken a nasty knock to the leg, she has. Bruised black and blue. At her age, bones are brittle. She hasn't been able to leave her bed since.
Shall we have the healers from Zesheng Pharmacy examine her before we proceed?
The skin wasn't even broken! Not a drop of blood! If she were actually hurt, Bi'an would have arrested me by now!
You've got a nerve! Just because it looks fine on the surface doesn't mean the bone isn't shattered underneath!
I demand you step in right now! We want a proper mediation and justice for my family!
You're just trying to stir up trouble and fleece me for money!
Enough! I'll put this all in the log. Go home for now; an official will take over the case in a couple of days. We'll visit you both to investigate properly and ensure a fair hearing for everyone.
To live well, keep to Heaven's Mandate, steadfast as Mr. Shazhou. To learn well, keep to your studies, diligent as Master Zhuxi.

Take Mr. Shazhou: upon joining the Xuanheng Sect, he revolutionised the art of Incense Discernment. He compiled a lifetime of knowledge into volumes, paving the way for all in Huaxu with the ambition to master the craft.

Then there is Master Zhuxi. He shunned the pursuit of high office to dedicate himself to teaching and writing. He founded Academy of Reflections, creating a sanctuary for thousands of scholars like myself.
Now the academy thrives, and its brilliant graduates are scattered across the world. If Master Zhuxi is watching from beyond, he must surely be comforted by our success.
Mr. Shazhou is a legendary incense warden in the annals of Huaxu. Before his time, Incense Discernment was an esoteric art reserved for geniuses. Mere diligence was never enough to master it.
As I mentioned earlier, though he once held office, he became the founder of our academy. He is a pioneer loved and revered by every student here.
Yet Mr. Shazhou codified his insights into A Compendium of Incense. He divided it into two volumes, the first written specifically for the scentless, granting even them a glimpse into the art.
Though Master Zhuxi has long since passed, his philosophy of Distinct Reasoning lives on in our halls. It is under this very ethos that the academy continues to flourish.

options.content: You sound like you really respect him.

talks.content: I admit, my own knowledge of Mr. Shazhou is somewhat limited. If you wish to learn more, you would be best served by visiting the archives at the Hall of Incense.

options.content: What do you mean by "the scentless"?

talks.content: Master Zhuxi served in the Ministry of Fortune. During his tenure, the region suffered terrible droughts. It is a famous tale — how the Ministries of Fortune and Works joined forces to build irrigation systems and save the people.
To be honest, I am not a native of Haojing. I travelled from afar to study at Academy of Reflections, drawn solely by the Master's reputation.
Put simply, it refers to those without a natural affinity for incense arts — which accounts for the vast majority of ordinary folk in Huaxu.
As he grew older, however, he left his post to devote himself entirely to the academy. Even in his final years, he painstakingly annotated our textbooks, chapter by chapter.
Or perhaps I should say: every student here holds him in high regard. I am merely one of thousands.
In fact, I count myself amongst them...

The greatest library Haojing ever saw was built through the advocacy of Master Zhuxi and his colleagues. It is a profound tragedy that scoundrels later burned down the majority of it... a great loss indeed.
When did I ever say I met Master Zhuxi in person? What I said was this: when my father was young, he heard Master Zhuxi give his final lecture at the academy.
Father said the Master was white-haired and nearly blind by then. Yet, despite his hunched back, he taught with a spirit that made you forget his age entirely.
You lot, always shirking your studies. Master Zhuxi poured his heart into annotating those books you neglect. Now you've heard the tale, isn't it time you cracked them open?
You're fobbing us off, Master! We asked for a fun story, not another lecture on studying!
What else am I to talk about in a school? Off with you now, you little scallywags, shoo!
(The students scatter, grumbling under their breath.)
Eh? Hello? Which class are you from? I don't recall seeing your face around here.
Ah, I keep saying — building a school right by the street asks for trouble. Passers-by wander in all the time. We really must put up a wall.
My peer class... what do you mean?
It means I don't study here but still bring you peer pressure.
Right then, young scholar. What can I do for you?

options.content: How did Master Zhuxi pass away?
Could you tell me the "fun story" those kids missed out on?

talks.content: I can't say for certain. Rumours abound, but most say old age and the exhaustion of running the academy simply worked him into the grave.
Aha, so that's your game! Very well, I suppose I can tell you a little something.
Others claim he was plagued by an illness that worsened until he finally succumbed.
I've heard Master Zhuxi was fond of his drink — a stark contrast to his usual austere manner. He'd invite friends to burn incense, warm wine, and debate philosophy.
Whatever the cause, nearly a thousand students gathered for his funeral. It was a sea of white mourning dress; their grief was palpable.
But rumour has it he was a terrible drunk. Once the wine hit, he'd lose his scholarly grace, raising his voice and arguing just for the sake of winning.
After all, Distinct Reasoning is a contentious subject. Even a well-reasoned debate can easily be mistaken for a row.
But if you ignore the debate and just shout your own "truth" at people... well, that's just an argument.
And that was Master Zhuxi. He'd argue until he silenced the room. Eventually, people stopped wanting to drink with him altogether.
But when the thirst took him, he'd swallow his pride, bring a gift to an old friend's door, and beg forgiveness just for a drinking companion.

options.content: Sounds like the esteemed Master Zhuxi was a bit of a nightmare on the drink.
That wasn't very interesting. Got anything else?

talks.content: No man is perfect. Every object has a thousand facets. Why should a human being be any different?
That's your lot, young scholar. If you want more stories, sign up for classes. We can have a proper chinwag next year.
Now, I must go and check if those children are actually memorising their texts.
They're too loud... How's anyone meant to learn like this!?
To inherit the world is a matter of great weight. The great sages of the world perform great deeds...
The world... the world belongs to all. Choose the virtuous and able... Argh, rubbish! That's from a completely different chapter!

Oh, bother. The master gave me three days, and time's up. I'm getting tested tomorrow; I'm absolutely done for... It's all because of this blasted noise! Of all the places to build an academy, why stick it right next to the high street?

options.content: What's wrong with being next to the street?

talks.content: Just listen! Peddlers shouting, children screaming! And smell that! The roasting meat, the perfumes! It's enough to drive a man to distraction. Two minutes of reading and I'm already itching to go out and buy a snack...

options.content: Fair point. But why is the academy built on a shopping street?

talks.content: Look at you. You're about my age, yet you sound exactly like the master! "Amidst the bustle, I alone am calm." If I had that sort of discipline, I'd have...
Sigh... It's just how Haojing developed. When the academy was first built, there was no East Market. It was all golden woods back then, peaceful as anything.
I'd be a master myself by now! Do you think I'd still be stuck here reciting texts?
Then the city expanded, and this massive market just sprouted up around us. I don't see why they couldn't have moved us somewhere else.
I can't chat anymore, I've got to cram. Woe is me! "Amidst the bustle, I alone am calm..." Master! It's no use! I just don't get it! Come save my soul! Aaaargh!!!

"One law" is the idea that heaven, earth, and all things share a single underlying truth. "Myriad reflections" means that the countless differences we see are simply manifestations of that same truth.
Master, I'm lost. How can everything be the same? Are you saying that you and I are... the exact same thing?
Let me put it this way. Consider the Law of "Master and Apprentice". You have a master, just as I do. My master had his own teacher, and if you apply yourself, you too shall have students one day.
We are both bound by the same governing Law of that relationship, yet our specific roles and circumstances differ. That distinction is what we call "Myriad Reflections."
But Master... what is this "Law", actually?

It is the cosmic order and the turning of the seasons. It is the ethics of society, the rules of the household, and the stability of the state. It is everything logical and correct — the standard for our conduct, the rules we follow, the very reason behind existence.
I... I still haven't the foggiest idea...

Very well. Look at the Nine Chapters of Dafeng. You know its laws. Yet you also know that if a man is determined to be wicked, the Nine Chapters cannot possibly list every single specific crime he might invent.
After all, there are only nine chapters, not a thousand or a million. And yet, when villains devise new forms of evil not explicitly written down, are their actions not still despicable?
The Nine Chapters represent the Law itself. You must follow the spirit of that Law, using it to judge each unique situation as it arises. That is "One Law, Myriad Reflections."
I think I might... possibly... sort of... maybe... vaguely understand now...
Splendid. Off you go then. Back to your books!

Flavours may differ a thousand ways, yet all tend towards the good. Tunes may change without end, yet all return to harmony. The young may vary in temperament, yet all share a quickness of wit. Methods of teaching may be many, yet all come back to the heart.
If we are to honour Master Zhuxi's founding vision, we must tailor our teaching to the individual. There is no other way.
Consider two children: one wild and playful, the other buried in books. Can you truly say which is the clever one?

options.content: The one with the better marks?

talks.content: Not so. You assume that high marks equal intelligence, and low marks stupidity. But the world is vast, and many things within it cannot be measured by an exam paper.
The playful child might tinker away until he's built a working wooden horse from scratch. The bookworm might stare at a page for hours, yet fail to memorise a single verse.
Now, who would you say is the clever one?

options.content: Perhaps the builder is the cleverer one, then.
Then maybe the studious child is the clever one after all.

talks.content: Wrong again. What if I told you the builder cannot read a word? That the mere sight of poetry gives him a headache and sends him running for the hills?

options.content: You're just going to contradict me whatever I say, aren't you?

talks.content: Yes, and no. That studious child later discovers he has an extraordinary nose for Incense Discernment. He can distinguish even the subtlest scents in an instant.

options.content: You're just going to contradict me whatever I say, aren't you?

talks.content: Haha, don't be cross. I simply wish to illustrate why we must teach according to a student's aptitude.
The Law we teach is not about mastering a specific trade. It is quite common for a child to have a poor memory for texts, or to struggle endlessly with arithmetic.
But to force every child into the same mould is to limit the Law itself. Our duty is to teach them to judge right from wrong, good from bad.
A child must honour their parents. A subject must serve Lord Argent with devotion. Partners must be faithful. And friends must be loyal and true.
In dealing with others, one upholds benevolence. In study, one practises discernment. In life, one follows the path of self-reflection.
If every child here can truly grasp these truths, then whether they achieve greatness or live simple lives, they will never stoop to harming others for their own gain.
That, precisely, is the wish Master Zhuxi held when he founded this Academy of Reflections.
There's one law behind everything. If it encompasses all things, it must come before all else!
Rubbish. This "Law" is invisible and intangible. One can only perceive it by examining the Diversity of Reflections — by looking at actual events.
Without a guiding Law — without an origin — how could specific things ever come into existence? You are speaking absolute nonsense!
And without concrete things to embody it, your so-called "Law" is nothing but a castle in the air. We must observe the Reflections before we can deduce the Law!
Then tell me this: without the Law to underpin your judgment, how do you distinguish right from wrong? Gut instinct? Or do you simply jump to conclusions based on nothing?
And I shall ask you: without action and reflection, how can you grasp the Law at all? We spot connections between events first, and then we summarise the truth.
Preposterous! Master Zhuxi once said there is only one sun, yet its light reaches every corner of the earth. Does that not prove the sun must exist before the light?
That is a flawed analogy and a weak argument. I'm done wasting my breath on you.
Get back here! If you walk away now, that means I have won!
You see? You only deduced the "Law" of your victory because of the specific event of me leaving. So I ask you again: which comes first? The One Law, or the Myriad Reflections?
You! You scoundrel, you tricked me!
Wasn't it your turn on duty today? You said your mum had a cold, so I covered for you for three days. Now even the teacher's starting to get suspicious!
Please, just two more days. Mum's cough has been getting worse, and I want to take her to Zesheng Pharmacy after class today.

You expect us to believe that? My dad saw you the other day at the candied fruit stall on the west side of town. He even asked why you weren't home, and you just pretended not to see him. You were obviously scared he'd catch you out.
That's rubbish. Mum's throat has been hurting, so I went to buy her some candied fruit to go with her medicine.
Fine... I'll cover for you again. But you have to explain it to the teacher yourself, alright? He keeps looking at me like I'm up to something...
You're the best! I'll go and explain everything to him right now!
He's obviously lying. He only does this because he knows you'll let him get away with it. You're too soft on him.
School's off for the Grand Incense Rite. Where are you guys going? My brother's just got back, and he says he's bringing me some cool stuff from abroad.
Your brother? Your Starweaver brother? The one who hasn't been home in years?
So what? It just means business is going well for him out there. You know that country that's always at war?
Er... my dad mentioned it once. What was it called again? The Hyper... Bored... something Empire?
It's the Hyperborean Empire. My brother does business there. Even their emperor treats him with respect!
Oh, come off it... My dad says that emperor's every bit as strong as Lord Argent. If even Lord Argent wouldn't make a fuss over your brother, why would the emperor?
Fine, don't believe me then. This time he's bringing me a music box that sings. I'll bring it to school, and then you'll all be jealous.
We're one short for the football match this afternoon. Have you checked with Yueshan yet? If he can make it, we'll absolutely wipe the floor with them.
I did. He said he's got something to deal with, so he can't make it today.
What? No way! If he's out, we don't even have enough players. There's no match then!
It's not just him. Zhen isn't feeling well today either, so she's not coming.
So are we playing or not? I couldn't focus in class at all. I spent the whole lesson thinking about this match.
Not enough for a proper match. You could still get a few people together and have a casual game. Better than nothing.
Nuh-uh! That's boring. I'm not doing that.
Alright then. Zhen said she wants to go hiking in the western hills in a couple of days. Are you coming?
We're talking about today. Why bring up something that's days away? And hiking's exhausting. You come back barely able to walk. Who'd want that?
Qianqian's going too. Well? Are you coming or not?
Tch... fine. I'll go.

Good. That settles your afternoon, then. Zhen wants pastries from that shop in the East Market. There's always a queue, and they open whenever they please. Since they're actually open today, you may as well go queue up.
Why? If she wants pastries, she can buy them herself. What's it got to do with me?
Suit yourself. Just don't forget you made a promise. You said that if she played football with you, you'd buy her pastries for a whole month.
...Alright, alright, I'll go. But tell her she's not backing out next time. Otherwise the deal's off.
At this rate, it's bound to expand again... but where can it possibly go from here?
We've already expanded the academy once. But now that we're admitting younger children as well, we find ourselves short of classrooms again.
And now they're building a new shopping street next door. Even if we were to expand again, where exactly would we put it?

Oh, absolutely. We've had applicants ever since the academy was founded. In the early days, when tuition was free, some parents even turned up carrying a pair of live geese, hoping it might improve their child's chances.
The fees we introduced later were modest, but at least we no longer had geese wandering about the grounds and interrupting lessons.

options.content: Why do you think it's so popular?
What happened to the geese in the end?

talks.content: There are many reasons. At first, people came because of Master Zhuxi's name. After that, word simply spread.
Ah... well. Most of the ones fit for eating were served at the New Year feast. The rest were given to farmers outside the city. And those we couldn't eat...

In the end, though, it was the Ministry of Fortune that funded the major expansion. That was when the academy truly began to make its name in Haojing. Before then, very few academies in Huaxu had grown to this size.
We released them in the spring. We did receive some criticism for it, though. Apparently, introducing birds from elsewhere disturbed the local flocks for a time.
Most were fairly small; one or two teachers would suffice. Academy of Reflections, however, is something of an exception. Perhaps that is part of what draws people to it.

options.content: So if you were to expand again, where would you go?

talks.content: Heh, but that's all in the past now. No lasting trouble came of it, really.

options.content: So if you were to expand again, where would you go?

talks.content: Hmm... we haven't quite decided. One of the teachers once suggested moving beyond the city walls. The students do complain that it has grown rather noisy around here.

I've thought the same myself, from time to time. Somewhere a little farther out — quieter, with clear streams and green hills. Peaceful. A touch rustic, perhaps... It does sound rather lovely, doesn't it?
But then again, we do have quite a few very young pupils now. If we moved too far out, those travelling in from the city would face a long journey every morning. That would be hard on them.
Ah well. We'll think about it properly when space truly becomes an issue. Perhaps that day will never quite come.
That's right. Come spring, I'll hand in my resignation. And when the time comes, I won't forget any of you, so don't worry.
Won't you reconsider? If it's about pay, I can talk to them. A raise isn't out of the question.
It isn't about that. I've been in Haojing a very long time. Lately... I've found myself missing home. Old friends. Familiar streets.
If it's homesickness, take some leave. Go home for a while, then come back after the Grand Incense Rite.
That's... part of it. It's just... my family, you know...
You've always had a mind of your own. Very well. Do as you think best.
Thank you for understanding.
(The old man put his hands behind his back and walked away.)
How could I possibly leave? I can't bring myself to go.

options.content: If you can't bear to leave, why say that you will?
You weren't entirely honest with him just now, were you?

talks.content: Oh! Where did you come from? You gave me quite a fright.
It seems you heard most of that. You're right. I didn't tell him everything. Some things are better kept to oneself. And besides...
It's something I must work through on my own. Until I have some idea of how to resolve it, speaking of it would only trouble others needlessly.

options.content: What is it that troubles you so much?

talks.content: It isn't so much distressing as it is complicated. When I first came to the academy, I hoped to exchange ideas with great minds — to test my thoughts against theirs and see what might come of it.

And after graduation, I stayed on to work here. Over time, my understanding of dialectics deepened, and I encountered ideas I had never even considered before. At first, I found it deeply invigorating.
But over time, something began to feel... amiss.

It feels as though academic exchanges and debates have become little more than contests in quotation. People hide behind texts, invoke ancient sages and famous scholars, and dress simple thoughts in ornate language. More often than not, the point seems less to seek the truth than to win the argument.
In the end, a debate rarely concludes because one side is persuaded. It ends because someone is too exhausted to continue.
That kind of exchange no longer brings me any new insight. I no longer feel that quiet delight when an idea is patiently worked through, or when someone helps me see my own thoughts more clearly.
I do not yet know how to mend it. Going home may not be the answer, but for now it is the only step I can think to take.
Perhaps I ought to set the books aside for a while and return to ordinary life... step out of the ivory tower, if only for a time.
Ah... listen to me. I must sound rather odd.

options.content: It makes sense. Perhaps you need to return to something more grounded.
Or perhaps you're simply tired and want a break.

talks.content: I'm not certain whether going home is the right answer. But something has to change.
You may be right. Perhaps a few days at home, wrapped up in the trifles of daily life, will leave me longing once more for the scent of ink and paper.
Whatever the case, thank you for listening. You've been very kind.
It's getting late. My family will be here to pick me up soon, so I won't keep you. If fortune allows, we shall meet again.
Take Master Wenzhu of the Four Drifters. If she and her companions had not stepped in, what else would have forced those who exploited loopholes in the Nine Chapters of Dafeng back into hiding?
Because of her, those they had wronged finally received the justice they had long been denied.
I disagree. The so-called Master Wenzhu— no, that criminal Drifter — merely answers violence with violence and intimidates others into submission. That does nothing to bring peace to Huaxu.
Meeting violence with violence merely perpetuates it. Fear spreads, and fear breeds instability. Even if such methods suppress wrongdoing for a time, they sow unrest in the long run.

On what basis do you say that? Violence used to restrain violence can, in some cases, be an effective means of checking wrongdoing. When people exploit the very rules and institutions meant to preserve order, can we still claim that peace truly exists?

You spoke just now of order. As you yourself said, peace in Huaxu rests upon the order established by the Nine Chapters of Dafeng — an order tested and upheld by generations before us. That is no empty slogan.
Where order already stands, vengeance does not mend injustice. It multiplies it.

If matters of right and wrong beyond the law are left to private judgment, violence will only spread. In the end, it harms others and corrupts those who use it. If that is so, what peace can there truly be?
Excellent. That concludes the first round. The two students may take a short rest. The second round will begin when the gong is sounded.
Now that's a debate topic. I haven't heard one this interesting at the academy in ages.
Ah! Pardon me — are you a student here? Or have you come to watch the debate?

options.content: I'm not a student. Just passing through.

talks.content: Ah, I see. It sounded as though you caught part of it. I'm curious — what do you make of it?

options.content: I don't really know much about this sort of thing.
Is it really all right to be discussing Drifters out in the open?

talks.content: Ah... my apologies. I thought that, since you stopped to listen, you might be interested. If not, I won't keep you.
Hmm. Do you mean you'd rather not judge without knowing the full story? Or is it simply that the subject is too sensitive, and you'd rather keep your thoughts to yourself?
Ah, I understand. The Drifters are hardly a comfortable subject in Huaxu. People say they've committed more crimes than anyone can count, do they not?
But you needn't worry. At Academy of Reflections, no subject is forbidden. This is a place for debate. Any view, no matter how controversial, may be argued and challenged here.
If you can defend your position, you may argue it. We all agree that the sun is round. But if you insist it is square, and can make your case, then others must at least hear you out.
That is what sets this academy apart. Here, there is only one rule: no resorting to force. If you wish to prevail, you must do so with words and reason.

options.content: So you're all pretty savage debaters, then.

talks.content: It is. That's why I came all this way to study here. To put it plainly, you may argue even the most absurd claim imaginable — and if you argue it well enough, you will find an audience ready to be convinced.
Savage? We're civilised here. We argue with facts, not fists.
Many truths, before they were accepted, were once dismissed as nonsense. Wouldn't you agree?
But really, debate isn't so different from invention. When a new idea first appears, most people think it absurd.
But those who dare take that first step — and keep refining their arguments, putting them to the test — are often the ones who turn bold ideas into accepted truths.
So then, what do you think? Do you side with the first speaker — that the Drifters, in their own way, help preserve peace in Huaxu? Or with the second — that their actions do more harm than good?

options.content: I agree with the first speaker.
I agree with the second speaker.
I don't want to pick a side.

talks.content: If you hurt people, you should pay for it. If the law has loopholes, then someone has to step in.
Getting even might feel good, but it doesn't keep the peace. If we want real solutions, we need to find another way.
If the law were truly fair, none of this would be happening in the first place.
Hmm... you've given me something to think about. Thank you. In the second round, those in the audience may join in as well.
I think I know which side I'll take now. Or perhaps you have simply helped me see my own thoughts more clearly.
In any case, thank you for speaking with me. I'd best go and put my name down. Perhaps we shall meet again.
All talk, no action. If you've got time to spare, go and read a book.
I can't stand people who hide behind "open debate" just to talk dangerous nonsense. These students are supposed to be the future of Huaxu, and this is what they waste their time on.
What else? A pack of fools arguing about the Drifters.
What's the point? If the Drifters were truly in the right, would they be shunned and hated wherever they went?
And those so-called Four Drifters? Spare me. Just a handful of outlaws fancying themselves heroes. The Magistrates of Yingtian will round them up and make an example of them.
That's a bit harsh, isn't it?
You might have a point.

Harsh? Do you even know what the Drifters have done? That Miemeng device of theirs — do you know how many people in my hometown suffered because of it? Tch. Forget it... We're clearly not going to see eye to eye. I'd better not waste my breath.
One of those so-called Four Drifters — that woman with her Miemeng device. When the thing collapsed, do you know how much farmland it destroyed?

My hometown used to be rich and fertile. After that accident, we had flooding for three straight years. The embankments gave way, and the crops were washed away. Do you have any idea how many families lost everything overnight!?
Every one of those Drifters should answer for what they've done. None of them should escape punishment. And those who defend them... they ought to answer for it too...
And what makes you say that? Honestly, Huilan, you visit a few gardens, buy a few bundles, and suddenly you can't stop praising them?
Oh, come off it. I'm only telling the truth. We're still hauling manure and water around by hand, while the bigger gardens have already started using new tools.
New tools? What sort?

I heard some of them have been working with the Jishu Sect. Their artificers made something for them... what was it called again? Some kind of farming kite, I think. Looks small enough, but it can carry a fair bit.
They use it to water the fields from above, so everything gets covered evenly. It's a lot quicker than trudging back and forth with buckets.
And that's not even counting things like clearing the land. Their methods are just far more advanced.
Even so, Huilan, better tools don't necessarily mean better incense.
No, I do think it matters. If it didn't, why would we have been buying more and more incense from outside gardens these past few years?
Even with the extra fields we bought in Jiaolan Village, it still isn't enough. We can't keep up with demand on our own, so we still have to buy from outside.
I know, I know~ But... Miss Shuyao, could I come along this year?
You've only been here a year. It's not really your turn yet. Still, if you really want to go, I can put your name forward.
Really!? That's great! You're the best, Miss Shuyao!
Not so fast. You're never this eager when it comes to your usual work, so what's brought this on?
Come on, Miss Shuyao~ You know what it's like here. Every day it's the same work — hauling incense, laying it out to dry, processing it...
It's been a year— no, more than a year! And I'm still doing the same thing every single day. It's so boring~
But if I got to go, I'd at least get out for a change, wouldn't I? I might finally get to see something new and interesting!
Don't get ahead of yourself. Even if you do go, you'll be there to inspect the incense on site, choose the best batches, and bring them back. Same work, different place.
What? That sounds awful. Then I'm not going!
That's not for you to decide on a whim. You've been here a year, and your Incense Discernment is still barely beyond the basics. You can't keep coasting on what you came in with.
I'm taking you this time so you can learn properly. If you don't build a solid foundation in Incense Discernment, you'll never be able to tell the difference when two batches are close in quality.
Aww... noooo! That's not what I wanted!
May I ask where the incense warden is? I've come from Yinyuan, and I have an appointment with him.
Good day. We were to meet here, were we not? I am not late, I hope.
The white-clad Loongscion... was that not you? Did you not say we were to meet outside the Hall of Incense in three days' time?

options.content: You've mistaken me for someone else.
Yes, that's me. You've found the right person.

talks.content: Ah... my apologies! I've never been any good with faces, not since I was young. How embarrassing. I did not mean to trouble you.
You said before that the Skylilies from our garden were of fine quality, though perhaps somewhat dear. After I returned, I raised the matter again with my young master.
I shall step aside at once. Please forgive me.
We would be willing to lower the price by two per cent, but only if the Hall of Incense increases its order. As you know, our Skylilies are well regarded throughout Huaxu.
Even without the Hall of Incense, we could always sell to private traders. So I am afraid this is the furthest we can go.

options.content: Still sounds a bit steep to me.
We can't have you taking a loss!

talks.content: Now, that's hardly fair. We're coming to you in good faith here. If this goes through, we're talking long-term business.
No, no, that won't do at all. We can't have you losing money on goods like these. We really do want to make this work.
Selling a few batches here and there isn't the same as landing a steady official order with the Hall of Incense. Come on, you know which deal's better.
Tell you what — we'll add three percent to the original price. No, make it five! We want the very best Skylilies you've got!
B—But, {性别:sir|ma'am}, our Skylilies are famed for a reason. Our water, soil, and fertiliser are all of the highest quality, and the costs are considerable. If we lower the price any further...
...What? Th—That is rather...
Ah, well, that does make things awkward... If that's your final word, I suppose this goes no further.
And as for quantity... however much your garden grows, we'll take the lot. Every batch, every grade — all of it.
(Just as you are running your mouth, you hear hurried footsteps approaching.)
Ahem... right, bad timing. Something's come up. I've got to run!
Wh—What? Wait—
Excuse me — are you the representative from Yinyuan?
Hm? Wait... then who was that?
(Run! If they catch you now, you're dead!)
How come you're the one offering incense today? Has your brother gone back to Mistwharf again?
Don't even get me started. All he cares about these days is money.

He only came back a couple of days ago. Mother asked him to stay a little longer, but he just brushed her off. We all thought he would at least stay through the Grand Incense Rite. And yet he left so soon!
Well... he is a businessman, after all. The slightest hint of trade and off he goes. That is only to be expected.
Here, today's incense. Make your offering, then head home early, all right?
Oh? Are you here to make an offering as well? Hmm... no. You're not from Haojing, are you?

options.content: So if I'm not a local, I can't offer incense?

talks.content: By scent. You don't have it on you.
Not at all. Lord Argent welcomes any who come with kindness in their hearts.

Most of those who come to the Hall of Incense for the daily offering are Haojing locals. When they register at the Hall of Founts, an incense warden performs a rite that marks them with a distinct scent.
You don't have it on you. That's how I knew.

options.content: What sort of rite is that?

talks.content: It is called Incense Discernment. Every incense warden learns the basics of it at the start of their training.

At its simplest, it is merely the ability to tell one scent from another. At a more advanced level, it allows one to place a scent mark on others. Any Loongscion trained in the art would recognise such a mark at once.
There are exceptions, of course. Some Loongscions are naturally gifted. Even without formal training, they can sense that something is unusual, though they may not be able to explain it.

options.content: I see. And what can it do once someone has mastered it?

talks.content: Oh, quite a lot. At more advanced levels, one may draw fragrance into the body, fortify the body, or even refine the soul through scent. Within the Xuanheng Sect, there are many disciplines devoted to such arts.

But not everyone has the chance to learn such things. Most of those with real talent are chosen by Lord Argent to become Magistrates of Yingtian. As for the rest of us, with enough practice, we may at least serve the people as capable incense wardens.

options.content: So can I offer incense or not, then?

talks.content: Of course. It is only that the offering made by a visitor differs from that of a registered resident. If you mean to remain in Haojing for the long term, you would do best to register at the Hall of Founts.
After all, the grade of one's offering determines how much protection one receives from Lord Argent. So it is rather important.
Here is your incense. May your virtue endure for all time.
May Heaven bless us, and may Lord Argent watch over us. May my father be in good health, and kept safe from illness.
*cough* ...May Lord Argent have mercy. Please let my father recover soon. Spare him this pain. If it meant saving him, I'd give my own life... *cough*
Who— *cough* ...Who are you?

options.content: You shouldn't say things like that.

talks.content: I... I know. I was just so worried about my father, I wasn't thinking... *cough*
My father is bedridden now. All I could do was come here and pray for Lord Argent's mercy.

options.content: Shouldn't you be at home looking after him?

talks.content: *cough* ...As you can see, I've been down with a chill these past few days. I'm afraid that if I stay near him, I'll pass it on to my father. He's already so frail...
I'm going to Zesheng Pharmacy shortly to pick up some medicine. Once this cough eases, I'll go home and look after him properly.
Thank you for your concern. May Lord Argent watch over you as well.
Mm... I just want to be taller. Just a bit. Like everyone else...
(As you approach this Luno, you notice something slightly unusual about her.)
Hey! What are you staring at? Mesmerised by my beauty, are you? Well, I am different from the other Lunos. Naturally, you'd be drawn to me~

options.content: I don't see anything special about you.

talks.content: (You give her a careful once-over, trying to figure out what makes her seem different.)
What!? Seriously!? I'm taller than the other Lunos! Look — they barely come up to your waist, but I... I can at least make it past your belly button!
H—Hey... stop that... You're staring a hole through me...
Now that you mention it... I suppose you do.
(I've got it! She is a bit taller than the other Lunos!)
Hehe~ See? Those three extra-thick insoles did the trick. I stand out straight away!

options.content: So that wish earlier was about your height?

talks.content: Are you... a bit taller than an ordinary Luno?
Yeah... I come here every day to offer incense. I'm hoping Lord Argent will see how sincere I am and make me grow a little taller~

options.content: Can praying really make you grow taller?
Why do you want to be taller?

talks.content: Y—You figured it out!? I secretly stuffed three whole insoles into my shoes... I—I mean... how did you even notice?

options.content: So that wish earlier was about your height?

talks.content: Hmph. You're no fun. I won't know unless I try.
Mm... I just think being a Lunarian is a bit... boring. We all look exactly the same. Same head. Same body.
And clearly, all my hard work has paid off — you spotted me in the crowd straight away and came over to talk to me.
I want to be more unique. At least different enough to stand out from the rest. Not because of fancy clothes or accessories, either — I want to be reeeally special all on my own.
So obviously, you've fallen for my charm!
(She's every bit as full of herself as Snow...)
Hehe~ My height-boosting plan is working perfectly. I'd better hurry home and find even more insoles to stuff in~
In past years, they always needed plenty of extra hands at the Hall of Incense during the Rite. So why's it gone so quiet there this year?
You hadn't heard? There was some sort of accident at the Hall a few days ago. It drew several Sable Bi'an.
Oh? Then it must have caused quite a commotion. How did I not hear about it? What happened after that?
Apparently, two of the temporary workers they'd just taken on stepped in and drove the Sable Bi'an away. Otherwise, things might have got badly out of hand.
Ah, it's always a mad rush before the Rite. I knew something was bound to happen sooner or later. Maybe now they'll finally start being more careful.
Still, I wonder where they found people capable of driving off something as vicious as a Sable Bi'an. If I ever get the chance, I'd quite like to meet them.
Inspect the incense reserves in every censer across the city. Be thorough. Pay special attention to the one on the water in the central square. Don't miss a thing.
Everything is in place. We've also collected the incense gauges from the Hall of Craft and issued them to today's incense wardens.
Good. You may go.
...We must proceed with care. We cannot allow that disaster to happen again.
Hm? You... you're not from Haojing, are you? If you were, you'd already know.
There are reasons I can't speak of it in detail. But I can at least tell you the broad outline.

Put simply, during the Rite, while everyone was occupied with their duties, a criminal exploited the confusion and extinguished Haojing's most important censer — one that had burned uninterrupted for over a century.
That threw the ambient incense density across much of Haojing badly out of balance, and all sorts of disasters followed.
The Magistrates of Yingtian eventually intervened and brought the matter under control, but... it would be best not to say any more.
Hm? If you have to ask that, then I'd wager you're not from Huaxu either. Very well. I'll explain.
You do know that Huaxu relies on incense diffused through the air to keep the Nine Chapters of Dafeng operating, don't you? Ambient incense density is simply the concentration of incense in the air.
Only when it remains above a certain level can the Nine Chapters continue to function steadily, without being disrupted by outside influences, and better protect the people of Huaxu.

options.content: What do you mean by "outside influences"?

talks.content: With a specialised device known as an incense gauge. It's very small — about the size of two copper coins.
Several things. The most common are changes in the weather — rain lowers the ambient incense density, while clear skies tend to raise it somewhat.
They're difficult to manufacture, and the materials are extremely costly, so under normal circumstances only incense wardens on duty are permitted to sign one out.

Another is whether the local censers are being properly maintained and replenished with Lunarose incense. There were occasional oversights in the past, but ever since the Hall of Craft developed the regional incense gauge, that has ceased to be a problem.

options.content: Thank you. That was very informative.

talks.content: You heard it just now, didn't you? With the Grand Incense Rite approaching, the Hall has been monitoring the ambient incense density far more closely. That's why I sent that new girl to requisition a gauge under my authority.

options.content: Thank you. That was very informative.

talks.content: You're welcome. I should return to my duties now. Enjoy your stay in Huaxu.
Has my mind really gone dull? Can't I come up with any new incense recipes any more?
No point denying it... I'm getting old. My mind simply isn't as quick as the young ones any more.

Here — take a sniff. This is someone else's work. At first, you catch the sharp, bracing clarity of Lantern Bloom. Give it a moment, and a thread of honeyed sweetness begins to emerge. Then, as the fragrance settles, the weight of Ivorywood reveals itself — deep, still, and steady.

options.content: (You lean in for a closer sniff.)

talks.content: (The scent hits your nose, sharp enough to sting. You instinctively pull back and take a breath of fresh air. Yet beneath that bite, a faint sweetness begins to bloom.)
(Just as you begin to savour that sweetness, it fades, leaving behind the scent of smouldering wood — not exactly pleasant, perhaps, but far less biting than before.)
Well? What do you think, my friend? An unusual fragrance, isn't it? It suits its name perfectly.
It's called... The Road to the Spring of Yu.

Doesn't the name suit it perfectly? The Spring of Yu is the place where, according to Huaxu legend, the souls of the dead return. The name alone sends a shiver through you, much like the first piercing note of Lantern Bloom.

But then your thoughts begin to wander. You remember fragments of your life — people you once knew, moments that once meant something to you. And with those memories comes a sweetness... tinged with sorrow.

And then, at last, you understand. Whatever ties once bound you in life can hold you no longer. What remains is a quiet stillness — the same lonely calm that lingers in Ivorywood long after the rest of the fragrance has faded.

options.content: I didn't really get all that.
That's a beautiful way of putting it.

talks.content: Ah... that's only natural. I didn't either, at first. It took me nearly a month of studying this blend before I began to understand what its creator was trying to express.

Ah... to tell the truth, when I first heard the name, I couldn't make sense of it. It sounded far too grim for a blend. But after spending a month studying it, I gradually began to understand what its creator was trying to express.
Whoever created it must have spent a long time thinking seriously about death.

Sometimes I think blending incense is very much like living. You take all that you've lived through, all that you've come to understand, and work it into a single blend. Through fragrance, you give voice to what lies in your heart.

Perhaps that is why people like us — shut away in the upper halls, far removed from the rough edges of ordinary life — can never create blends with this kind of depth. When faced with work like this, all we can do is marvel... and sigh at our own limits.
Perhaps it's better that we simply tend to the work before us — perfect each stick of Lunarose incense, and make sure we do not disappoint Lord Argent.
Different incense recipes have different effects. You're new here, so it's no wonder you don't know.
Master, what I don't understand is this: what role does the art of Incense Discernment actually play in making incense?
I've read through A Compendium of Incense several times, and no matter how I look at it, the process seems no different from the way incense is made outside the Hall.
That is because you have not yet mastered the art of Incense Discernment. The Hall does not teach its other formulae to novices.
The subtler uses of Incense Discernment cannot be explained in a sentence or two. Let me give you an example. You know the ingredient Yueheng, do you not? Tell me what you remember of its properties.

Yueheng... it prefers warmth and can withstand drought. Its calyx may be used medicinally. It is covered in fine hairs, so before it can be used in incense, the top must be removed, washed clean, and the hairs carefully plucked away with tweezers. It is said to improve the complexion, clear the mind, and sharpen the senses.
Good. Then let me ask you this: have you ever made incense with it yourself?

I have. There was a time when I spent all day working on blends that used it as a base. I breathed in that scent from morning till night, and all it gave me was a pounding headache. So much for clearing the mind!

That is because such properties do not emerge through ordinary blending alone. Only Incense Discernment can truly bring out a material's particular effects. Tell me — do you still think it is useless?
What? Master, are you saying Incense Discernment is not merely a way of telling ingredients apart, but an art that draws out their properties fully?

In Incense Discernment, one begins by learning to distinguish scents and ingredients. Only when you are thoroughly familiar with the nature of each ingredient can you truly unite their distinct effects into one. That is what it means to blend incense.
It sounds incredible... But Master, why can't I start learning it now? I think I already know these ingredients very well.

Because the time has not yet come. Study for a few more years. One day, amid that tangle of scents, you will suddenly catch the one true note that belongs to each ingredient. When that happens, you will have reached the threshold.
What!? And that's only the threshold!?

What else did you expect? That I should turn you muddle-headed little greenhorns loose on the blends, only for you to push arum's properties to such absurd extremes that the moment it is lit, everyone in the Hall drops asleep?
That's enough. Quiet your mind, compose yourself, and learn properly.
Have you heard? The Hall of Incense has brought in a special incense warden this year. They say it's... a Lunarian!
Oh, come off it. A Lunarian incense warden? At that height, could she even reach the rim of a censer?
I'm serious. That's what I heard. Apparently there's a Lunarian who's obsessed with incense — studied it for years, sat the exams three years in a row, and finally earned herself a place in the Hall.
Heh. And what exactly is a Lunarian meant to do in there? Sounds to me like the wardens just wanted to make a show of it.

options.content: That's a bit harsh, don't you think?

talks.content: What do you mean?

options.content: That's hardly fair to the Lunarian.
That's hardly fair to the incense wardens who accepted her.
That's hardly fair to the Lunarian and the incense wardens.

talks.content: You don't even know her, yet you've already decided she's unqualified. If she worked that hard to earn the position, isn't that a little unfair?
You don't know the full story, yet you've decided the incense wardens only took her in for attention. That seems rather unfair to them.
You don't know the full story. Yet you've already decided the Lunarian is unqualified, and that the incense wardens only took her in for attention.
I think our friend here has a point. You may have gone a bit too far.
Isn't that a rather narrow way of looking at it?
I... I didn't mean it like that...
All right... I was wrong. I let my prejudices against the Lunarians get the better of me, and I ended up speaking out of turn about the Hall's incense wardens as well.
I'll go and find out what really happened. Until I know the full story, I won't be so quick to judge anyone again.

options.content: What's that saying again? "To admit your mistake..."

talks.content: "...is a virtue indeed."
All right, all right — it was only a bit of hearsay. No need to get so serious over it.
A Lunarian!? Those stunted, big-headed little creatures? How could one of them possibly be fit to serve as an incense warden?
You narrow-minded oaf — what's that supposed to mean? Why can't a Lunarian be an incense warden?
Could they even tell those thousand-odd ingredients apart? With fingers that tiny, they'd struggle to handle even the simplest task around the Hall.

That Lunarian's been helping out at Boshan Incense House for years. Anyone who's been there will tell you she knows her ingredients inside and out — some would even say she knows more than the incense wardens at the Hall.
People just thought she was adorable and praised her the way they would a child, that's all. You're not seriously taking that at face value, are you?
Being an incense warden is serious work. It takes maturity and sound judgement. Lunarians aren't made for that sort of responsibility. I don't see this ending well.
Whether it ends well isn't for you to decide. You stubborn fool — I'm done talking to you.
Have you asked at the Hall of Founts? It's always hectic before the Grand Incense Rite. Best to chase that allocation up early, or you won't get much done.
