Now that Haojing has grown to its present size, it is rare to see public works large enough to bring out the whole Ministry of Works. Only around festival time does the place feel properly lively again.

Uncle Boyuan, this year's Incense Proving is meant to be larger than in previous years. When the Ministry of Fortune came by earlier to discuss arrangements, they said we could ask for a little extra funding this year.
But I looked over the budget proposal we submitted, and we didn't ask for a penny more than the bare minimum. You're always saying how rare it is for everyone to get together like this, so why not...
What crooked little idea are you cooking up now? We of the Jishu Sect are honest craftsmen. We do not dip into public funds for our own benefit.
I didn't say we should do anything improper! I just thought... perhaps we might ask for a little extra — enough to buy the artisans some wine, or a few gifts to show our appreciation.
Don't be absurd. Funds from the Ministry of Fortune are meant to benefit the people of Huaxu, not to be spent on our own enjoyment.

We in the Ministry of Works may not be flush with money, but we can still afford to look after our own. Go and tell the others this — once the Grand Incense Rite is over, I'll reserve Bazhen Pavilion, and we'll all have a proper feast.
Really? Wonderful! Uncle Boyuan, that's so generous of you! I'll go and tell everyone the good news at once!
Any idea why this burner keeps acting up? Sorry to trouble you again, but it won't behave.
Nothing to apologise for. If something's broken, we fix it. That's what I'm here for.
Have you been running this incense burner nonstop? Letting it overheat and then cooling it too quickly?
I... I'm not sure. When things get busy, everyone's passing tools around, and different ingredients have to be handled differently. Maybe someone splashed water on it while cleaning it between uses.
Looks that way. I'll add another insulating layer. Once you take it back, it should work properly again. Just remember what I told you and handle it with care.
I will. And... sorry again for the trouble.
Still apologising? If you feel that bad about it... come here. Lean closer.
My head? What do you— Ow! That hurt! Why did you flick my forehead?
Ha! Weren't you feeling bad about it? That'll help you remember.
That really hurt!
Good. That means it worked. Now we're even. Next time something goes wrong, come straight to me. I'll fix it — and maybe flick your forehead again.
We're here tending the incense, and all around it's chatter and mutter, whisper and yap, grumble and grouse without end. How are we supposed to do our duties properly like this?
Mhm. I've been sitting here listening to you chatter and mutter, grumble and grouse without end all day. No wonder my head's buzzing.
Stop copying the way I talk!
The joint you've made won't hold. With the puppet lifting its arms and twisting at the waist all the time, that tenon's going to split sooner or later.
What use is durability if the thing can't move properly? That brass pin of yours is far too cumbersome. Once it's in, the puppet won't turn cleanly. How's anyone meant to perform with that?
Listen to yourself. Your puppet won't even make it through half a performance before it falls apart.
Master drilled this into us on day one: in our trade, the first thing is that it has to be sound. It's only been a few years, and you've already forgotten that.
Don't throw Master's words in my face. He also said that when a craft reaches its limits, you find a way beyond them. Even if that means taking an unconventional path, you keep going.
There's no talking sense into you. Let's get someone else to settle this.
Fine, then. You there — you've been listening to us this whole time, haven't you? Come over and tell us what you think.
(Both men, red-faced from arguing, turn towards you.)
Here's the matter, then. We've been commissioned to make puppets for a street troupe in West Market.
As you heard, we can't agree on what to use for the joints.
He wants to use brass pivot pins for the joints. I say they're too heavy. A performance puppet needs to take all sorts of poses — if it can't twist properly, what's the point?
He wants wooden tenons. But wood wears down under repeated strain. No matter how tightly you fit them at first, give it time and the whole thing will work loose.

options.content: I'd go with the wooden tenons.
I'd go with the brass pins.

talks.content: I think wood makes more sense. They're stage puppets, after all. If it moves too stiffly, it'll spoil the performance.
I think brass is the better choice. A commissioned puppet ought to last, and if it falls apart mid-performance, that's no small matter.
That's beyond me. You should probably ask another master in the Hall.
Hear that? That's what I've been saying! We'll do it my way!
Hmph! Hear that? Now that's proper advice.
Ah... yes, you're right. I didn't think that through. Sorry to have troubled you.
I'll take my puppet over to them myself right now. Ha!
When they come to collect the order, just shove your puppet aside and let them take mine.
Check this out — our new wind-up wooden Petit Boar. Wind it up and it'll dash ten metres in a flash. Want to learn how to make one? Sign up as an apprentice with the Jishu Sect!
Hmph. What's that even good for? My dad's always said you lot at the Hall of Craft are no good at anything except causing trouble.
What if that thing goes charging off and hits someone? And even if it doesn't, what if it smashes into a stall or a wall?

You blockheads! Why can't you do something proper like the Hall of Incense across the street? All you ever do is wave these wooden toys about to lure children over, then pester us to join your sect. What a bore!
You cheeky brat... have you no manners? I was speaking to you in good faith, and this is how you answer me?
Hmph. Useless carpenter. I'm off. Go play with your wooden scraps.
(The child vanishes in the blink of an eye, leaving just you and the artisan staring at one another in awkward silence.)
Ha ha... well. Sorry you had to see that.

options.content: Has the Hall of Craft really got such a bad name?
Is this how you recruit apprentices?

talks.content: People misunderstand us. Can't blame them — they don't see what these mechanisms can really do.
All we can do is use a few clever little gadgets to draw children in. Once they start learning the craft for themselves, they won't be so quick to believe all those rumours and prejudices.
Hang on... are you interested in Jishu? Fancy apprenticing with us? It won't make you rich overnight, but it's always good to have a trade under your belt.

Oh! You are? Ever since he went off to Mistwharf, he hasn't sent so much as a single letter back to us. I was beginning to think he'd holed himself up in some mountain cave, buried in his work, and forgotten all about us.
But seeing you puts my mind at ease. Looks like he hasn't forgotten the duty of passing on the Jishu Sect's craft after all. You seem a sharp one.

options.content: Why are people so prejudiced against you?

talks.content: Ahem... well, it goes back a long way. Some large combat mechapuppets were once built with offensive capabilities, and the Nine Chapters banned any further research into them. That was where the distrust began.

But we've done a great deal of good as well. The censers all across Huaxu? We built them. The tools used by the incense wardens? Ours too. Even all sorts of gear the Starweavers rely on comes from us.
Huaxu couldn't function without the Jishu Sect — without the Hall of Craft and the Ministry of Works. Surely you can see that.
Exactly. If I keep doing all I can to pass on the Jishu Sect's craft, people will see us differently one day.
Listen to yourself... I'll pretend I didn't hear that. The Jishu Sect will turn things around. Sooner or later.
And when that day comes, instead of sending every gifted child off to the Xuanheng Sect, people will be clamouring to get their children into our Hall instead.
Things are already looking up, aren't they? Master Gongshang managed to bring someone as exceptional as you into the sect. I'd say the future's looking pretty bright!
Sir, what's that? It's so cute! Can I have it?
Oh? You like this? It's one of my finest pieces. Go on, pick it up.
I'm scared... What if it suddenly flies up and pecks my fingers?
It won't! The little birds I make are perfectly safe. Here, take it. Feel along its back — see that little knob near the tail?
Um... I think so... Oh! There it is!
Just give it a little turn. Nice and slow. Go on — try it.
(The child does so hesitantly, and the little bird begins chirping in her hand.)
Wow! That's amazing! I want one too!
Impressive, isn't it? Hehe — but I can't just give you this one for free.
Huh? How much is it, then? I'll go home and ask my mum for the money!
Hehe. If you want a little bird like this, you'll need to hand yourself over to the Jishu Sect, spend the rest of your life learning the craft, and make one for yourself in the end.
H—Hand myself over!? Waaaah! There's a bad man here trying to kidnap children!
What!? No! That's not what I meant! I only meant you could join the Jishu Sect— oh dear, don't cry!
Year after year we recruit, year after year nobody comes. Instead of trying to rope people in, we'd be better off pouring that effort into a project that'll shake the world.
Up on the high stage, peeking from far away — silly little builders, stacking it up all day~
Soft footsteps, slow and light~ A pale figure comes to stand by my side~
Hello, pale figure. Are you one of those silly builders too?

options.content: What do you mean, silly builders?
And what about you? You're not one of the silly dots, then?

talks.content: Look for yourself. From up here, the ones who walk on the ground, swim in the water, and fly through the sky... don't they all look like little dots?
Of course not. Those silly dots are dark, mostly dark... sometimes they cover themselves in bright colours to seem different.
The little dots move so slowly. Sometimes they gather together, and sometimes they drift apart. By day they're black, and by night they turn into little yellow ones.
But they're solid through and through. I'm not. I'm blue... and hollow. I don't have to walk on the ground. I don't have to swim in the water. I don't have to fly through the sky. I only drift here.

They don't know where they're supposed to go, or what kind of dot they're supposed to be. Maybe one day they'll all join together and become lines instead. Who knows? That's why I think they're silly.

options.content: Then I suppose I'm not one of them.

talks.content: So I'm not one of those silly dots. But you... hmm... maybe you are.
Maybe you are. Maybe you aren't. But since you came here, and since you're talking to me, perhaps you're not that silly after all. You can stand up high and look down at the silly dots too.
(No point arguing with a Wishen. I'd better go.)
But you seem silly as well. You're standing where you were never meant to stand, and you're being led by things you cannot see, all the while believing every step was your own choice.
Goodbye, pale figure. Come and see me again sometime~
And yet... hmm...
Hehe... I'm not telling. Didn't you say you weren't silly? Then you can work it out yourself.
Ah! Another visitor with a long nose? Hey~ why are you staring at me like that?
Not yet. But it will be, one day. You're not from Huaxu. I could tell at a glance.

options.content: So people from Huaxu don't grow long noses?

talks.content: Once, there was a pretty girl from a faraway place. She carried a little square box, and when I asked what was inside, she wouldn't tell me.
The people of Huaxu are all under Lord Argent's protection. A nasty curse like that can't touch us.
She said it was a secret. She'd promised someone she wouldn't tell. And if she told me, she'd be breaking that promise — and people who break promises grow long noses.
Once, there was a strange foreigner who told me that where she came from, people grew long noses if they broke their promises.

So I said, how could that be? People fail to keep their promises all the time. When I was little, I'd promise my friends I'd go out and play with them, but if Mum kept me indoors, of course I couldn't keep my word.
I didn't believe her, so she said, "Look, I've got a little box here. I promised someone I wouldn't tell anyone what's inside. If I tell you now, I'll grow a long nose straight away."

options.content: So did you ask her to tell you what was inside?

talks.content: And then she said that rule only works where she comes from. The people of Huaxu are under Lord Argent's protection, so a nasty curse like that can't take hold here.
No. She was pretty. If a nose as long as a carrot had grown on her face... wouldn't that have been dreadful?
But looking at you now, I don't see any sign of a long nose yet. Still, since you're from elsewhere, it'll probably happen sooner or later.
So I didn't ask again. Besides... that box looked quite plain. It didn't look like there was anything good inside anyway.
Of course, you should keep the promises you make. But there are so many things in this world that people cannot help. So if your nose really does grow long one day, it might not be your fault.
I only hope you won't go against your own heart.
(The Wishen seems to be hinting at something, but without knowing its story, it's hard to make sense of it.)
Look at you, all dressed in white. Far too plain. You look like you're going to a funeral!
Exactly! Not like a Huaxu child at all. It's the Grand Incense Rite — Qianxiu Pavilion's packed with bright reds and deep purples, and you're still wearing white from head to toe.
Who else would we be talking about? Come here, child. Let me have a proper look at you.
(There's something oddly hard to refuse in the woman's voice. Before you know it, you've stepped forwards — and in the next instant, she's already tugged you over.)
Oh, my word, look at you. Those little arms are thin as twigs. You poor thing... your family isn't treating you badly, are they? Haven't they been feeding you properly?
And look at that face — pale as paper! You look like you've just come through a famine. Come round to mine, child. I've cooked a whole table of food. You must come and have a proper meal.
This batch of incense isn't dry enough yet. Here, have a smell. The aroma hasn't developed properly.
Sniff, sniff... mm...
Hmm... it smells warm, like it's been sitting in the sun all day. How's that not enough?
Smell properly. Is there a damp note to it or not? That clammy, musty sort of smell?
No... mm... no... oh — yes! There is! I can smell it now! Like the mouldy smell a house gets after rain!
Tsk... lying again.
Ow! That hurt! Why'd you hit me on the head?

If I don't knock some sense into you every now and then, none of this will stick. And now you're lying right to my face — who taught you that? If you can smell it, say so. If you can't, say you can't. Honestly...
I've told you — fresh Skylilies go straight out to dry as soon as you bring them back. How do you forget every time?
Look at them — they've already wilted. We can't send stock like this to the Hall of Incense.
You silly thing... what am I going to do with you?
I'm sorry... I'll take whatever punishment you give me.
And what good would that do? This is my fault too. I thought you were ready to take charge of this on your own, but clearly I was wrong.

When the Skylilies came in that day, the weather looked off. I was worried putting them out straight away might affect the quality, so I thought I'd wait till it cleared a bit... and then... I forgot.
All right, enough. Set this batch aside for lesser use. If it's not even fit for that, we'll have to burn it.
Luosheng Incense needs a very fine grind. If there are still chunks this size after one pass, you'll have to run it through again.
Look — even if it crumbles when you pinch it, the stems can still be holding it together. Sometimes you have to work it back and forth, like this...
Don't just stand there. Come and have a go.
(The man beckons to the onlookers gathered before him, you among them.)
(You take the mortar from him, pick a stalk from the pile beside you — so dry it would crumble at a touch — snap it in half, and drop it into the bowl.)
For the first pass, you don't need the mortar at all. Just strip off the leaves. They'll crumble with hardly any pressure.
(You do as instructed.)
(You handle the incense your own way.)
Good. See how it turns to powder with just a little pressure? Now put the stems and leaf fragments into the mortar together, then work them back and forth as if you were kneading dough.
That won't do. Even if you've got the strength for it, the mortar's too small to take a whole stalk like that.
(You do as instructed.)
Open it and take a look — see how the stems and leaves are all mixed together? Pick the stems out first, then grind the leaves on their own.
Very good — you've got a real feel for it. Open it up and take a look. It should be a fine powder by now. That's ready for blending.
(You decide to force it instead.)
You've done very well. You hardly seem like a beginner at all. If you'd like to learn incense-making, I'd be happy to teach you more.
No, no, no, that won't do! You'll only tire yourself out...
I only stopped by by chance. I won't be staying in Huaxu for long. Still, thank you for the kind offer.
(You open the mortar and show him the result. The method was wrong, but the material has all the same been ground to powder.)
Ah, I see. Never mind, then.
Well... that works if the material's perfectly dry, I suppose. But if there's even a trace of moisture in it, you won't manage it that way. It's still best to do it the way I showed you.
Still, for someone so slight, you're surprisingly strong.
Comes from fighting.
Oh? That's a bold thing to say. Then I take it you're not from Huaxu. Best not go waving blades about here. Wouldn't want Lord Bi'an taking notice.
Help, Liang! Come quick! The stove's blown up again!
I swear, I only went over to the doorway for a second to watch the ants. I wasn't even touching it. Then it suddenly started rattling like mad.
I didn't even dare open the door. I came straight to you.
Did you get the heat wrong again? You left it on high the whole time, didn't you?
Well, it's Redshell... don't you have to keep the heat high the whole time? Otherwise how are you supposed to get the outer layer off?
Are you stupid? You're meant to peel off that fibrous outer layer by hand! Who told you to leave it on high heat?
I've always done it that way... It worked before...
And that's why your stove blows up every other day! Right, enough. Take me there. Now.
Incense blending is a craft. It's not nearly as simple as people think. You have to mind the proportions, mind the timing... and above all, work with the season.

Take today, for example — light breeze, clear skies, not a cloud in sight. A day like this is ideal for blending Mingyao Incense. When the weather turns a little cooler and there's moisture in the air, that's the time for Luosheng Incense.

options.content: What does the weather have to do with blending incense?

talks.content: Everything. Every ingredient has its own nature, and you have to handle it accordingly. Some must be washed, then dried in the sun. Some are left to dry slowly in the shade. Some need grinding, and some need only the lightest preparation.
Only when those materials are brought together properly does a true blend emerge. Different blends call for different ingredients, and those ingredients naturally all have their own properties.

Take Mingyao Incense, for instance. In Huaxu, mingyao means bright radiance. Even the name carries a sense of warmth and festivity, doesn't it? It is made with a generous amount of cinnamon, which grows in the hotter regions. Once harvested, the branches are ground into powder.

By the time it has been packed and shipped to Haojing, the powder usually holds a trace of damp. So it is first kept indoors to warm and dry through, and only brought out for blending on a day with some proper warmth in the air.
Only then can the incense retain its warming nature, and so nourish body heat and dispel cold.

options.content: That's an awful lot of fuss. Sounds like more trouble than it's worth.
That's an awful lot of care. Sounds like something deserving of real respect.

talks.content: Jiaolan Village earned its name through the art of aromatics, so naturally we're more exacting in these matters than places that simply turn out incense.

These days, many incense blenders with no regard for the old traditions care little for such things. All they want is a blend that catches the eye — or rather, the nose — and so they are often far too bold in their choice of ingredients.
What they fail to understand is that incense begins with gifts taken from Heaven and Earth, and so Heaven and Earth must in turn be met with due reverence.
Is that batch of incense packed and ready yet? The client has asked a few times already.
Which one? The Lunarose for the Hall of Incense, or the Luosheng ordered by the Starweavers over at Mistwharf?
One of the incense wardens came for the Lunarose this morning. Were you not in the village?
I thought they were here for something else. I didn't realise it was the Lunarose. But the Luosheng still hasn't been sent out. Why don't you ask Liang?
It still hasn't gone out? How many days has it been now...? Wait.
You want me to ask Liang? Don't tell me he's in charge of the blending now. And that little apprentice of his...
Qiao's just a bit too playful, that's all. Give him some credit. He won't make the same mistake again.
I... I'd better go ask, then.
Just this last bit to plough... then I can get home and put my feet up.
Oof... if Old Tang hadn't let those kids take the Kuiniu Type Ⅰ to bits, I wouldn't be out here working the fields and wearing these old bones out.
Hm? Ah! You're the guest Su Yi brought back. I remember now. Shouldn't you be back at the house resting? What are you doing out here in the fields?
That Kuiniu Type Ⅰ — it's the farming machine Su Yi built for working the fields up here.
You sit on it, work the levers a bit, and it'll move and till the soil for you. Faster than doing it by hand, that's for sure.

Trouble is, Old Tang decided to teach the youngsters how those mechapuppets work, and used the whole machine for the lesson. Took it clean apart! And Su Yi's been tied up with other things lately, so she hasn't had time to put it back together.
So here I am instead. These old arms may not look like much, but there's still some strength left in them.

options.content: That can't be easy on you.

talks.content: Oh, it's nothing. Just a few hard days, that's all. Once that girl's free, she'll put the machine back together.

Though... let's just hope Old Tang doesn't get another bright idea and start tinkering with some new mechapuppet. I'd hate to spend all day ploughing, only for one of his failed experiments to blow the whole field to bits that night.

Bah! That old fool! Just talking about him gets me worked up. Always tinkering with who knows what, blowing up fields left and right, and calling it "necessary testing". And what's come of all that, eh? I've yet to see him make a single useful thing.
Last time he said he'd built a Diloong Type Ⅲ. Said it'd be better than the Kuiniu — you wouldn't even need to ride it. It'd plough all by itself.
Well, true enough, no one needed to be there — but it didn't move either. Just sat there spitting sparks. I didn't dare go near it, and the next moment it blew up!

The whole field was scorched black. It very nearly became a proper disaster. We had to haul out the Red Carp Type Ⅰ to put the fire out. That patch still hasn't been put right. It's been barren ever since.

Better to leave these things to people you can rely on. That disciple of Yan Shanting's no better, either. There used to be a bamboo grove on the back hill, and he'd go there to practise his swordplay.
Cut the whole grove bare. Good thing bamboo grows fast.
That's enough chatter. One more strip to finish, then I'm heading home for supper. My stomach's been rumbling the whole time — I'm eating three bowls of rice tonight.
Can't tell what they're up to.
Heard someone's been making moves out in the western outskirts lately, using the Drifters' name. Can't tell what they're up to.
No use worrying. Good news never travels, but bad news spreads like wildfire. Our name's been dragged through the mud for years already, so what's a little more?
Maybe so. But while people are swaggering about, swindling folk in our name, we're stuck up here in the mountains keeping our heads down...
If they really make a mess of things, there'll still be time for us to step in. Besides, if they do anything that harms common folk, Bi'an and the Magistrates of Yingtian will be on them in no time.
Instead of fretting over that, you'd do better to practise your swordplay. Give me but time to hone my blade, and I'll cut down foes in droves! Ha!
(He flicks out a neat flourish, as though he were holding a sword.)
Oi! You shameless Drifter! Waving weapons about in open defiance of the law! You lawless wretch!
So what of it? Come and arrest me, then!
So you're the one Su brought back? Well, look at you. Aren't you a charming youngster.
Who else would I mean? There's only one Su of the Heavenly Artisans here in Outer Peaks.
There used to be another Su here once... but she's already... Ah, never mind. If Su wants to tell you, she will. It's hardly much of a secret.
Still, Outer Peaks doesn't usually take in outsiders. You must be someone rather special.
My name's {nickname}. I'm a Phoxhunter.
A Phoxhunter...? That's not a name I've heard in Huaxu. Still, it does sound a bit like the Drifters.
So are you something like Hyperborea's Drifters, then?
Come on... when are we going down the mountain? I'm so bored up here...

Just be patient. Sister Yi and the others are still in Haojing, trying to win a name for us. Once the Nine Chapters of Dafeng recognise us, we'll go into Haojing properly — heads high, swords at our hips — and let everyone know who we are.
Ooh! I know this one! "I'm Shi Ji — a Drifter!"
That's the spirit. Till then, we stay here and wait our turn. If you're really that bored, let's go and see Uncle Tang. Maybe he's finished building some new mechapuppets.
Yeah! The one that could swing a sword was so cool! He said this time he'd build one we can actually ride. Come on, let's go see if it's ready!
Hmph. I told you not to bring outsiders back. Sooner or later, someone's going to find this place.

There are already enough people out there using our name to stir up trouble. And now we've got strangers coming and going from our hideout as they please. If the Nine Chapters of Dafeng catch wind of this place, they'll wipe us out in one sweep.

options.content: What trouble could I possibly stir up?

talks.content: That's not overthinking. It's called being careful. Better that than dead.
Who knows? Arson. Murder. Robbery. Plenty of ways.
For all I know, you could be up to anything. So watch yourself — and don't go stirring up trouble in our name.
Just behave yourself.

options.content: You don't even trust someone your own people brought here?
If you won't trust me, you should at least trust Su Yi.

talks.content: Hmph... I know that girl too well. Soft-hearted, stubborn, all at once. Say a few sweet words to her and she'll believe anyone. How do I know you haven't fooled her already?
I'll be watching you. The moment you step out of line, I'll have the mechapuppets pin you where you stand!
(Forget it... There's no point arguing with him. He's just trying to protect Outer Peaks.)
What's so great about the Jishu Sect, anyway? Come on, grab your sword. You and me. Let's have a proper spar. That's what matters.
No... I want to learn about mechapuppets from Uncle Tang, not swordplay.
Hmph. Always messing about with those contraptions. Before our parents left, they told me to carry on the family sword art. And now look at you — all you ever do is fuss over those things.
You're already carrying it on... isn't that enough for both of us?
What good are those machines anyway? You protect yourself with your own hands. With skill. With a blade.
That's not true! Mechapuppets are amazing! The ones Sister Yi made can send a Sable Bi'an flying with one punch!
They're slow and clumsy! Me? I'd put my blade straight through a Sable Bi'an in one strike.
You're only saying that because you don't think mechapuppets are any good. Just wait and see — I'll build one even better than Sister Yi's. Stronger, and faster too.
And when I do, you can spar with my mechapuppet. I bet your sword won't even scratch its armour!
Nonsense! There's nothing my blade can't cut. Go on, then. Let's see what you can actually build!
It's... someone new... I really, really want to say hello...
(The Wishen peeks out shyly from behind a pillar, as though they want to come closer but don't quite dare.)
Ah... they're looking this way!
You mean me? You... you really said hello!
That was really kind... It's been so long since anyone said hello to me like that...
You... you're not afraid of me? I'm a Wishen... doesn't that scare you?
I've met many Wishens before.
R—Really!? That's good... Then this place doesn't bother you, does it? We're all nice here... just a little lonely...
Sometimes people wander in here by accident. Some of them can't even see us. They just mutter to themselves... "It's cold... this place is creepy..." We try to talk to them, but they never answer.
After a while, we stop trying and just show them the way out.
Then there are the ones who can see us. They're even worse... They scream and run through the alley, crying out every time they spot one of us.
They make so much noise it gives us a headache... so in the end we have to guide them out too.
But you... you're different... You seem so calm. Being near you makes me feel so happy... and warm.
Could you... stay a little longer? I want to spend a little more time with you...
H-H-H-Hands in the air! If you want to get through, you'd better tell me your name!
Wh—What!? Why are you looking at me like that? Did I do it wrong? Wasn't I fierce enough? Or... or am I just not as big as her?

options.content: You're missing the big sack she always drags around.
You're missing the part where she threatens to rough me up.

talks.content: Oh! You know Luno too? So you could tell I was copying her?

Really? I don't remember her saying anything like that. She just shouted her line and popped out of nowhere. Then, when she realised we Wishen didn't have anything, she just slunk off all disappointed.
Why are you trying to copy Lulu Lunoloot?
Because she's amazing! She just appears out of nowhere, and all eyes are on her.
Isn't that incredible? To grab everyone's attention just like that. I can't do that. I have to stay close to a big rock. If I move around too much, I lose my strength.
All I can do is startle the people who can see me. The ones who can't... well, they don't notice me at all.
If one day I could shout a cool line and drop in from the sky just like her, wouldn't that be amazing...?
Every time she tries to rob me, I chase her off before she can even finish the line.
Ah... that's a bit mean. She's not a bad person.
That day, she came to this alley for some reason. She looked a little sneaky, so we went over to say hello. But instead, she tried to rob us.
We didn't have anything to give her, so we just floated around in circles and told her she could take some stones if she wanted.
When we're bored, we play with stones and toss them around. They're the most valuable things we have.
But she didn't take any! She just left, dragging that big sack behind her. She's a good Luno.
I don't even know what we'd play with if she'd taken our stones...
Well... that's...
She even tossed us some copper coins! Now we use the coins and stones to play board games! If it weren't for her, we'd never have discovered such a fun new game.
I think I had an older brother... and a younger sister... but... where did they go...?
Why am I still here? I want to go home... but I can't... Hello, stranger... can you take me home?
I can't remember... I think it was a town. Our house was the biggest one there. I had an older brother... he did business in town.
When he was younger, he never cared much for studying, so Mother stopped sending him to school. Later, when I was old enough, I told her I wanted to go... so she sent me instead.
I also had a little sister. She was much younger than I was. Every day after class, she'd wait for me by the school gate. There was an old man there who sold sugar figurines.
I skipped breakfast every day... just so I could save enough to buy my little sister a sugar figurine.

options.content: That's still not enough for me to figure out where your home was.

talks.content: I can't remember... I just remember my brother didn't come home very often. But whenever he did, he'd always give my sister and me lots of pocket money.
So whenever he came home, I was always so happy. I always looked forward to it. He promised that next holiday, he'd take me on a trip.
He did... But on my way to meet him, a strangely coloured Bi'an suddenly rushed out. Maybe it mistook me for a criminal... and bit me. And that's how I died.
My brother must have been very sad... He had only just promised to take me on a trip, and before I could even see him, I...
(I see... a victim of a Sable Bi'an.)
I still can't remember where my home is. If one day you happen to come across my family out there... could you ask how they're doing? Especially my brother... I hope he wasn't too heartbroken.
Though... I don't suppose they'd still be so sad. At least, not after all this time. I don't even remember how long it's been. If they were still grieving for me now... I'd feel awful.
I think... my brother's name was Xiangshan... And my sister was... Asheng...
I miss them so much... I hope they haven't forgotten me... and yet, at the same time... I hope they have.
Trailing Glory Teahouse — now open in East Market! Bring the family — free pot of flower tea!
(She gives the pitch a few half-hearted shouts, then gives up, impatience all over her face.)
What's the point of this...? The birds still haven't been found...
Ah! You caught me slacking off, didn't you? Did the boss send you to check up on me?
Please, {性别:sir|ma'am}, have mercy! I won't slack off again, I swear. Please don't tell the boss... and even if you do...
Phew, you gave me a fright! Just passing through? Here, take a flyer. The boss drew them by hand.
...put in a good word for me, will you? Please don't let him dock my pay!
Once we've got our Emeraldfinches back from the docks, we can open properly. When that happens, do drop by.
薄薄一张纸，其上绘的翠屏雀却是栩栩如生，像是要随时跃出纸张一样……看来绘制者是位画技高超之人。
The best brews? You'll find them at The Asphodel, no question.
Intoxicating aroma, full-bodied flavours, and what sets it apart most? The smooth, clean finish — it lingers on the tongue.
A fine drink is like a seductive lover... Ah, I think I need another refill...
There's more to The Asphodel than just great drinks.
Because you can enjoy a tipple here without having to worry about getting caught in a brawl with drunkards or getting whacked by some random lunatic...
After all, this is Camilla's turf. Her name alone keeps everyone in line — no one dares stir up trouble here.
Boohoo... Boohoo...
Love... what does it really taste like!? Was it the rush of ecstasy when I joined Camilla's fan club, or the crushing heartbreak when I heard she disbanded it?
Boohoo... Only Lady Camilla's smile can piece back together my shattered heart!
What!? Again...? Can't you just fail once? Fine, fine... guess it still needs a bit more work.
Yep, that's more like it! Honestly? Still not sure what practical use it has... but hey, gotta be good for something.
I gave this thing another upgrade — go on, give it a whirl and help me test the tweaks. Cost me a fortune to smuggle in from Elysium, y'know. No way you're getting through this time!
You're back. Good timing — I gave it another upgrade. Last one was way too easy. But this time? I bet you'll trip at least once.
Again!? Seriously!? I've poured so much into upgrading this thing... But I'm not giving up! Just you wait — I'll get you next time!
Hah! Watching you flail around just now gave me an idea. I'll pitch it to my superior — slap this baby on the Icelake gates and stop anyone from barging in!
There you are! I've been waiting. I poured every last coin into this baby — she's a beast now. No way you're getting through this time.
Again!? Are you kidding me!? Ugh... Y'know what, forget it. I should've known better than to trust Elysian tech. This is what I get for smuggling their junk behind His Majesty's back.

Ha! Gotcha at last! This thing's a masterpiece — I oughta present it to His Majesty himself. Perfect for screening recruits. I'll finally rake in a fat bonus and pay off all the debt I racked up building it.
(The machine hums softly. A crude dial sits atop it, etched with three labels: Easy, Hard, and Extremely Hard. Looks like the handiwork of that overly chatty soldier.)
You wanna go again? Sure, why not. You nimble types really love bouncing around, huh?
You wanna go again? Sure, why not. You nimble types really love bouncing around, huh?
You wanna go again? Sure, why not. You nimble types really love bouncing around, huh?
That's right! You picked the right colour — so in you go!
Nope! Have another think. A really good one this time!
Eeya~ Better count again, just to be sure!
So was it the cars that came first... or Catizz?
That's right! You picked the right colour — so in you go!
Nope! Have another think. A really good one this time!
Eeya~ Better count again, just to be sure!
So was it the cars that came first... or Catizz?
(Looks like it is planning to stay at the Sanctuary. Time to give it a name.)
Have you come across any treasures lately? Show me, and I might forge a truly extraordinary weapon out of it!
That's my little friend. Tiny, but strong — it keeps the forge fire going.
Ah! I... I wasn't slacking off... Ahem! I mean, what can I get you?
... (Lunoeggy writes on the board: "So glad you're here!")

options.content: I feel like I've seen you somewhere before...
Have we met in a place called Icelake?

talks.content: ... (That's right! It's me! I've got loads and loads of copies of myself. If you don't believe me, just wait until you reach the next city — you'll see another me there.)
A Lunoeggy with countless copies... what an incredible little creature.

options.content: So... can you open the eggshell and show me what's inside?

talks.content: You're just different Lunos hiding inside the same sort of eggshell, aren't you? You just happened to pick matching shells, for some reason.
...! (Absolutely not! Under this eggshell is another eggshell, and under that is another one! Definitely not a Luno... definitely not!)
... (Hah! That's because the best hiding place is in a crowd of me!)
... (That way, when one of me beats you at dice and you try to win your money back... you'll never know which one it was!)
That actually makes sense.

options.content: So... can you open the eggshell and show me what's inside?

talks.content: Hey! Look who it is — Snow the Demon King and her trusty Loongscion! You came to see me!
I have a name.
Haha, I know! Just messing with you, {nickname}! You're a good friend of mine too! And that red horn of yours — like a pretty maple leaf — I'm sooo jealous, I want one too!
Hey, Lunocarp, what's that tall machine stuffed with all those little balls?
You're really sharp, Snow the Demon King! Spotted the good stuff straight away! This here is my secret money-maker!
I went to a craftsman from the Jishu Sect — Master Gong... Gong-something — and had him build this Lucky Egg machine for me! Toss in a token and — pop! — out comes a random prize!
The trick is letting randomness work its wonders — that's how you make money! This genius idea hit me while I was praying to Lord Argent. Amazing, right?
So... is business any good?
...Meh. Only so-so.
It's just too ahead of its time, so I still haven't made back what I spent on it. Guess that's the fate of a true genius.
Anyway... if you pick up any Taixu Runes, gears, or stuff like that around Mistwharf, you can use them for a spin on my Lucky Egg machine.
These little pieces of useless rubbi— um, I mean, the prizes! Whatever comes out, it's yours! Think of it as a little gift from me!
Hey, it's {nickname} and Snow the Demon King! You came to visit me again! I've got brand-new Lucky Eggs today — wanna give it a spin?

options.content: Ask Lunocarp about her business ideas.

talks.content: Me? I used to be just a plain old Luno, trying every day to squeeze a few more orders out of those stingy Starweavers. But then Snow the Demon King showed up — and she changed my life!
Ooh, about that — I had an epiphany lately! The Lucky Egg isn't just struggling because it's ahead of its time — the real problem is that the prizes are boring! That's the fatal flaw!
I'm not the same Luno I used to be! I'm gonna become a Starweaver whose name goes down in history — and bring the Lunos back to glory!
Some Starweavers in Huaxu made deals with the Xuanheng Sect to sell limited-edition sachets, and they're selling like crazy! That totally inspired me!
Someday, right next to the Demon King's palace, there'll be a huge, fancy shop with my name on it — absolutely!
And if we're talking irresistibly adorable prizes, it's obviously us Lunos!
It's both a dream and a promise! Just you wait — I'll make it happen!
If I make a collab with the Demon King and put it in as the secret rare drop — it's gonna be a massive hit, right? What do you think, {nickname}?
Okay, okay, off you go — you've got things to do! And I've got dreams to chase too... no way I'm falling behind!
Haha! I'll be rolling in coins till I'm dizzy!

name: Captain of "May the Holy Light Shield You"

talks.content: There you are! You heard I refitted Qingluan Type Ⅱ again, right? Come on, I'll show you... Huh? You're just here to chat?

options.content: So what do you do for fun?
You said you've got a pretty high standing in the sect. What do you mean by that?
Come to think of it, I've been seeing a little bird around you a lot lately.

talks.content: Hmm... Putting mechanisms together, polishing gears, tracking down new materials... and tinkering until the next version's better.

Both the Jishu Sect and the Drifters take lineage seriously. Say a ninety-year-old master takes a ten-year-old as his last disciple — suddenly half the sect has to treat that child as an elder. (matter-of-fact, explanatory)
Oh, that's Qingluan Type Ⅲ — my new pet!
The Outer Peaks, huh... that's a good question.

Remember when Uncle Tang took that fall and hurt his leg? I've been free lately, so I've been working on a vehicle with smoother, steadier takeoffs. Jishu disciples like to push for results like they've got a spare life. I'm not letting that carry on.
I got lucky — my teacher was my aunt, and she was way up in the sect. So yeah, that still bumps me up too. (bright, explanatory)
See? Doesn't it look just like a real Skywing Gull? I simplified the boot-up — press and hold the top of its head and it'll go into mimic-flight mode. And speaking of flying—

We found each other because we'd been through similar things, and we're fighting for the same goal. We understand each other. We trust each other. In a fight, we've got each other's backs. And when you're worn out, you're not on your own. It's... a really good place.
Don't you ever get tired of working all the time?
Kezhou's the unlucky one. His master, Yan Shanting, is lower in the lineage — so by the rules, he has to call me "Great-Auntie".
Look at the feathers! I used naturally shed Skywing Gull feathers, then sealed them with an improved water-repellent finish — it hardly adds any weight.
To a lot of people here, the Outer Peaks feel like home.

Tired? How could I be? What could be more fun than this? You break a mechanism down in your head, piece by piece — then you build it in the real world. That moment it all clicks into place and actually works? Best feeling in the world.
What about me?
Its colours won't fade, it stays fluffy forever — and when it perches on your arm, it won't dig its claws in like a real bird. All the cuteness, none of the scratches. Perfect pet.
Is it home for you too?
That's what makes it so good. So — want to try? The best Artificer in the Outer Peaks happens to be free right now. I can teach you hands-on.
Master Gongshang's pretty high up too. Let me do the maths... oh! We're the same generation.
Why not keep a real one?
It... yeah. Of course it is!
Heehee. If Kezhou ever gets cheeky with you, you can make him call you {性别：Grandpa|Grandma}.

Skywing Gulls belong in the sky. If you keep one, you're basically shutting it in a cage. And if I caught one just for my own enjoyment... how would I be any different from the Xuanheng Sect back then?
You seem off. What's wrong?
Hang on... Snow calls you her "Little Minion", right? So she's your master...? No way. Don't tell me the one who outranks all of us is a tiny Luno!

Some animals make good companions, but a Skywing Gull clearly isn't one of them. That sharp beak, that long tail, those wings built to cut through the wind... it says it all. It belongs in the sky, not in anyone's palm.
You're sharp. Is that the instinct of a mercenary— no, a Phoxhunter? And it's not just for fights... you can read people too? If only my mechapuppet's nav system were as quick as you...
I'm just... a bit lost. What's a home supposed to feel like, anyway?
Somewhere you come back to, no matter how far you go.
Then... if you can't go back... is it still home? ...Sorry. That was silly. Just forget I said anything.
Business is what gets me out of bed. What about you?

options.content: What are those big barrels at your tavern for?
Can't imagine Phoxhunters in Icelake without The Asphodel. You've built something impressive here.
What does money really mean to people?
That mysterious figure who brought me to Icelake — what do you know about them?

talks.content: Barrels? For keeping the good stuff, naturally. Tales of Icelake — crisp, refreshing. Legion Wolfblood — bold, with a kick. Azure Loong's Draught, brought in from Huaxu — clean, with a long finish. And Luca's Masquerade Rhapsody... ten flavours in one. Everyone swears it tastes different.

You flatter me. Phoxhunters have been around far longer than my tavern. They just need somewhere to chat, brag, and pass work around. If it weren't The Asphodel, it would be some other name on the sign.
Instead of asking me, shouldn't you ask yourself? I still remember you turning up in Icelake with nowhere to go. You know perfectly well money's what keeps you on your feet in this world.

Not much, I'm afraid. I've been in Icelake for years, and I've never seen them before. They were wrapped head to toe in a cloak, and they spoke through a voice modulator. Where they came from, whether they were a man or a woman, even their age — I've no idea.
Well? Fancy a glass?
As for why they come here... it's nothing more than good drinks, a broker who plays fair, and a small favour now and then when someone's down on their luck.
I haven't forgotten. Being broke really is hard.
The only thing I can be certain of is that they were far stronger than they had any right to be. We exchanged a few moves. That was enough to tell me I wouldn't have come out on top.
Don't give me that. I knocked on them — they're empty. Always have been.

Get enough money behind you and, even if you can't change where you came from, you'll have the nerve to take on whatever fate throws at you. When times are rough, you can at least buy yourself a warm drink... maybe even share a sip, do someone a good turn, and bank a favour for later.
Didn't take you for the modest type.
Heh. You've gotten a lot sharper — not like that wide-eyed greenhorn who first wandered into Icelake.
Now, does that answer your question?

Heh. In my line of work, you learn to count your chips — and size up what the other side is holding. Bluffing only works when you're playing for similar stakes. I pick my fights. That's how you stay alive.
Go a little over a hundred kilometres north of Icelake. Cross the Vidofnir Mountains and you'll reach the fjordlands of Askard — the Charons' homeland, if the stories are true.
Actually... there was one thing they said before they left.
For many Charons in Icelake, what's a hundred-odd kilometres and a mountain range? The promised land isn't so far out of reach after all... wouldn't you say?
They said what they wanted from you... was an "answer".
Don't tell me you're helping them slip across the border...
Shh. I never said that.
Don't push yourself too hard. We still have to save some strength for those Filthoids.
It's done... Argh...
<W>Your hands are drenched in wet, slimy filth, uncertain whether it's the Filthoid's secretions or its innards. Yet, a sudden joy tingles through your soul, bringing an inexplicable elation.</>

options.content: (Shut up! That was not how I felt!)

talks.content: <W>Do not resist, because I am what you actually are. I am your instinct for death. One day you shall follow my lead and obey the ancient will...</>

options.content: (You refuse to let the ramblings erode your will and try to stay sane.)

You! Hmph!
Never mind, arguing with a youngster isn't worth my time.
Actually, I caught a whiff of something remarkable as you passed by just now.
That's right. It's the scent of a <H>legendary weapon</>! Do you have any special weapons on you, kiddo?
Weapon? This sword is all I have.
(She carefully examined the sword, attempting to glean some information from its pattern.)
Amazing! That's incredible! Look at the texture and the craftsmanship! This clearly wasn't made by those mediocre Hyperborean blacksmiths. Where did you get it?
(The Luno blacksmith recognised that this sword was no ordinary weapon.)
I'm not sure...
This sword has been with me for as long as I can remember. Maybe it was passed down to me by my parents?
Intriguing. Very intriguing. I've been a blacksmith my whole life, yet I've never seen a weapon like this before.
Kiddo, I'm Lunosmith, a wandering blacksmith. Would you mind if I accompanied you on your journey?
I've travelled all over the land, from Hyperborea to Elysium, and I've forged countless weapons. If you require any weapons, I'm at your disposal.
Wow! So you're an experienced master blacksmith!
All I request is a basic salary, and an opportunity to examine your sword, hehe.

(Some, driven by hunger, have mistaken Eclipta Grass for food.)
(If the poison hasn't set in too deep, this compound can help neutralise the toxins.)
(You've obtained a remedy that might help with Luna's throat)
What's this doing on the floor? This might actually help Luna!
Could you take a closer look? The well-being of flowers hinges on careful observation, but I can't do that now...
